items.title: Fransys
items.text: Fransys is a Python toolkit for electrical cabinet and harness design. You write the design as a short Python script against a part library, and Fransys checks it as it builds. From that one model it produces the schematic PDF, the parts, terminal, cable and PLC lists, and the KiCad and WAGO exports.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Fransys is not on PyPI yet. Pin it as a git dependency, at a release tag:

[project]
dependencies = [
    "fransys @ git+https://github.com/OleJBondahl/fransys@vX.Y.Z#subdirectory=packages/fransys",
]

Replace vX.Y.Z with the release you pin.

items.title: An example
items.text:
This script builds a small motor starter from the demo parts and writes one PDF into out/.

"""A small motor starter, built and written as one PDF into out/."""

from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BK, BU


class Starter(NamedTuple):
    x1: fr.TerminalStrip
    pe: fr.Run


@fr.unit(
    "motor-starter",
    title="Motor starter",
    number="MS-1",
    revision=1,
    interface_version=1,
    date="2026-10-06",
    text="v1",
    by="OJ",
)
def starter(c: fr.Design) -> Starter:
    x0 = c.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
    ac = c.ac_supply("400V", "230", x0[1], x0[2], x0[3])
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24"))
    q0, q1, f1 = (
        c.device(t, p)
        for t, p in (("Q0", "DEMO-MCB-3P"), ("Q1", "DEMO-CTR-3P-24"), ("F1", "DEMO-OVERLOAD-3P"))
    )
    s1, s2 = (c.device(t, "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC") for t in ("S1", "S2"))
    x1 = c.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5", interface=True)
    c.series(ac, q0.element, q1.main, f1.main, x1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
    c.series(dc.plus, s1.nc, c.parallel(s2.no, q1.aux), f1.aux, q1.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    return Starter(x1, x1.run("PE", 1))


d = fr.design("demo_parts")
s = d.add(starter, "U1")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")
d.series(s.x1, w1, m1.motor, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.earth(m1.motor["PE"], s.pe[1])
cover = Path("cover.md")
cover.write_text("# Motor starter\n", encoding="utf-8")
result = fr.build(d, fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "motor-starter", cover=cover))
fr.write(result, Path("out"))

The first schematic page of that PDF:

items.text:
• The guide: every consumer task with its one spelling.
  • The part-file contract: how a part library is written.
  • The examples gallery: whole designs, their PDFs and exports.
  • The API reference: every name the public surface exports.

items.title: Roadmap
items.text: Fransys is in beta. This page lists what comes next, in no fixed order. Each release's guide says what changed.

items.title: Drawings
items.text:
• Cable and harness drawings, with their own layout.
  • Revision marks on changed drawings, and a revision table on unit covers.
  • Block diagrams of units.
  • Steady work on drawing quality.

items.title: Checks
items.text:
• A check that the supply and signal levels match where two units meet.
  • A list of interface changes between two revisions of a unit.
  • A finding for a power input with no supply path, and for two rails joined only through contacts.

items.title: Outputs
items.text:
• Board fabrication files (Gerber, drill, position, BOM) through KiCad's command line.
  • Document sets for one unit, with its nested units shown as black boxes.
  • Items supplied by others, drawn dashed and kept off the BOM.

items.title: Documentation
items.text: • A documentation index for coding agents.

• A stable API, kept stable across minor versions.
  • A review of the packaging: PyPI, and whether stable building blocks such as the symbol toolkit become packages of their own.
  • A lighter, cleaned-up repository.

items.title: allocate_plc
items.text:
def allocate_plc(model: Model) -> tuple[Model, tuple[Finding, ...]]

Bind every plc_request facet to a free channel of matching SignalType.

Wiring first: a request whose ports share a physical net with channel functions binds to the first free one in serving order whose net holds no other request's function, in any unit. The rest are served by the first unit on their chain (item's unit, then each Unit.parent, top level last) that declares a channel of their signal type, from one free queue per (unit, signal type). Siblings never share and nothing reaches downward. If that unit's channels are all taken, or the chain declares none, the request gets PLC_REQUEST_UNSERVABLE with no fall-through. Requests serve by (priority, requesting Function.key, Function.id), channels by (rack Item.key, module position, module Item.key, plc_channel.channel, Function.id). A request already carrying a plc_binding is skipped. Returns the model with one plc_binding per request served and one finding per request left (PLC_CHANNEL_CONTESTED once per channel wired to two or more kind-matched requests, which bind nothing); a model with nothing to bind comes back as the same object.

items.title: board_netlist
items.text:
def board_netlist(model: Model, board: Id[Item]) -> BoardNetlist

board's parts, footprints and nets as one BoardNetlist.

Parts are the footprinted descendants of board. Nets join its internal conductors and its declared nets, never Mates; part designations are relative to board.

Args: model: The model to read. board: The item whose netlist is built.

Returns: A BoardNetlist (defined in derive.rows) for board.

Raises: SchemaError: board is not an item of model, or it or a listed item has no designation.

items.title: board_pins
items.text:
def board_pins(model: Model, board: Id[Item]) -> BoardPins

board_netlist's nets with each pin resolved once, and the open pins of its parts.

A pin of an item with no part row takes its board-relative designation. unconnected lists, per part in board_netlist order, every port of its functions whose ref:pad is in no net.

Args: model: The model to read. board: The item whose netlist is built.

Returns: A BoardPins (defined in derive.rows_netlist).

Raises: SchemaError: as board_netlist.

items.title: boards
items.text:
def boards(model: Model) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

Every item whose Part carries a pcb facet, in designation order.

PcbFacet.subject is a Part, not an item: an item is a board when its own part is one that carries the facet. Shared by fransys's export enumeration and the pdf document contents, so the two never disagree about what a board is.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every board item's id, by natural designation, then id.

items.title: bom_lines
items.text:
def bom_lines(model: Model, scope: Id[Item] | Id[AspectNode] | Id[Unit] | TopLevelScope | None=None, *, without: Collection[Id[Item]]=()) -> tuple[BomLine, ...]

One BomLine per Part of an installed, not external item, by (mpn, revision, part).

An item with no part has no line; a crimp contact part has one, counted per used pin. designations are printed_designations; revision is "" on a part line. scope narrows:

  • None (default): every installed item of the model, no unit lines.
  • Id[Item]: that item and its descendants; Id[AspectNode]: the items at or below it.
  • Id[Unit]: its own items and a part=None line per nested unit; its sole root prints none.
  • TOP_LEVEL: items with no unit, plus one line per top-level unit, the same way.
  • without: items the None, item and node scopes leave out (a document's undrawn harness).

Raises: SchemaError: scope is none of the above kinds, names a unit the model does not hold, or a counted item has no designation.

items.title: bom_sort_key
items.text:
def bom_sort_key(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> tuple[int, NaturalKey, str, int]

Sort key for one item within a bom_lines line's designations.

A terminal with a parent sorts (0, its strip's item_designation, its own group, its own index): by strip, then group, then index. group/index come straight off the TerminalFacet, never re-parsed from rendered text, so "L1:10" sorts after "L1:2". Any other item sorts (1, natural_key(its own item_designation), "", 0): digit runs by value (-K2, -K10).

Raises: SchemaError: as item_designation.

items.title: box_pairs
items.text:
def box_pairs(model: Model, drawn: Collection[Id[Port]] | None=None) -> dict[Id[Function], BoxPair]

Each function wired point to point to one function of another item, and the port pairs.

Every port of the function has a two-port net to a port of that one function, one to one, and that function has no other port. Two partners, a split group, a third member or a net of three ports leave the function out. The relation is symmetric; which box is fed is layout's reading of the box sides. With drawn, only the ports in it count on either side: a port the profile leaves off the page is no member of its function.

items.title: build_indexes
items.text:
def build_indexes(model: Model) -> Indexes

Build every index together off model.

Cached on model.digest, holding the last few results: two calls with an equal digest return the identical Indexes object, so a caller never has to thread it through by hand. The digest ignores origins and aliases, which no index reads, and an Indexes holds only ids, so equal digests mean equal results. Identity is guaranteed within one thread.

items.title: cable_items
items.text:
def cable_items(model: Model) -> frozenset[Id[Item]]

Every item whose part carries a cable_product facet, built once per digest.

The one selection rule behind is_cable: an item is in this set exactly when its Item.part is one of the parts a CableProductFacet names as subject. Reads nothing else -- not category, not the item's own CableFacet (installed length only).

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every item id whose part carries a cable_product facet.

items.title: cable_list_rows
items.text:
def cable_list_rows(model: Model, *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> tuple[CableListRow, ...]

One CableListRow per cable of one reading: unit's own, or the top-level ones.

unit=None: every cable item (is_cable) with no unit, harness cables included. A unit: the cables whose own Item.unit is unit, read with its facts. Rows sort by (designation, id). from_label is the first end's designation; to_label the others', joined by ", ".

Args: model: The frozen model to read. unit: The unit whose own cables to list; None is the top-level ones.

Raises: SchemaError: unit is no unit, or an item has no designation.

Args: model: The frozen model to read. cable: The cable item whose cores to list. unit: The unit whose own document draws the cable, keyword-only; None is the whole model.

items.title: changeover_throws
items.text:
def changeover_throws(model: Model, function: Id[Function]) -> tuple[Throws, ...]

The poles of the CONTACT_CO function function, one Throws per common port.

A common port gets a Throws when a switched internal link joins it to a BREAK or MAKE port of the same function. Roles come from the part's PortTemplates, never a pin name. Sorted by common; it never raises. Cached on model.digest.

Args: model: The model to read. function: The CONTACT_CO function whose poles are found.

Returns: One Throws per common port, sorted by common; empty for a function that is not a changeover, is not in model, or whose ports carry no COMMON/BREAK/MAKE roles.

items.title: conductors_on_item
items.text:
def conductors_on_item(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> frozendict[Id[Item], frozendict[PortRole, tuple[Id[Conductor], ...]]]

item's conductors, grouped by terminal child item and then by port role.

Holds only the terminal-facet children with a conductor and, per child, only the roles with one; a conductor with both ends on one child is listed once per role it touches.

items.title: connector_at_line_end
items.text:
def connector_at_line_end(model: Model, function: Id[Function]) -> bool

Whether function is a plug, the function a plug mates, or a fan-out pin's function.

Read from harness_line_ends of the lines draws_as_line holds, and nothing else. The box rule, the middle-outline edge rule and the side hint's WARNING call it and never ask again. A connector at no line gives False.

items.title: connector_box_lines
items.text:
def connector_box_lines(model: Model, function: Id[Function], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> tuple[str, ...]

The lines of function's connector box: its designation, its part line, its landed pins.

The designation is connector_designation in unit's context. The part line is the MPN, only when every function of the item is a connector function. A unit boundary then prints the port_designation of each pin a conductor lands on; any other connector prints none. A line prints once however many ports or conductors reach it.

items.title: connector_facets
items.text:
def connector_facets(model: Model) -> frozendict[Id[FunctionTemplate], ConnectorFacet]

Every connector facet by the function template it describes.

items.title: connector_item
items.text:
def connector_item(model: Model, connector: Id[Function]) -> Id[Item]

The item that owns the connector function connector.

Raises: SchemaError: connector is not a function of model.

items.title: connector_items
items.text:
def connector_items(model: Model) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

Every item with a connector function of a connector-faceted template, designation order.

The items a connector table can be headed by; unit_connector_items keeps a unit's own.

items.title: connector_label
items.text:
def connector_label(marking: str | None, name: str) -> str | None

The label a connector function prints, None for none: the one home of that rule.

marking is the connector facet's (or the part file's) marking, read like Port.marking: None means the function's own name is the label (None again for an empty name), and "" means no label (a shell or an earth stud, whose pins print under the item). A function that is no connector has no label either: the caller does not ask. _connector_label here and the part lint call it after reading their own inputs.

Args: marking: The connector facet's (or part file's) marking, or None for unset. name: The function's own name, the fallback label when marking is None.

Returns: The label to print, or None for none.

items.title: connector_rows
items.text:
def connector_rows(model: Model, board: Id[Item], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None, context: Id[AspectNode] | None=None) -> tuple[ConnectorRow, ...]

One ConnectorRow per connector of board, with its pins, nets and mate.

A connector is a connector-kind Function of board or a descendant whose template carries a connector facet. designation is connector_designation: the item's own designation, or <item designation>-<label> when the item has two or more connector functions. Rows sort by (designation, connector id). mate is the other end of a Mate; a pin's mate_port is the port of equal name on it, and its net the declared net listing its port. pins sort by marking, digits first by value. context (default None, full paths) is the location the list prints against. unit is the unit whose document prints it: inside it reads unit-relative, and for a nested unit a mate outside its subtree prints None; context is ignored once unit has one.

Raises: SchemaError: board is not an item of model, or an item shown has no designation.

items.title: connector_rows_of
items.text:
def connector_rows_of(model: Model, item_ids: Collection[Id[Item]], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None, context: Id[AspectNode] | None=None) -> tuple[ConnectorRow, ...]

One ConnectorRow per connector function of exactly the items item_ids, sorted.

connector_rows is this over a board and its descendants; the rest is its contract.

items.title: connector_segments
items.text:
def connector_segments(labels: Iterable[str | None]) -> tuple[str, ...]

The segment each function prints behind its item's designation, in order.

labels holds the connector label of each function of one item: "" or None for none (a function that is no connector, or a shell that says marking=""). A device prints its connectors as sub-parts (-U2-X1:1) when two or more of its functions have a label, so that two pins named alike never print one text: a labelled function then gives -<label>, an unlabelled one "". With no label, or one, every segment is "" (-J1:1). This is the one place the rule is decided: connector_segment and the part lint both call it.

Args: labels: Each function's connector label, in index order, "" or None for none.

Returns: Each function's printed segment, in the same order: -<label> or "".

items.title: contact_list_key
items.text:
def contact_list_key(model: Model, function: Id[Function]) -> ListKey

The key a contact list sorts its contacts by: a 3-pole-plus first, then the first entry.

The caller breaks a tie by the function id.

items.title: contacts_not_drawn
items.text:
def contacts_not_drawn(model: Model) -> Counter[Id[Page]]

The contact-image entries that print N/A, by the page of the coil's image.

An entry is a spare contact when it names no partner port (image_entries).

items.title: contents_rows
items.text:
def contents_rows(cables: tuple[HarnessCable, ...]) -> tuple[ContentsRow, ...]

One ContentsRow per cable, in the order given.

Pure reshaping of HarnessCables a caller already built (harness_cables_for, top_level_cables, unit_cables): no Model parameter, no re-sort -- the caller's own order, already sorted where it needs to be, is kept. ends is every end's designation, blanks dropped, joined by an en dash (moved here verbatim from pdf's own copy).

Args: cables: The HarnessCables to reshape, in the order to keep.

Returns: One ContentsRow per cable, same order, same length.

items.title: core_colour
items.text:
def core_colour(model: Model, conductor: Id[Conductor]) -> str

The colour of core conductor: its carrier's core_colours[index - 1].

The one reader of a core's colour: the facet holds only the index, and the colour is the cable product's fact. cable_rows, the harness rows and wireviz read it here.

Args: model: The frozen model to read. conductor: The core conductor whose colour to render.

Returns: The core's colour, an IEC 60757 code (or code pair); "" for a core past its product.

Raises: SchemaError: conductor is not a core of a cable, or has no core facet.

items.title: core_list_rows
items.text:
def core_list_rows(model: Model, *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> tuple[CoreListRow, ...]

One CoreListRow per core of every cable cable_list_rows lists, in its order.

Cores sort by number within a cable. The ends are cable_rows' and open_core_rows' own texts.

Args: model: The frozen model to read. unit: The unit whose own cables to list; None is the top-level ones.

Raises: SchemaError: unit is no unit, or an item has no designation.

items.title: cores_text
items.text:
def cores_text(core_count: int | None, pairs: int | None) -> str

The cable list's Cores cell: 2x2 for a paired product, the count otherwise.

items.title: crosses_unit
items.text:
def crosses_unit(model: Model, one: Id[Item], other: Id[Item]) -> bool

Whether the two items lie in different units, strictly.

A sub-unit is a different unit from its parent, so a nested unit's item crosses against the parent's. An item in no unit differs from one in a unit, and equals another in none.

items.text:

items.title: current_chains
items.text:
def current_chains(model: Model) -> tuple[CurrentChain, ...]

The rated current paths of model grouped by loop, and what bounds each.

The result is facts.current.chains.chains_unordered, whose module docstring holds the graph and the law, with each chain's positions run in path order from its supply end. A chain's positions are edges of a block; its end ports are the nodes one position touches. The supply end is the end with the best port_potential_rank; with no ranked end, or a tie, the lower designation text. The positions follow a walk from it.

A block that is no path (a loop with no end, a star, a position in parallel) runs by a depth-first walk from its best end, or its best node when it has none; at a fork the position with the lower designation text goes first, function ids only on equal texts. Chains sort by their ordered positions' functions, so the result is the same for any record order. Cached on model.digest, the last few results of chain_blocks.

items.title: enclosing_boards
items.text:
def enclosing_boards(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

item and its ancestors by Item.parent that carry a pcb facet, outermost first.

item itself is included when it is one. Cycle-safe: a parent cycle ends the walk. The board parts come from the per-model unit index. The one predicate every board-membership question in this repo answers: derive.designation.designating_ancestors (item designations, excluding item itself; it walks boards and harnesses alike), checks.connectivity's board-realised rule (DESIGN 8: a net needs no conductors when one board is common to every port's item, intersecting frozenset(enclosing_boards(...)) over the net's ports), derive.structure. schematic_functions (a function on or under a board item, board-relative walk), and layout's board-internal connection rule -- one walk, so a drawn connector can never fail to count as its own board's by one copy drifting from another.

items.title: fold_level
items.text:
def fold_level(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit], opened: OverviewRef | None=None, *, fold: bool=True, strip: Id[Item] | None=None) -> FoldLevel

unit's level folded to its function groups, or one group or the strips box opened.

With no opened: one box per group (its item, nested-unit and strip counts, and the connections inside it), the strips with no group as "Terminal strips (n)", every other item and nested unit as itself; one line per pair of boxes and kind with the connections lifted into it; stubs folded by far end. A unit with fewer than two groups opens straight: its devices, as an opened group is drawn, folded false. With a GROUP, its devices with a terminal that passes wires through drawn as a line labelled with its strip, the rest as strips or boxes. With STRIPS, the strips with no group as boxes, their wires to other boxes ending at stubs. With fold false and no opened, a unit of several groups opens straight too: all its devices, strips see-through (the all-devices view, O16). A strip of the level opened in it stands as its terminals; the groups view opens none. Raises SchemaError for a group or strips box the unit does not hold, or a strip it lacks.

Cores are cable_rows' own. Ends are one per item a core lands on, in cable_end_rank order (a unit member first); a terminal's end is its strip. A non-cable child is left out.

Args: model: The frozen model to read. harness: The item whose cable children to list.

items.title: harness_line_ends
items.text:
def harness_line_ends(model: Model, subject: Id[Item]) -> tuple[HarnessLineEnd, ...]

The ends of subject's line: a harness's cables and wires, or one cable on no harness.

The one home of branch numbering: the line-text function reads -W13.n from branch and never numbers on its own. A plug is an end whose item is a direct child of subject or of one of its cables and which a core or wire lands on a connector function of. Cable and wire ends merge by end item into one order. Plugs come first, by the natural order of the connector's designation, then fan-out ends by their first pin's designation; an end item's id breaks a tie. So -W13.k ends at -W13-Pk in the common case.

Raises: SchemaError: subject is neither a harness nor a cable.

def is_plc_module(model: Model, item: Item) -> bool

Whether item's part has category PLC_MODULE: the one test of what a rack holds.

A rack is an item with at least one such child; plc_rack_modules lists them.

items.title: is_rail_terminal
items.text:
def is_rail_terminal(model: Model, terminal: Id[Item]) -> bool

Whether terminal is a rail terminal: on a DC rail or a PE net, bridged within its strip.

A rail terminal draws no symbol: its pins show the rail's power symbol. An AC rail, an unbridged terminal, a terminal whose part has a protective link and any item that is not a terminal are False.

items.title: is_replica_only_undrawn
items.text:
def is_replica_only_undrawn(model: Model, drawing_set: DrawingSet) -> bool

Whether the set has placements, all replicas, and no conductor route or LinkMarker.

A replica of the page unit's own boundary counts as drawn.

items.title: is_sole_unit_root
items.text:
def is_sole_unit_root(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> bool

Whether item is the only own-root item of its own unit.

False when item.unit is None. Otherwise True only when unit_own_roots of that unit is exactly (item,) (external items are not roots): a board that is the whole content of its own Unit is a nested unit, not a board sitting inside a larger one -- and a board sitting inside a larger unit still carries that larger unit on itself and on everything nested under it via parent=, so "shares a unit with an ancestor board" cannot tell the two cases apart; only "is the sole root of its unit" can. enclosing_boards above answers "which board (if any) encloses this item"; this answers "is that board a whole unit on its own, or merely furniture inside one".

Raises: SchemaError: item is not an item of model.

items.title: is_unit_owned_kind
items.text:
def is_unit_owned_kind(subject: Id[Record]) -> bool

Whether subject names an item, function, port, unit or document: what a unit owns.

items.title: item_description
items.text:
def item_description(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> str

The text a list shows for item: its own description, else its part's, else "".

An item stores only the description its author wrote; the part's is never copied onto it. A part-less item with none authored has no text.

Args: model: The model to read. item: The item whose list text is looked up.

Returns: item's own description, else its part's, else "".

Raises: SchemaError: item is not an item of model.

items.title: item_designation
items.text:
def item_designation(model: Model, item: Id[Item], *, relative_to: Id[Item] | None=None, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None, held_switches: bool=True) -> str

Render item's label: a terminal's group:index, else its text, behind its chain (A1-K1).

Args: model: The frozen model to read. item: The item to render. relative_to: An enclosing board: drops it and every ancestor outside it; None keeps all. unit: The unit whose own document is printed; drops its root's tag. None: whole model. held_switches: as takes_parents_designation.

Returns: item's printed label; an accessory's is its holder's.

Raises: SchemaError: designation_refusal of the same arguments is not None.

items.title: item_functions
items.text:

Each item that has functions, with the set of its functions.

items.title: item_installed
items.text:
def item_installed(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> bool

Whether item is installed; a drawing greys an item that is not (installed=False).

items.title: item_kind
items.text:
def item_kind(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> ItemKind

What item is: harness, cable, terminal, strip, PLC module, board, bar, connector or device.

The first that holds, in that order. Each test is the one predicate that already decides it: is_harness, is_cable, terminal_items, strip_set, is_plc_module, a part with a pcb facet, bar_items, and an item whose functions are all connectors. DEVICE is the rest.

Raises: SchemaError: item is not an item of model.

items.title: item_label
items.text:
def item_label(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> str

What an item is called in a message: its own text, else its authoring key joined by /.

Reads no holder and no numbering, and never raises, so it serves an item that has no designation (item_designation raises).

items.title: item_location
items.text:
def item_location(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> Id[AspectNode] | None

The LOCATION node item is placed at, own or inherited; None if it has none.

effective_placement in the LOCATION aspect. A unit's list document with no location of its own reads its strip's or board's here.

Args: model: The model to read. item: The item whose location is looked up.

Returns: The LOCATION AspectNode id, own or inherited, or None when there is none.

Raises: SchemaError: item is not an item of model.

The item whose function owns port.

items.title: item_pages
items.text:

Every item with each drawing page of a whole-system write that draws one of its functions.

The file is the one write names the document's PDF; the text is position_text of the page and the frame cell of the first placement on it. Empty when the model has no document.

items.title: item_parents
items.text:

Each child item's parent item, in the order the items table gives the parents.

items.title: item_role
items.text:

The role of item: its item_kind row plus the rack, external, accessory, root flags.

Lives beside item_kind so facts/roles never imports it back.

items.title: item_tag_text
items.text:

A component's tag on a drawing: its item designation only, "-Q11".

The page states the location, unit and groups, so a tag never carries them, in a unit's own set (unit, unit-relative) and at top level alike. The one function every component and strip tag on a drawing is built from.

items.title: item_unit
items.text:

The unit item is recorded in by Item.unit; None for the integrating script's own.

Return every Item in model, by id.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every Item in model, keyed by id; the model's own table, so nothing is copied. Empty when the model holds none.

items.title: items_at
items.text:
def items_at(model: Model, node: Id[AspectNode]) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

Every item at node or at a node in subtree(model, node), once each, sorted by id.

An item counts by its own Placement, else by its nearest placed ancestor's (effective_placement): a board's own component is listed at the board's location or group.

Args: model: The model to read. node: The aspect node (and its subtree) to list items at.

Returns: Every item's id found at node or its subtree, once each, sorted.

Raises: SchemaError: node is not an aspect node of model.

The distinct lanes lanes uses (the highest lane plus one), not one per group.

Each jumper group's lane, from groups (each row's jumper_group), by group number.

items.text:
def keep_whole_sets(model: Model) -> KeepWhole

The KeepWhole sets of model: add-on item boxes, pole groups and units with a line.

An item box is today approximated by "an item with children": the generic-box test lives in layout (read/views.box_drawn, needs the symbol rules) until EL-2 gives function_role.box.

The sheet a page of kind of unit is on (layout.sheet_for) as a SheetRow.

The text a lane prints: its group's folded-box text, on one line.

The first switch of function's group that is wired, else the group's first; else None.

items.title: line_conductors
items.text:
def line_conductors(model: Model) -> frozendict[Id[Item], tuple[Id[Conductor], ...]]

Each line's owner with the conductors its line carries, for owners with two or more.

The owner is a harness, or a cable on no harness. Cores count for their cable's owner and a single wire for its harness (harness_of_wire). Conductors are sorted by id.

items.title: line_designation
items.text:
def line_designation(model: Model, harness: Id[Item], branch: int, *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> str

-W13 for a line between two ends, -W13.n on each branch of three or more, else "".

branch is the HarnessLineEnd.branch of the end; this never numbers on its own. Raises SchemaError when branch is no branch of the line.

items.title: line_stub_line
items.text:
def line_stub_line(line: str, *, north: bool, far: Sequence[tuple[str, str]]) -> str

A leaving line's single stub, -W3 → +EXT-M1 p2:4A, +EXT-M2 p2:5C: line, arrow, far devices.

far is each far device with where it is drawn in the stub's drawing set, position_text's form, or "" for none. No place at all keeps the first device alone, the text without places. The arrow points up (←) for a stub facing north, else →.

items.title: line_tabs
items.text:
def line_tabs(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None) -> tuple[LineTab, ...]

The end tabs of unit's cable lines (None: the system), one row per diagram line.

ref is the line's LineRef on overview_level; tab_a stands at its a box and tab_b at its b box, each the text the block diagram prints there, None for no tab. A line of another kind, or a cable line the diagram lifts differently, has no row.

items.title: link_role
items.text:
def link_role(model: Model, link: Id[InternalLink]) -> LinkRole

The role of an internal link: its kind's row, with the pole and rest the function adds.

A protection's conductive link is a pole; a switched link rests as declared, else as its function's kind implies.

items.title: link_state
items.text:
def link_state(model: Model, function: Id[Function], link: Id[InternalLink]) -> LinkState

The state in which the internal link link of the contact function is closed.

A switched link's declared rest decides first (CLOSED is "rest", OPEN "operated"). Otherwise CONTACT_NO implies "operated", CONTACT_NC "rest", and CONTACT_CO the roles of the link's ends through _pole (common to BREAK "rest", to MAKE "operated"). Anything else is "both", an unknown id too; it never raises.

Args: model: The model to read. function: The contact function the link belongs to. link: The internal link whose closed state is found.

Returns: "rest", "operated", or "both".

items.title: link_throw
items.text:
def link_throw(link: InternalLink, templates: Mapping[Id[PortTemplate], PortTemplate]) -> tuple[Id[PortTemplate], PortRole, Id[PortTemplate]] | None

(common, BREAK or MAKE, throw) when link is a switched link joining a common to a throw.

The template-level reading changeover_throws builds on; authoring reads it before a model.

items.title: list_context
items.text:
def list_context(model: Model, subject: Id[Item], *, location: Id[AspectNode] | None=None) -> Id[AspectNode] | None

The location a list's ends print short against: the document's, else subject's own.

None means no context: the list queries print full paths.

Args: model: The model to read. subject: The strip or board item the list is of. location: The location document's own node, keyword-only; None falls back to subject's.

Returns: location when given, else item_location of subject; None when neither exists.

Raises: SchemaError: location is None and subject is not an item of model.

The interface text of the unit a baseline listing lists.

The v.r text of the version and revision of the unit a baseline listing lists.

items.title: load_limits
items.text:
def load_limits(model: Model) -> tuple[LoadLimit, ...]

The draw of each load edge and the limit that bounds it, per current kind.

A load with no stated draw, no current kind or fewer than two conductive ports has no entry. One load at a time is added to the graph, so the loads never bound each other.

items.title: location_fold
items.text:
def location_fold(model: Model) -> LocationFold | None

The system level folded by top place, or None when the model has under two top places.

A box in no place stands in a "No location" box, last. A line joins two boxes with the number of distinct cables between their members; cables inside one place are no line.

items.title: location_node_designation
items.text:
def location_node_designation(model: Model, node: Id[AspectNode]) -> str

Render an aspect node's signed path, root to leaf (+C1, nested +ER+C1, a group =G1).

The node's own aspect gives the sign, repeated at every level: for a location, exactly the segment location_designation renders for an item placed at node. scope_path calls it too, so a title block's scope cell prints the same full path (+R+S1).

items.title: location_place_title
items.text:
def location_place_title(model: Model, place: Id[AspectNode]) -> str

A place's printed title, its designation then its text on one line (+ER Engine room).

The box prints these as two lines; the overview's panel prints the title. One spelling.

items.title: manifest_rows
items.text:
def manifest_rows(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None) -> ManifestRows

The identity, history, part libraries and nested releases of unit's manifest.

unit=None is the system. Each nested row carries the sha256 of the nested listing's canonical text, hashed once here. Warning texts and package versions stay with the facade.

items.title: mate_port_of
items.text:
def mate_port_of(model: Model, port: Id[Port], function: Id[Function]) -> Id[Port] | None

The port of function mated to port by name (the lowest id of that name), else None.

items.title: mate_ports
items.text:
def mate_ports(model: Model) -> tuple[tuple[Id[Port], Id[Port]], ...]

Each mate's (a port, b port) pairs, ports of equal name paired once, sorted by id.

A name held by several ports of one side pairs each with the first port of that name on the other side, so equal-named ports stay one chain.

items.title: mates
items.text:
def mates(model: Model) -> tuple[MateRow, ...]

One MateRow per mate in model, sorted by (a_designation, b_designation).

A mate joins two connector or terminal functions, kept in the authored order of d.mate. A mate on a board and one between a plug and a unit's interface connector both appear, where connector_rows covers board connectors only. Each designation is the text the connector list prints at system level. Reach an item through the function.

Raises: SchemaError: a mated function is not of model, or its item has no designation.

items.title: mixed_sheet_groups
items.text:
def mixed_sheet_groups(model: Model, document: Id[Document], pages: tuple[PageKind, ...]) -> tuple[SheetGroup, ...]

Each sheet format the drawn pages name with its page numbers; empty unless more than one.

items.title: moved_findings
items.text:

DESIGNATION_MOVED: a pinned item or instance now prints a different own text.

items.title: natural_key
items.text:

Sort key of a printed text: digit runs by value, so -W2 sorts before -W10.

Text runs compare as strings and sort after numbers; the whole text breaks a tie.

Every unit nested in unit's subtree, sorted; None is every unit of the model.

The label of aspect node node.

items.title: number
items.text:
def number(model: Model) -> tuple[Model, tuple[Finding, ...]]

Number every item that has no own designation from its Part.class_code.

Each such item gets a facet.assigned_designation of class code plus a counter, one counter per sibling group (unit, nearest designating ancestor, class code). A tag or existing facet is kept; terminals, partless items and accessories are skipped. Also reports the *_DUPLICATE and HARNESS_END_AMBIGUOUS findings (all ERROR).

Args: model: The model to number.

Returns: model itself if nothing was numbered, else evolved with the new facets; and the findings, sorted by (code, subjects, message).

items.title: one_line_field
items.text:
def one_line_field(preferred: str, *, size_mm: float, bold: bool=False, width_mm: float, shorter: tuple[str, ...]=()) -> tuple[str, bool]

(text, fits): the first of preferred and shorter that fits, else the last, cut.

The one rule for which text a one-line cell prints and whether it needs the cut; shorter follows preferred in decreasing length.

items.text:
def open_core_rows(model: Model, cable: Id[Item], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> tuple[OpenCoreRow, ...]

One OpenCoreRow per open core of cable, by core number.

Args: model: The frozen model to read. cable: The cable item whose spares and one-ended screens to list. unit: The unit whose own document draws the cable, keyword-only; None is the whole model.

The strips of level that open: those holding at least one terminal, in box order.

What operates a switch function: its own part's operated_by, else its nearest holder's.

None for any other kind, or when no part on the way up states one.

items.text:

The item whose part states what operates a switch function.

Its own item when its part states one, else the nearest holder that does; None for any other kind, or when none states one.

items.text:

Every layout.page in set then page order; replica-only sets drop out when asked.

The text of a line to a stub: its carrier relative to unit, else the count text.

The text of a field box's lifted line: its cables as overview_lifted_text prints them.

The text of a folded level's line: its label (cables or -X3 x 3), else the count text.

The text lines of a folded stub's box: its far name; a closed fold prints no member list.

A fold of several members prints its name and count (Field devices (2)); any other stub also prints the port tails of its members.

items.title: overview_fold_stub_text
items.text:
def overview_fold_stub_text(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit], stub: FoldStub) -> str

The text of the line to a folded stub: its carrier relative to unit, else the count.

items.title: overview_graph
items.text:
def overview_graph(model: Model) -> OverviewGraph

The overview: one node per item, the aggregated links between items, the multi-item signals.

This query does not raise for an item with no designation yet: OverviewNode.designation (and a link's via_designation) is None there, so a half-finished design still draws. Other designations are printed_designation ("-K1", "-X1:L1:1"). Nodes sort by (designation with None last, id). A link joins two items by one kind and one via: wire for a conductor with no carrier, cable for the conductors of one cable item, mate for Mates between functions of the two items (count is the number of mates, conductors empty). a is the smaller id; links sort by (a, b, kind value, via), no via first. A signal is a physical net (physical_nets) that reaches at least two items, its ports sorted by (item id, pin order, port id); signals sort by their first port.

items.title: overview_lane_nodes
items.text:
def overview_lane_nodes(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> dict[BoxKey, Id[AspectNode] | None]

Each box of unit's level: its function group node, None for a strip or no group.

items.title: overview_lane_strips
items.text:
def overview_lane_strips(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> frozenset[BoxKey]

The boxes of unit's level that are terminal strips, which stand in the shared lane.

items.title: overview_level
items.text:
def overview_level(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None) -> OverviewLevel

One level of the overview: the system (unit=None) or unit opened.

The system level is diagram_lines of the block diagram: unit boxes with tabs, by-others items dashed, one line per cable. An opened unit has one box per nested unit (with its boundary tabs), per terminal strip (folded, with its terminal count) and per other root item, with connectors on a box as its tabs. A line joins two boxes per kind and carrier; a connection between items inside one box is dropped, and count is the connections lifted into the line. A connection to an item outside unit is a stub at the inside box, named by stub_far_end. Designations are relative to unit. Boxes and lines are in box text order.

items.title: overview_lifted_text
items.text:
def overview_lifted_text(kind: OverviewLinkKind, carriers: Sequence[str], count: int) -> str

The one text of a line for count connections carried by cables printed carriers.

One carrier prints its designation, several print x N for N carriers, none print the count text (x 3 for a wire or mate line of three, else empty). Every level's lifted lines use it.

items.title: overview_line_text
items.text:
def overview_line_text(line: OverviewLine) -> str

The text of a line: its carrier's designation, else the count text.

items.title: overview_location_line_text
items.text:

The text of a location line: its cables as overview_lifted_text prints them.

items.title: overview_power_lines
items.text:
def overview_power_lines(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> frozenset[tuple[BoxKey, BoxKey]]

The ends of each line of unit's level that carries a conductor on an AC potential.

items.title: overview_strip_joins
items.text:
def overview_strip_joins(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> dict[BoxKey, int]

Each box joined to a terminal strip: the place of the first terminal it joins.

Strips run in box text order, each strip's terminals in the strip's own order; the place counts terminals over all strips. A box that joins no strip is absent. A stub box counts as joined: its far end is the box that joins the terminal.

items.title: overview_stub_lines
items.text:
def overview_stub_lines(stub: OverviewStub) -> tuple[str, ...]

The text lines of a stub's box: the far device, then its port tails when it has any.

items.title: overview_stub_text
items.text:
def overview_stub_text(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit], stub: OverviewStub) -> str

The text of the line to a stub: its carrier relative to unit, else the count text.

items.title: overview_stub_west
items.text:
def overview_stub_west(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit], end: OverviewRef) -> bool

Whether the lanes stub for end stands west of the level of unit; else east.

West: an item that is a terminal strip, or one held by a unit that encloses unit.

items.title: overview_tree
items.text:
def overview_tree(model: Model) -> tuple[TreeRow, ...]

The rows of the parts tree in display order, each naming its parent row by index.

items.title: overview_units
items.text:

None for the system, then every unit instance by the natural order of its designation.

items.title: overview_view_rows
items.text:
def overview_view_rows(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None) -> tuple[ViewRows, ...]

The views of unit's level (None: the system), each with its boxes and lines.

The plain level, each of its strips opened, and for a unit its folded levels: the groups, the all-devices level and each group. A fold is never a view of its own. A level with no box has no view.

items.title: own_drawing_line

def physical_nets(model: Model) -> tuple[PhysicalNet, ...]

Union-find model's ports into physical nets.

A port with no connectivity or no template is its own singleton PhysicalNet. Sorted by each net's ports, so record order never matters; cached on model.digest.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every physical net, sorted by its own ports tuple.

items.title: plc_channel_rows
items.text:
def plc_channel_rows(model: Model, *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None, context: Id[AspectNode] | None=None) -> tuple[PlcChannelRow, ...]

One PlcChannelRow per pin of each PLC channel Function, in the PLC list's table order.

The order is plc_channel_key: controllers by designation, each one's own channels then its modules in rack order, last the channels on items in no rack. wired_to is the far end of every conductor at that pin's port. unit keeps only channels of that unit; context is the location node the list is printed for, ignored once unit has one.

Raises: SchemaError: a module or device has no designation, or unit is no unit of model.

items.title: plc_list_rows
items.text:
def plc_list_rows(rows: Iterable[PlcChannelRow]) -> tuple[tuple[str | None, ...], ...]

One PLC_COLUMNS line per row for a printed list: the signal as its word.

A channel bound to no field device and wired to nothing prints spare for its signal name. The cells follow PLC_COLUMNS' order, so a column change edits that tuple alone.

items.title: plc_rack_modules
items.text:
def plc_rack_modules(model: Model, rack: Id[Item], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> tuple[PlcRackModule, ...]

One PlcRackModule per PLC module of rack, in physical rack order.

The modules are the children of rack by parent whose Part has category PLC_MODULE; a module with no channel (a coupler, an end module) has channels=(). They order by position (integers ascending, None last), then the module's own tag in natural order (plc_module_key), the order allocate_plc serves them in; installed is ignored. A module's channels are the functions whose template carries a plc_channel, bound or spare, ordered by plc_channel_tie. The field device is read as plc_channel_rows reads it; scaling is its scaling facet, None for a spare channel or a device without one.

unit prints the designations as that unit's own document does; None the full form.

Raises: SchemaError: rack is not an item of model, or a module or device has no designation.

items.title: plc_tables
items.text:
def plc_tables(model: Model, *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None, context: Id[AspectNode] | None=None) -> tuple[PlcTable, ...]

The rows of plc_channel_rows, one PlcTable per carrying item, in the same order.

A controller's own channels form its table, then each module's follow in rack order; the items in no rack come last, one table each. An item with no channel has no table. unit and context are plc_channel_rows's.

Raises: SchemaError: as plc_channel_rows.

items.title: port_designation
items.text:
def port_designation(model: Model, port: Id[Port], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> str

Render port as its item's designation and its name (-K1:13), always dash-prefixed.

A terminal's port drops its name (terminal_designation); a connector pin reads -U2-X1:1; a bar's port drops it too (-PE1): the screw is no part of the wiring (PE-BAR B4).

Args: model: The frozen model to read. port: The port to render. unit: The unit whose own document is printed; None renders the whole-model form.

Raises: SchemaError: port is not of model, or its item (a terminal's parent too) has none.

items.title: port_is_reached
items.text:
def port_is_reached(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> bool

Whether a wire inside the drawing of port's unit, or a net, reaches port itself.

The same rule as function_is_reached, for one port: layout draws a connector pin only where this holds for it or its mated pin, or a parent's black box needs it.

items.title: port_is_unused
items.text:
def port_is_unused(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> bool

Whether no conductor (wire, jumper, cable core or link) ends at port and no net has it.

A mate does not count. This is the one test of an unused port; a function is unused when all its ports are (function_is_unused).

items.title: port_name
items.text:
def port_name(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> str

The raw name of port on its function, not the printed one (printed_port_name).

items.title: port_potential_current
items.text:
def port_potential_current(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> Current | None

The current, AC or DC, of the supply behind port_potential_rank's potential.

None when the port has no rank, and for protective earth, which belongs to no supply.

items.title: port_potential_rank
items.text:
def port_potential_rank(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> int | None

The rank of the potential port carries in service: smaller is drawn higher up, else None.

The order comes from the supply's declared facts, never from a rail's name: AC rails with a phase, by phase; DC rails above 0 V, highest first; the AC rail at 0 V; the DC rail at 0 V; DC rails below 0 V, highest first; protective earth last. Equal facts tie by potential text, since declaration order is no model fact (models differing only in it are equal). A port takes its own declared net's potential, else what the rail closure reaches through conductors, mates, conductive and switched links (port_rails), so a pin behind a contact keeps its rank. Reached from two rails (a changeover between two sources), it takes the lower rank. A net potential that no supply declares gives None. Power-symbol eligibility is a separate question that keeps the physical net.

items.title: port_power_kind
items.text:
def port_power_kind(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> PowerKind

The PowerKind of the physical net of port; NONE when port is not in model.

A load pin wired to a 24 V terminal gets the kind of that net though no Net lists it. Cost: O(1) once per model digest, like port_rails.

items.title: port_power_text
items.text:
def port_power_text(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> str | None

The text the power symbol at port prints: power_text of its physical net, else None.

A load pin wired to a 24 V terminal prints that net's text. Cost: O(1) once per model digest.

items.title: port_rails
items.text:
def port_rails(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> frozenset[str]

The rails port carries: the empty set for a port that carries none or is not in model.

A rail is a potential some SupplySystem declares and a declared Net carries. Each spreads from its nets' ports through conductors, mates, conductive and switched links (contacts counted closed) but never enters a net carrying another rail. A changeover's common reached from two rails carries both. Only structure is read, never a port name. Which rails stand at once: rail_pairs. Cached on model.digest.

Args: model: The model to read. port: The port whose rails are looked up.

Returns: The names of the rails port carries.

items.title: port_role
items.text:
def port_role(model: Model, port: Id[Port]) -> PortRole

The PortRole of port: the one reader of Port.role.

items.title: ports
items.text:
def ports(model: Model) -> frozendict[Id[Port], Port]

Return every Port in model, by id.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every Port in model, keyed by id; the model's own table, so nothing is copied. Empty when the model holds none.

items.title: power_kind
items.text:
def power_kind(model: Model, net: Id[Net]) -> PowerKind

The PowerKind of declared net, read from its physical net, never from its name.

A net of class PE is PE, supplied or not. Otherwise the physical net's one potential is looked up in the supplies: a DC rail above or below 0 V is SUPPLY, a DC rail at 0 V is GROUND. An AC rail, a potential in no supply, no potential, or two potentials on one physical net are NONE, as is a net whose ports fall in physical nets of different kinds. A physical net of exactly two ports, bridges and links counted, is NONE whatever its potential: a wire, not a rail; it keeps the potential. A DC supply that declares no 0 V rail leaves its 0 V net NONE: declare it.

Raises: KeyError: net is not a declared Net of model.

items.title: power_text
items.text:
def power_text(model: Model, net: Id[Net]) -> str | None

The text a power symbol of declared net prints, or None when it prints none.

Only SUPPLY prints: Net.name, else Net.potential (which carries the sign of a negative rail, -15V). GROUND, PE and NONE print none.

items.title: previous_release
items.text:

The stored release with the highest order strictly below identity's, or None.

items.text:

The sets some document of model prints, by number; none that no document prints.

items.title: profile_of
items.text:

The profile unit authors (None: the top design), or the house one (default_profile()).

The one reader of a profile. It matches unit exactly and never falls back to a containing unit or to the top's: a unit with no profile of its own draws with the house numbers.

items.title: project_facts
items.text:
def project_facts(model: Model) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, str, str]

(title, number, customer, revision, revision_date, author); all empty with no Project.

items.title: prospective_fault
items.text:
def prospective_fault(model: Model) -> tuple[ProspectiveFault, ...]

The prospective fault current at each protective position, per current kind.

One entry per position whose function is a protection one and per kind its rails carry. A bolted fault at either terminal joins it to every other rail of its supplies; the loads are left out, every source and every declared supply that states a fault current counts. A position no source reaches reads 0.

items.title: rack_modules_for_cdp
items.text:
def rack_modules_for_cdp(model: Model, rack: Id[Item], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> tuple[CdpRackModule, ...]

The modules of rack that have channels, each with its ordinal and single_signal.

A module with no channel (a coupler, an end module) is left out. ordinal counts the kept modules of one mpn in rack order from 0, so an output can letter them; single_signal is the one signal type all channels share, None when they differ. unit: as plc_rack_modules.

Raises: SchemaError: as plc_rack_modules raises it.

items.title: rail_pairs
items.text:
def rail_pairs(model: Model, function: Id[Function]) -> frozenset[tuple[str, str]]

The pairs (low, high) of rail names, low < high, that can stand across function.

Two rails at two different ports of the function, whose conditions agree (no item in two states). A rest link needs its item at rest, an operated link operated, both nothing; a link only adds a condition, never blocks. Two rails at one port are never a pair. Known limit: all contacts of one item move together, so a pair may be missed (it errs towards silence).

Args: model: The model to read. function: The function whose standing rail pairs are found.

Returns: Every pair (low, high) of rail names that can stand across function; empty for a function with no pair, an unknown function, or no rail.

items.title: readability_units
items.text:
def readability_units(pages: Iterable[ReadabilityPage], loose: Mapping[Id[Unit] | None, int]) -> tuple[ReadabilityUnit, ...]

One row per unit of pages, in the order its first page comes; None is the design.

items.title: reading_cables
items.text:
def reading_cables(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None) -> tuple[HarnessCable, ...]

The one home of that choice, so no output or layout step repeats it.

unit and every unit below it, deepest first, then the system; None covers the model.

The key text of the record subject names, looked up in the table of its kind.

items.title: reference_designation
items.text:
def reference_designation(model: Model, item: Id[Item], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> str

Render item's full IEC 81346 reference: =A1+C1-K1, and =A1-X1:L1:1 for a terminal.

Own placements give the =/+ labels (reference_leaves), then the product part, as printed.

Args: model: The frozen model to read. item: The item to render. unit: The unit whose own document is printed: keeps its own nodes. None: whole model.

items.title: release_names

The name of every unit release, in table order.

items.title: release_order

(version, revision): the ONE order of unit releases and of history entries.

The plain pair of two ints, never the printed text: (1, 9) < (1, 10) < (2, 1), where the text "1.10" would sort before "1.9". Every later pin-source and previous-release selection calls this function and never compares revisions again.

items.title: resolve_wire_rows

Write the WireFacet of every hinted wire from its row; the rest are ERROR findings.

What source says about unit's revision: moved designations, then new floating ones.

items.title: revision_history
items.text:
def revision_history(model: Model, release: Id[UnitRelease] | None=None) -> tuple[Revision, ...]

Every Revision of release, in date order, then version and revision order.

release=None selects the project's own history: every entry with Revision.release is None. Every instance of a release shares the release's history. "Revision order" sorts by the ints (version, revision), so revision 2 sorts before revision 10.

Raises: SchemaError: release is not None and names no UnitRelease of model.

revision_history as rows: date order, then version and revision order.

items.title: revision_text
items.text:
def revision_text(version: int, revision: int) -> str

The revision as printed: f"{version}.{revision}", 1.1, 2.1, 1.10.

The one home of the print form: a title block's Rev cell, a revision history row, a unit line's BOM Revision column, a black box title and a message naming a revision all call it. Nothing else formats the pair.

items.title: run_point_text
items.text:

A strip terminal's point text in a run, "L2:1".

The terminal's own group:index, the strip's designation left out (strip_tag_text prints it). A terminal that is no part of a run prints terminal_designation, never this.

items.title: same_version
items.text:
def same_version(previous: tuple[str, int], current: tuple[str, int]) -> bool

Whether two releases are the same name and version; revision is never compared.

previous/current are each (name, version), read straight off whichever record the caller has (UnitRelease, a stored listing's unit, a release target) -- never a new record type of its own.

items.title: schematic_functions
items.text:
def schematic_functions(model: Model) -> tuple[Id[Function], ...]

Every Function the schematic engine actually attempts to draw, in Id order.

Excludes a cable item's own function and every function on or under a board item (enclosing_boards), with two exceptions. A CONNECTOR function on or under a board is always drawn: the board is a black box on the cabinet page, its edge connectors are not. A non-CONNECTOR function stays when the nearest enclosing board is_sole_unit_root: a board that is the whole content of its Unit is drawn like any unit's set. One predicate for layout and render, since neither package may import the other.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every drawn function's id, sorted.

def sheet_key_text(key: SheetKey) -> str

The printed form of a SheetKey, for a message: <document>#<KIND>#<ordinal or none>.

items.title: sheet_text
items.text:
def sheet_text(model: Model, sheet: Page | DiagramSheet) -> str

The sheet number a sheet prints: 3, 2.3 in a set past its unit's first, B1.

The destination label and a reference keep the set-and-page form p1.3 (set_page_text).

items.title: sheet_title_text
items.text:
def sheet_title_text(model: Model, sheet: Page | DiagramSheet, title: str) -> str

Sheet 3: Pump 1: a sheet's outline entry text; with no title, Sheet 3.

items.title: sheets
items.text:
def sheets(model: Model, document: Id[Document], kinds: tuple[PageKind, ...]) -> tuple[DiagramSheet | Page, ...]

Block diagram sheets in number order, then schematic pages in set then page order.

kinds is the document's page kinds: a dropped kind contributes no sheet.

items.title: short_title
items.text:
def short_title(entries: tuple[str, ...]) -> str | None

first to last with their shared leading words printed once; None for one entry.

"Relay 1" and "Relay 3" give "Relay 1 to 3"; with no shared word, or none left after it, "Supply to Pump 2". A first and last entry that are the same text have no short form.

items.title: sideless_pins
items.text:
def sideless_pins(one: str, first: tuple[PortTemplate, ...], two: str, second: tuple[PortTemplate, ...]) -> SidelessPins

Order each end by port_order_key; problem names one and two when they do not pair.

A pin with no printed marking sorts by its name. The ends do not pair when they have a different number of pins, or the same names in another order.

items.title: signal_kind
items.text:
def signal_kind(signal: SignalType) -> SignalKind

The form and direction of a PLC signal type, for a channel's facet or a field request's.

DI is digital in, DO and RELAY digital out; the two analogue inputs and RTD analogue in; the two analogue outputs analogue out. A channel and the request it serves give one kind.

items.title: signal_lens
items.text:
def signal_lens(model: Model) -> tuple[LensModule, ...]

The PLC modules with their channels and field devices.

Racks in plc_rack_key order, then plc_rack_modules' physical order within each, so the lens reads the rack as the PLC list does. Each channel carries signal_kind of its signal type. A module with no channel is not listed. Raises SchemaError, as plc_rack_modules does, for a module or device with no designation.

items.title: signal_word
items.text:
def signal_word(signal: SignalType) -> str

The datasheet word for signal: DI, DO, AI (V), AI (mA), AO (V), AO (mA), RTD.

A relay output prints DO (relay).

items.title: sizes_of
items.text:
def sizes_of(model: Model, document: Id[Document]) -> Sizes

The font sizes of a document's pages: its unit's profile (the top's) sets the smallest.

document is the document's id.

items.title: stale_patterns
items.text:
def stale_patterns() -> tuple[str, ...]

The top-level file patterns a write owns and sweeps: every kind of export_set.

Per-item kinds give <kind>-*.<ext> and the bare <kind>.<ext>; PDFs are *.pdf.

items.title: standalone
items.text:
def standalone(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> bool

Whether every item of model belongs to unit's subtree.

A unit is standalone when nothing in model sits outside it: no item with unit=None and no item of another unit that is not in unit's own subtree.

Raises: SchemaError: unit is not a unit of model.

items.title: stands
items.text:
def stands(model: Model) -> frozendict[Id[Port], PowerKind]

Each port of a rail net, mapped to the net's PowerKind; a wire or a signal is absent.

Built on power.port_power_kind, the one rail rule, so a two-port net is never a stand.

items.title: strip_of
items.text:
def strip_of(model: Model, item: Id[Item]) -> Id[Item] | None

item's strip when it is a terminal: its Item.parent; None for anything else.

items.title: strip_side_headings
items.text:
def strip_side_headings(model: Model, strip: Id[Item]) -> tuple[str, str]

Ends headings: the strip's shared non-empty markings, else TERMINAL_LABELS.

items.title: strip_stubs
items.text:
def strip_stubs(model: Model, strip: Id[Item], unit: Id[Unit]) -> tuple[TerminalStubs, ...]

The stubs of each terminal of strip opened on unit's level, in strip order.

A terminal wired to an item outside unit has one stub per far end, as the level's stubs are named (stub_far_end), standing at the terminal. A terminal with none has an empty tuple.

items.title: strip_view
items.text:
def strip_view(model: Model, strip: Id[Item], unit: Id[Unit]) -> StripView

strip opened on unit's level: its terminals in strip order, each with its lines.

Strip order is the terminal's group (natural order) then its index. A line runs from the terminal to the box on the other end, left out when that end is the strip itself or lies outside unit.

items.title: stub_ends
items.text:
def stub_ends(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit], placed: Sequence[tuple[OverviewRef, OverviewStub | FoldStub]]) -> tuple[tuple[StubBox, ...], tuple[StubLine, ...]]

The stub boxes and lines of placed, each stub with the box at it hangs on.

A box holds the first stub's far text, then the port tails of all its stubs once each, in order. Counts add per kind and carrier; a line's text is overview_end_text, or x N to a closed fold (N its distinct cables when it is a cable fold). Both keep first-seen order.

items.title: subject_kind
items.text:
def subject_kind(subject: Id[Record]) -> SubjectKind

What subject names: an item, port, function, conductor, unit or location node, else other.

Example: the id of an item gives SubjectKind.ITEM; the id of a net gives OTHER.

items.title: subject_kind_text
items.text:
def subject_kind_text(subject: Id[Record]) -> str

The kind text of subject's handle ("net", "item", ...), as an error names it.

items.title: subject_label
items.text:
def subject_label(model: Model, document: Id[Document]) -> str

The heading's subject: location, unit or item label; "" for SYSTEM.

document is the document's id.

items.title: subject_marks
items.text:
def subject_marks(model: Model, rows: ViewRows, lookup: dict[RefKey, int], subject: Subject) -> tuple[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]]

(boxes, lines) indexes of rows the subject counts on; the lines when it has any.

lookup is view_lookup(model, rows). A cable item counts on its own lines, a conductor on the line between its two boxes; else the subject counts on each distinct box of its ends.

items.title: subject_part_mpn
items.text:
def subject_part_mpn(model: Model, subject: Id[Record]) -> str | None

The mpn of the part of an item, or of a function's item; None when it has no part.

items.title: subtree
items.text:
def subtree(model: Model, node: Id[AspectNode]) -> tuple[Id[AspectNode], ...]

Every descendant of node by AspectNode.parent, node excluded, sorted by id.

Follows parent whatever the aspect (ASPECT_CROSS_PARENT is the validator's) and is cycle-safe.

Args: model: The model to read. node: The aspect node whose descendants are listed.

Returns: Every descendant's id, sorted.

Raises: SchemaError: node is not an aspect node of model.

items.title: supply_share
items.text:
def supply_share(model: Model, function: Id[Function]) -> Fraction

The share of function's connected pins that carry a supply potential, 0 with none.

A pin carries a supply when port_potential_rank gives it a rank: a rail, 24 V or GND. It is a rank, not a direction, since a potential cannot tell "fed by" from "feeds". Layout calls it to split a unit's interfaces between its two edges and never asks again.

items.title: supply_systems
items.text:
def supply_systems(model: Model) -> frozendict[Id[SupplySystem], SupplySystem]

Return every SupplySystem in model, by id.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every SupplySystem in model, keyed by id; the model's own table, so nothing is copied. Empty when the model holds none.

items.title: symbol_port_subject
items.text:
def symbol_port_subject(model: Model, function: Id[Function] | Id[Item], port_name: str) -> Id[PortTemplate] | Id[Part] | Id[Function] | Id[Item]

The PortTemplate of function's template named port_name, else its Part, else itself.

function is a Function of the model, or the whole Item of a one-view draw (no template).

items.title: system_has_no_top_level_cables
items.text:

A SYSTEM document whose model has no top-level cable at all.

document is the document's id.

items.title: tag_text
items.text:
def tag_text(model: Model, function: Id[Function]) -> str

A TAG label's text: the designation the layout engine used.

A terminal function's tag is the designation of its lowest-handle port; every other function's tag is its item's item_tag_text.

items.title: takes_energy
items.text:
def takes_energy(model: Model, function: Id[Function]) -> bool

Whether function takes energy in: its role's energy (a load, actuator, coil or in).

An energy-in function (a load, a motor, a coil, or a supply declared energy = in) sits above an energy-out one.

items.title: takes_parents_designation
items.text:
def takes_parents_designation(model: Model, item: Id[Item], *, held_switches: bool=True) -> bool

Whether item is an accessory: it prints its parent's designation, having none of its own.

True for a part-bearing item with no own text, terminal facet, board or harness role, whose parent is a designated part-bearing item (an own text, or a part class code), not a terminal, enclosing board or harness. A footprint part, or a function in the subtree (a device, but not an add-on contact block), makes item a part of its own. Unknown: False.

Args: model: The frozen model to read. item: The item to classify. held_switches: False: no contact block of held switches (before 0.18.2).

Returns: True if item is an accessory that prints its parent's designation.

items.title: terminal_items
items.text:
def terminal_items(model: Model) -> frozenset[Id[Item]]

Every item that carries a terminal facet, built once per model digest.

items.title: terminal_rows
items.text:
def terminal_rows(model: Model, strip: Id[Item], *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None, context: Id[AspectNode] | None=None) -> tuple[TerminalRow, ...]

One TerminalRow per strip terminal, by (natural_key(group), index, id).

Args: model: The model to read. strip: The terminal strip item whose rows are built. unit: The unit whose own document prints the list, keyword-only; None for none. context: The location node the list prints for, keyword-only; ignored once unit has one.

Returns: One TerminalRow per terminal child of strip, sorted.

Raises: SchemaError: strip is not an item of model, or a far end's item has no designation.

items.title: terminal_strips
items.text:
def terminal_strips(model: Model) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

Every item that at least one terminal facet names as its strip, in designation order.

A terminal's strip is its parent item: TerminalFacet carries no strip field of its own. Shared by fransys's export enumeration and the pdf document contents, so the two never disagree about what a strip is.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every strip item's id, by natural designation, then id.

items.title: text_room
items.text:
def text_room(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None) -> int

The grid units a text line gets under unit's profile (None: the top) and its sheet.

The one reader of the profile and sheet for the text room; sizes come from text_room_g.

items.title: text_room_g
items.text:
def text_room_g(text_height_mm: Decimal, module_mm: Decimal) -> int

The grid units a text of capital height text_height_mm gets: font size over one G, up.

items.title: text_under_floor
items.text:
def text_under_floor(profile: Profile) -> Decimal | None

The capital height of profile's text when it is under min_text_height_mm.

items.title: text_width_mm
items.text:
def text_width_mm(text: str, *, size_mm: float, bold: bool=False) -> float

The width of text in DejaVu Sans Condensed at size_mm, from the one table.

items.title: title_block_overflows
items.text:
def title_block_overflows(model: Model, document: Id[Document], sheets: DocumentSheets, rooms: Mapping[str, float]) -> tuple[TitleBlockOverflow, ...]

The fields that miss their cell: the six document-level ones, then each checked page's.
