items.text:
def title_block_strings(fields: TitleBlockFields, rooms: Mapping[str, float], sizes: Sizes, *, notice_width_mm: float, notice_capacity: int) -> TitleBlockStrings

What the title block prints: each field cut to its slot's room, the notice wrapped.

items.title: top_level_cables
items.text:
def top_level_cables(model: Model) -> tuple[HarnessCable, ...]

Every cable item with no unit, harness cables included, as HarnessCable.

Selected as cable_list_rows selects (_top_level_cable_ids): every cable item (is_cable) with unit=None, a cable inside a harness included. Built by _cable_facts, as in harness_cables. Sorted by (designation, id).

Args: model: The frozen model to read.

Returns: Every top-level cable (unit=None), sorted by (designation, id).

Raises: SchemaError: a cable, or an item one of its cores lands on, has no designation.

items.title: unconnected_ports
items.text:
def unconnected_ports(model: Model) -> tuple[Id[Port], ...]

Every port whose physical net is a singleton, in id order (physical_nets is sorted).

A conductor, a conductive link or a Mate reaching a port connects it; a declared Net does not, deliberately unlike FUNCTION_HALF_CONNECTED, which is about authoring intent.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every port with no other port on its physical net, sorted.

items.title: unit_boards
items.text:
def unit_boards(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

The boards unit owns directly, in designation order, never a nested unit's.

The boards of boards whose item.unit is unit; the one test of a unit's own boards.

items.title: unit_boundary_pins
items.text:
def unit_boundary_pins(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None) -> tuple[Id[Port], ...]

The ports of unit's boundary functions: functions in Id order, pins in pin order.

items.title: unit_cables
items.text:
def unit_cables(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> tuple[HarnessCable, ...]

Every cable item that belongs to unit itself, as HarnessCable.

Cables whose own Item.unit is unit, not a nested unit's, read unit-relative: an end outside a NESTED unit has designation == "".

Args: model: The frozen model to read. unit: The unit whose own cables to list.

Returns: Every cable whose Item.unit is unit, sorted by (designation, id).

Raises: SchemaError: unit is not a unit, or a cable or core end has no designation.

items.title: unit_chain
items.text:
def unit_chain(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> list[Id[Unit]]

unit, its parent, its parent's parent, ... up to the top-level ancestor.

Cycle-safe: a repeat ends the walk (UNIT_CYCLE is the validator's, not this query's).

items.title: unit_chain_below
items.text:
def unit_chain_below(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None, subject: Id[Unit]) -> list[Id[Unit]]

subject and its parents up to, not including, unit; None goes to the top.

items.title: unit_connector_items
items.text:
def unit_connector_items(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

The connector_items unit owns directly, never a nested unit's (as unit_boards).

items.title: unit_ids
items.text:
def unit_ids(model: Model) -> tuple[Id[Unit], ...]

Every unit id, sorted.

items.title: unit_index
items.text:
def unit_index(model: Model) -> UnitIndex

The UnitIndex of model, built once per digest and kept for the last few models.

Every field holds ids only and is immutable, so a caller may keep or share it freely.

items.title: unit_items
items.text:
def unit_items(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> frozenset[Id[Item]]

Every item of model whose unit is in unit_subtree(model, unit).

Reads the per-model unit index.

Raises: SchemaError: unit is not a unit of model.

items.title: unit_key
items.text:
def unit_key(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> tuple[str, ...]

The authoring key of unit.

items.title: unit_location
items.text:
def unit_location(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> Id[AspectNode] | None

The location node unit is placed at: its root items' location, else their common ancestor.

The roots are unit_own_roots (external items left out), each read at its effective_placement in the location aspect. One location for all of them is that node; several are their nearest common ancestor in the location tree; None when no root is placed or the roots' locations share no ancestor. The context every list of a unit document prints its ends against.

items.title: unit_matrix
items.text:
def unit_matrix(model: Model) -> UnitMatrix

Every system-level box against every other, with the cables.

The axis is the system level's boxes in box text order, less every unit's field devices (field_devices). A cell has row < col and counts the distinct cables whose lines join those two boxes; a pair with no cable has no cell. The counts come from the same lines the system level draws, so the matrix cannot disagree.

items.title: unit_name_unresolved
items.text:
def unit_name_unresolved(model: Model, name: str) -> str

The one sentence for a unit_name that does not resolve to exactly one unit.

Called only when units_named(model, name) is not exactly one match. Three cases, each ending with the same advice: no release has name (says so and names the release names the model does have, or that it has none); releases of name exist but no instance is in the model (names their versions and revisions); several instances match (names each, with its release's version and revision and, if it has a parent, where it sits).

Example: unit_name_unresolved(model, "relay-board") with no such release returns "no unit release is named 'relay-board'; the model has 'io-board'. Build the unit alone, or pass the instance's scope."

Raises: ValueError: name has exactly one matching unit; there is nothing to report.

items.title: unit_own_drawing
items.text:
def unit_own_drawing(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> str

The drawing set of a unit's own panel line: its box text, then "in" and its release.

items.title: unit_owned_ids
items.text:
def unit_owned_ids(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> frozenset[Id[Record]]

Every id unit owns: its subtree's items, functions, ports, units and its documents.

items.title: unit_racks
items.text:
def unit_racks(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit] | None) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

The racks (plc_racks) of unit, id-sorted; every rack for unit=None.

items.title: unit_release
items.text:
def unit_release(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> UnitRelease

The UnitRelease record unit is an instance of, the one reader of its release facts.

Raises: SchemaError: unit names no Unit of model.

items.title: unit_releases
items.text:
def unit_releases(model: Model) -> frozendict[Id[UnitRelease], UnitRelease]

Return every UnitRelease in model, by id.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every UnitRelease in model, keyed by id; the model's own table, so nothing is copied. Empty when the model holds none.

items.title: unit_strips
items.text:
def unit_strips(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

The terminal strips unit owns directly, in designation order, never a nested unit's.

The strips of terminal_strips whose item.unit is unit; one test of a unit's own strips.

items.title: unit_subtree
items.text:
def unit_subtree(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> frozenset[Id[Unit]]

unit and every unit whose parent chain reaches it.

Cycle-safe, like derive.structure.subtree. Reads the per-model unit index.

Raises: SchemaError: unit is not a unit of model.

items.title: unit_system_designation
items.text:
def unit_system_designation(model: Model, unit: Id[Unit]) -> str | None

The unit named from the system level, tags joined (-R1-A2); None when untagged.

items.title: units
items.text:
def units(model: Model) -> frozendict[Id[Unit], Unit]

Return every Unit in model, by id.

Args: model: The model to read.

Returns: Every Unit in model, keyed by id; the model's own table, so nothing is copied. Empty when the model holds none.

items.title: units_named
items.text:
def units_named(model: Model, name: str) -> tuple[Id[Unit], ...]

The ids of every Unit instance of a release named name, in id order.

Every version and revision of that name counts; an id order that does not depend on hash order (the tie-break).

Example: two UnitReleases named "relay-board" (1.1 and 1.2), one Unit instance of each: units_named(model, "relay-board") returns both ids, sorted.

items.title: unused_terminals
items.text:
def unused_terminals(model: Model, strip: Id[Item]) -> tuple[Id[Item], ...]

Terminal children of strip with no conductor on any port, sorted by id.

Args: model: The model to read. strip: The terminal strip item whose unused terminals are listed.

Returns: Every unused terminal child's id, sorted.

Raises: SchemaError: strip is not an item of model.

items.title: view_lookup
items.text:
def view_lookup(model: Model, rows: ViewRows) -> dict[RefKey, int]

Each drawn box's index by its reference; a place box also by each member it holds.

items.title: wire_rows
items.text:
def wire_rows(model: Model, *, unit: Id[Unit] | None=None, context: Id[AspectNode] | None=None) -> tuple[WireRow, ...]

One WireRow per wire-faceted WIRE conductor no harness carries, by (from, to, id).

A jumper, a cable core, a link and a harness wire never get a row. from/to are the ends as the list prints them (unit and context act the same); label is wire_text.

items.title: Aspect
items.text:
class Aspect

One of the three IEC 81346 views of the same objects.

Example: -K1 is a PRODUCT designation; +C1 is a LOCATION node.

items.title: AspectNode
items.text:
class AspectNode

A node in one IEC 81346 aspect tree.

Example: +C1 is a LOCATION node with label="C1"; a PRODUCT tree node -K1 groups the relay example under an enclosure. Guarded by validators.structure (ASPECT_CYCLE, ASPECT_CROSS_PARENT).

items.title: AssignedSeed
items.text:
class AssignedSeed

An unauthored item a pin still matches and the pin's text for it; key is the item's.

items.title: BoardNetlist
items.text:
class BoardNetlist

A board's parts, footprints and nets: one more Fransys output.

without_footprint are the board's descendants with a part whose part carries no footprint: the parts a netlist cannot place, which the query omits from parts. An accessory, which prints its holder's designation, is no part of its own and is never listed.

items.title: BoardPins
items.text:
class BoardPins

A board's nets with every pin resolved, and the pins of its parts that are in no net.

items.title: BomLine
items.text:
class BomLine

One BOM line, by Part, installed non-external items only; or one nested unit.

mpn/manufacturer/description are Part's own fields, projected here so a formatter never looks the part back up. A unit line has part=None, the unit's name in mpn, an empty manufacturer, and its own revision, printed as revision_text ("1.1"); revision is "" on every part line. A unit line's designations are per instance: its one root item's designation, else its location ("+C1"), else its root items' (bom_lines). Every designation a line prints carries its sign ("-K1", "-U2", "-X1:L1:1", "+C1").

items.title: Boundary
items.text:
class Boundary

A function that is part of a unit's interface.

Example: u.boundary(x1) in io_board makes connector X1 the board's interface. One function may be the boundary of several units, for a board connector that is also its cabinet's external connector.

name is the NamedTuple field name the unit's interface gave this function, or None; it is for the box's name line.

items.title: BoxPair
items.text:
class BoxPair

One function and the one function of another item it is wired to, pin to pin.

Attributes: function: The function the pairing is read for. partner: The function of another item that every port of function reaches. port_pairs: (port of function, port of partner), in the order of function's ports.

items.title: BridgePiece
items.text:
class BridgePiece

One drawn Bridge mark piece (bridge_piece_key): its SVG and its size in mm.

The SVG is width_mm by height_mm; pdf places it in a row's cell and, for a lane's line only, stretches it on y to the rows the lane covers.

items.title: CableBlockRef
items.text:
class CableBlockRef

One cable block of a run: its svgs key, its run's part number and that run's part line.

items.title: CableBlockSize
items.text:
class CableBlockSize

A laid-out cable block's width and height in G, and the module_mm of its sheet.

items.title: CableListRow
items.text:
class CableListRow

One top-level cable of the system document's cable list.

mpn, description, core_count, gauge_mm2 and length_mm are HarnessCable's own facts, None where the part or facet is absent. designation is the cable's printed_designation ("-W1"). Ends are ordered by cable_end_rank (a unit member first), so a cable authored either way round reads the same way round. from_label is the first end's HarnessEnd.designation, the text the drawing prints. to_label lists every other end's designation in that order, joined by ", ". With one end to_label is "", with none both are. pairs is the number of twisted pairs of the product, None for a product with none.

items.title: CableRow
items.text:
class CableRow

One core of one cable, both ends.

items.title: CableRun
items.text:
class CableRun

One part run: its heading (the part number, or NO_PART) and its blocks in their order.

items.title: CdpRackModule
items.text:
class CdpRackModule

A channel-bearing rack module with what CDP's module name is made of.

ordinal counts the channel-bearing modules of the same mpn, in rack order, from 0. single_signal is the one SignalType all its channels share, None when they differ.

items.title: ChannelScaling
items.text:
class ChannelScaling

The scaling facet of a field device, projected so a formatter never looks it up.

items.title: Conductor
items.text:
class Conductor

Realisation: an exactly-two-ended physical connection.

Example: one core of the invented cable W012 example is a Conductor(kind=CORE, carrier=<the cable item>) between a transmitter's port and a terminal's EXTERNAL port. a/b are stored in id order; direction is not a fact.

Net membership lives only in Net.ports: a conductor carries no net of its own. Guarded by validators.connectivity and validators.cables.

items.title: ConductorKind
items.text:
class ConductorKind

What physical realisation a Conductor is.

Example: a panel wire is WIRE; one core of the invented cable W012 example is CORE; a bridge between two terminals is JUMPER. JUMPER, MOUNT, BUSBAR, RAIL and LEAD are links: a bridge between terminals, plug-on contacts, a rack's power jumper, terminals bonded through their rail, a device's own lead ending in a pin of a fitted connector. A link joins its net and is never a wire: it has no WireFacet.

items.title: ConnectorPin
items.text:
class ConnectorPin

One pin of a board connector, the net on it and the pin it mates with.

marking is the port's name. net is the name of the declared net that lists the port, named as board_netlist names its nets; None when no declared net lists it. The mate's pin is the port of equal name on the mated function (a Mate carries no pin map). ends are the far ends of every conductor on the pin or its mate, as far_ends prints them.

items.title: ConnectorRow
items.text:
class ConnectorRow

One connector of a board, as listed by connector_rows.

designation and mate_designation are connector_designation: the connector's own item's designation, plus -<label> when that item carries two or more labelled connector functions (-JB1-J1; a device's connectors print as sub-parts); an item with one never shows it. style, pincount and gender are the connector facet of the function's template, projected here so a formatter never looks them up; gender is None when the part file states none. mate is the connector plugged into this one, None when unmated.

items.title: ContentsRow
items.text:
class ContentsRow

One cable of a document's CONTENTS page.

mpn, description, core_count, gauge_mm2 and length_mm are HarnessCable's own facts, as in CableListRow. designation is the cable's printed_designation ("-W1"). ends is every end's designation in the cable's end order, joined by an en dash, a blank end (outside a nested unit) dropped with its dash; unlike CableListRow it keeps every end. It is text, not a tuple, so cell_text cannot join it with CELL_SEPARATOR.

items.title: CoreListRow
items.text:
class CoreListRow

One line of the core list: a core with its ends, its pair word and its spare mark.

Every text is a field of a CableRow or an OpenCoreRow or core_pair_word; "" is none.

items.title: CurrentBound
items.text:
class CurrentBound

The most continuous current of kind that reaches a position: value, set by by.

states names the items the bound depends on: among the item assignments that give this same bound (value, setter and role), the (item, rest or operated) of each enumerated item that is in the same state in ALL of them (current_states), sorted by item id. An item that varies between such assignments does not matter and is not named; empty when none does. ports are the two end ports of the position whose limit set the bound.

items.title: CurrentChain
items.text:
class CurrentChain

The positions of one block of the current graph, in the order derive.current_chains gives.

The graph has every switched link closed. A position it shorts, but that exists in some state, is a chain alone.

items.title: CurrentPosition
items.text:
class CurrentPosition

One rated current path: the functions it passes through, sorted, and its bounds.

bounds holds at most one CurrentBound per current kind, AC before DC: the highest, over the item states in which the position exists and has one, of the smallest limit the law lets reach it, with the function that set it and the item states that give it. ports are the position's two end ports, its identity when equal functions repeat (one per pole).

items.title: DesignationMove
items.text:
class DesignationMove

One pin source entry still matched by a current item: its OLD and CURRENT own label.

items.title: DesignationRow
items.text:
class DesignationRow

One line of the tag/designation list (designation_list).

items.title: DiffMark
items.text:
class DiffMark

One box or line of a view that a ListingDiff marks, with the status the page prints.

at indexes the view's boxes, or its lines when on_line. status is added or changed.

items.title: DiffRest
items.text:
class DiffRest

One row no box or line of any view carries: its status and the subject text.

items.title: DiffViewMarks
items.text:
class DiffViewMarks

The marks one view takes from a diff: boxes then lines by index, and the rows that marked.

shown holds the indexes in ListingDiff.changes of the rows that marked a box or line.

items.title: DocumentRow
items.text:
class DocumentRow

The fields of one Document an output reads.

location and item are the subject's ids (the SYSTEM preset has neither), cover and notes the Markdown texts (notes is None when dropped) and logo the title block's SVG.

items.title: DocumentScope
items.text:
class DocumentScope

The selections one Document makes, each read once from its subject.

  • unit: document_unit, the unit every reading uses; the SYSTEM preset has none.
  • cables: the HarnessCables the drawings show (SYSTEM: the top-level ones, a unit: its own, an item: its cable children, a location: none); harnesses: the harness items with single wires the drawings add.
  • bom_location, bom_item and bom_top_level make bom_scope, the scope bom_lines takes: the unit, else TOP_LEVEL for the system, else the location, else the item.
  • bom_without: the harness items a location document does not draw, with all they own; bom_lines leaves them out (without=) and connector_items omits them.
  • strips: the terminal strips a terminal list covers; connector_items: the items a connector list covers for a unit or a location; boards: a board document's board.

items.title: DocumentSheets
items.text:
class DocumentSheets

A document's paper, its sizes, its pages' title blocks in page order, each paper's frame.

items.title: ExportRow
items.text:
class ExportRow

One file a write makes, before it is placed in data/.

  • export_kind: "bom", "plc", "wires", "designations", "cables", "cores", "overview", "terminals", "connectors", "wago" or "pdf"; extension ends the name.
  • subject: the strip, board, rack or document id; None for a whole-model report.
  • name: export_name or document_export_name; hint the unit-set name a clash of two units of one release should keep one document of, else None.

items.title: ExtUsage
items.text:
class ExtUsage

One (kind, key) pair still stored in some record's escape-hatch ext field.

Not a Fransys output format: read by whoever maintains this repo to decide what to promote to a real field next, keeping ext honest (kernel-records.md 5.3 and derive-queries-structure.md).

items.title: Extent
items.text:
class Extent

A box in G, in the frame of the symbol's body: top-left x, y and its size.

items.title: FieldFold
items.text:
class FieldFold

One unit's field devices folded into a box beside it: its text, members and cables.

unit is the top-level unit box all their connections land in; cables join them to it, and joins are the lifted lines of the fold to it, one per kind.

items.title: FieldJoin
items.text:
class FieldJoin

One lifted line of a field box to its unit: a kind, its cables and its count.

items.title: FieldOverflow
items.text:
class FieldOverflow

One field whose text missed its cell: the field name and the base text that did not fit.

items.title: FindingHold
items.text:
class FindingHold

One finding that counts on a mark: its index in the findings given, and its severity.

items.title: FindingMark
items.text:
class FindingMark

One box or line of a view that findings name.

at indexes the view's boxes, or its lines when on_line. held lists each finding that counts there, in the order the findings reached it.

items.title: FoldBox
items.text:
class FoldBox

One box of a folded level.

lines is its text. A GROUP counts its items, nested units and strips, and inner_lines, the connections between its own boxes. STRIPS counts the strips it holds. item_kind is an item box's kind, terminals a strip box's or STRIPS' terminal count.

items.title: FoldLevel
items.text:
class FoldLevel

A unit level folded to function groups, or one group or the strips box opened.

opened is the GROUP or STRIPS box opened as the level, None for the folded level and for a unit with fewer than two groups, which opens straight (folded false) with all its boxes. strips lists each strip the level holds or passes through, in designation order. wires is, for the strip opened in it, each terminal's share of the stubs its terminals hold together; empty with no strip open.

items.title: FoldLine
items.text:
class FoldLine

One line of a folded level, per pair of boxes and kind, or per strip passed through.

count is the connections it stands for, vias the cable items of a cable line. A line drawn through a strip has strip set, terminals the terminals it stands for and label as -X3 x 3; otherwise label joins the cable designations, "" for none.

items.title: FoldStub
items.text:
class FoldStub

The outside end of connections at a box, folded by far end.

far names the group, box, unit or location, or for END the far device as stub_far_end prints it; end is the same far end as a reference (a group, a box's own, a unit, a place or the far item). kind and via are the line's: a stub folds per kind, and via is set only for END. count is the connections. members are the single stubs it opens to: those of an outside fold, the stub itself for END, empty inside the unit.

items.title: Footprints
items.text:
class Footprints

The room a symbol takes: standalone, and in_strip_row without the strip's shared tag.

items.title: FrameLabels
items.text:
class FrameLabels

The reference labels of a frame: column numbers left to right, row letters top down.

items.title: FrameStrip
items.text:
class FrameStrip

One reference strip of a sheet frame in mm: its corner, one cell's size and its labels.

side is top, bottom, left or right; the cells run along axis, one per label.

items.title: Function
items.text:
class Function

One electrical function of one item: the unit Fransys draws as a symbol.

Example: the relay -K1 example has a coil Function drawn on the control page and a co_1 Function drawn on the power page; both reference the same item. Guarded by part_conformance when template is set.

items.title: FunctionKind
items.text:
class FunctionKind

What kind of Function an item exposes.

Example: the relay -K1 example has one COIL function and CONTACT_NO/ CONTACT_CO functions for its contacts. A BAR is a conductor bar sold as one product.

items.title: HarnessCable
items.text:
class HarnessCable

One cable of a harness with its product facts, cores and ends.

mpn and description are the cable Part's; core_count, gauge_mm2 and shielded are its cable_product facet; length_mm is the item's cable facet. Each is None where the part or the facet is absent. designation is the cable's printed_designation ("-W1"), the text the drawing's cable node title prints. open_cores are the cable's spares and one-ended screens (open_core_rows), which have no conductor and so are not in cores.

items.title: HarnessCore
items.text:
class HarnessCore

One core of a harness cable: the facts of a CableRow, plus the label its wire carries.

label is the label of the wire facet of the core's conductor, None when it has none. end_a/end_b are CableRow's own -- cable_rows itself orients every core of one cable to run from its one lower-ranked end to its one higher-ranked end (cable_end_rank, a unit member first; cable_end_owner), not Conductor.a/.b's raw port-id order, so end_a is always the same physical end for every core that lands on it.

items.title: HarnessEnd
items.text:
class HarnessEnd

One item a core lands on: a connector housing, a plain device, or a strip of terminals.

A core that lands on a terminal with a parent lands on that terminal's strip instead: item is the strip and pins holds one HarnessPin per landed terminal port, marked by the terminal's own bare designation ("L1:1", not dashed or strip-prefixed here) rather than a raw port name. designation is the item's product_designation for every end: a strip, a connector plug or a plain device alike, e.g. "-X1" unplaced, "+C1-X1" or "+EXT-M1" placed, never with a function segment; the same text the terminal list prints and the cable list's from_label/to_label repeat. The connector fields (connector, style, pincount, gender) are filled from the connector facet of a connector function of the item that a core lands on, and are None for a plain device or a strip alike (a strip is never itself a connector-kind function). Any other end -- a connector or a plain device -- has item the device itself and pins one per landed port, marked by the port's own name.

items.title: HarnessLineEnd
items.text:
class HarnessLineEnd

One end of a harness or cable line: plug is its connector function, else ports fan out.

branch is the 1-based n of -W13.n. mates is the function d.mate joins plug to, or None for a fan-out or an unmated plug.

items.title: HarnessPin
items.text:
class HarnessPin

One port of a harness cable's end that a core of that cable lands on.

marking is the port's own name, except for a port of a terminal with a parent (its end is grouped by strip): there it is the terminal's own bare group:index designation ("L1:1"), never dashed or strip-prefixed -- the end's own designation already names the strip, dashed (product_designation), and every consumer that draws a pin next to its end joins the two itself, so a dashed, strip-prefixed marking here would print the strip twice.

items.title: Indexes
items.text:
class Indexes

Every lookup table derive needs more than once, built together off one Model.

Each maps a record to the ids that refer to it, in Id order; a record nothing refers to has no entry, so read one with .get(key, ()). facets_by_subject holds facets of every kind, found through the subject field their kind declared.

Not a @value: it is never nested in a record, and its tables are keyed by Id, outside the closed set @value enforces.

Never stored in the model: call build_indexes again, or rely on its per-digest cache, rather than threading an Indexes value through a pass.

items.title: Item
items.text:
class Item

One physical thing.

Example: the invented relay -K1 example is one Item with part set to the relay Part; terminal strip X03 is an Item whose four terminals are child Items via parent. position is the physical order within the parent (PLC slot, place on the rail); it is a fact about the build, not a drawing coordinate. tag is the engineer's authored tag; tag=None means "number me". The numbered text lives in facet.assigned_designation, never here. installed=False keeps it in drawings and reservations but drops it from the BOM. unit is the unit this item belongs to by membership, not by key or location; None is the integrating script's own wiring. external=True: someone else supplies and owns it; an item is external if it or any parent-chain ancestor is, see derive.external. Guarded by part_conformance (when part is set) and validators.structure (CONTAINMENT_CYCLE).

items.title: ItemKind
items.text:
class ItemKind

What an item is, as the overview colours and filters it.

One value per item. TERMINAL is a strip's terminal, STRIP the item holding terminals. DEVICE is everything the other eight do not name.

items.title: ItemPage
items.text:
class ItemPage

One drawing page that shows an item: the PDF, the page's destination and its text.

items.title: JumperLane
items.text:
class JumperLane

One jumper group's row span and its lane; first and last are 0-based row indexes.

items.title: JumperLanes
items.text:
class JumperLanes

Every jumper group's lane, in group-number order.

items.title: KeepWhole
items.text:
class KeepWhole

Each set is drawn together; sets are sorted, so the order is stable.

items.title: LensChannel
items.text:
class LensChannel

One channel of a PLC module for the Signals lens: its signal kind and field device.

The device fields are None for a spare channel.

items.title: LensModule
items.text:
class LensModule

One PLC module of the Signals lens with its channels in channel order.

items.title: LimitRole
items.text:
class LimitRole

What set a bound: a source's continuous limit, or a full-range protective device.

items.title: LineRef
items.text:
class LineRef

The identity of a line on a level: its two boxes in text order, its kind and its carrier.

A box is a unit instance or an item id. via is the cable item of a cable line, else None.

items.title: LineTab
items.text:
class LineTab

The tab text at each end of one cable line, on the box border; None for none.

items.title: LoadLimit
items.text:
class LoadLimit

One load edge's draw and the limit that bounds it.

port is the star edge's port, None for a two-port load or a load that is already a position.

items.title: LocationBox
items.text:
class LocationBox

One top place of the location fold: its text and the system boxes in it.

place is the top location node, None for the boxes in no place.

items.title: LocationFold
items.text:
class LocationFold

The system level folded by top place; present only with two or more top places.

items.title: LocationLine
items.text:
class LocationLine

The cables between two places: count distinct cables, a before b in box order.

items.title: MateRow
items.text:
class MateRow

One Mate of the model, at any level: its two CONNECTOR or TERMINAL functions, with texts.

a and b keep the authored order of d.mate. A designation is the text the connector list prints for that connector at system level (connector_designation).

items.title: MatrixCell
items.text:
class MatrixCell

The cables between two boxes of the matrix: row before col on the axis.

row and col index UnitMatrix.axis; count is the number of distinct cables.

items.title: Net
items.text:
class Net

Declared intent: a set of ports that are one potential or one signal.

Example: a 24V supply net names the PSU + port and every load's supply port. N-ary; ports is a set, stored sorted by id. potential names the rail this net is ("L1", "24V", "0V", "PE"); None is an ordinary net. It is a fact about the plant, read by wire-colour rules and ladder discovery.

Guarded by validators.connectivity (NET_UNREALISED, NET_SHORTED, NET_POTENTIAL_CONFLICT).

items.title: NetClass
items.text:
class NetClass

What kind of potential or signal a Net carries.

Example: a 24V supply rail is POWER; a 4-20mA transmitter loop is SIGNAL.

items.title: NetlistNet
items.text:
class NetlistNet

One net of a board_netlist, by the pins it joins.

items.title: NetlistPart
items.text:
class NetlistPart

One placed part on a board_netlist (connectivity.md: the board's netlist replaces SKiDL).

installed is the item's own flag: a part not installed stays listed, and the output decides what to do with it.

items.title: NetlistPin
items.text:
class NetlistPin

One pin: its port and item by id, the component reference and the pad name.

items.title: OffDocumentReference
items.text:
class OffDocumentReference

A printed reference to a page of another document that its text does not name.

subject is the label or link marker, page the page it stands on, target the page it names.

items.title: OpenCoreRow
items.text:
class OpenCoreRow

One open core of one cable: the facts of a CableRow, with at most one end.

at is the port the one end lands on, None when it lands nowhere; at_designation is its printed designation, "" for none. spare is false for a screen (an SH core), true for any other open core.

items.title: Operating
items.text:
class Operating

What a function needs to run and what it is allowed to see; a field is None if unknown.

Example: Operating(nominal_voltage_v=Decimal("24"), min_voltage_v=Decimal("18"), max_voltage_v=Decimal("30")) is a 24 V DC input that works from 18 V to 30 V; capacity_ah is set on a battery only. voltage_ac_v and voltage_dc_v are the supply the function is built for, nominal_voltage_v the value it is specified at, and min_voltage_v/max_voltage_v the window it operates in. The model guarantees the types only. max_current_ac_a and max_current_dc_a are a source's continuous current limit, the most that flows through it in either direction, charging included; they bound the branch the source sits on. resistance_ohm, nominal_power_w and nominal_current_a are each stated at nominal_voltage_v; only nominal_current_a, a load's draw, is read. fault_current_ac_a and fault_current_dc_a are a source's prospective current into a bolted fault, fault_time_constant_ms the DC time constant.

items.title: OverviewBox
items.text:
class OverviewBox

One box of a level: a nested unit, a folded strip or an item.

box is a unit instance or an item id; kind is the item's kind, None for a unit. lines is the box text as the block diagram prints it, tabs the boundary or connector designations that stand on its border. terminals is a strip's terminal count, else 0. group and location are the item's effective function and location nodes.

items.title: OverviewGraph
items.text:
class OverviewGraph

Everything the overview output draws: the items, how they connect, the signals.

items.title: OverviewLevel
items.text:
class OverviewLevel

One level of the overview: the system (unit=None) or an opened unit.

items.title: OverviewLine
items.text:
class OverviewLine

One line of a level, lifted from the connections it stands for.

count is those connections: conductors, or mates for a mate line. label is the carrier's designation, "" for none. conductors is empty for a mate line.

items.title: OverviewLink
items.text:
class OverviewLink

The connections between two items of one kind and one carrier, aggregated.

a and b are the two items, the smaller id first. via is the cable item of a CABLE link, None otherwise; via_designation is that cable's printed_designation ("-W1"), None when there is no via or the cable has no designation yet. count is the number of conductors, or of mates for a MATE link; conductors are those conductors in id order, empty for a MATE link.

items.title: OverviewLinkKind
items.text:
class OverviewLinkKind

How two items are connected in the overview: the closed set of kinds.

WIRE is a conductor with no carrier, CABLE a conductor carried by a cable item, MATE a Mate between functions of the two items.

items.title: OverviewNode
items.text:
class OverviewNode

One item of the overview graph.

designation is None for an item that has none yet: overview_graph is the one query that tolerates it, so an overview of a half-finished design still draws. Otherwise it is printed_designation, behind its sign ("-K1", "-X1:L1:1"), as a list prints it.

items.title: OverviewPort
items.text:
class OverviewPort

One port of a signal: its item, the port and its marking (the port's name).

items.title: OverviewSignal
items.text:
class OverviewSignal

One physical net that spans at least two items, for tracing a signal through the overview.

items.title: OverviewStub
items.text:
class OverviewStub

The outside end of connections leaving an opened unit, read as the schematic's stub is.

box is the visible box inside the level. far is the far device's designation and ports its port tails (stub_far_end); end is its root item, count the connections it stands for.

items.title: PageWires
items.text:
class PageWires

The routes of one page: their bends and their total length_mm.

items.title: PartFunctionRow
items.text:
class PartFunctionRow

One function a part declares, with the rating it has.

A part with no function template has one row: template is None, name is "", kind is None, and rating is the part's own. Otherwise rating is effective_rating: the template's, else the part's.

items.title: PhysicalNet
items.text:
class PhysicalNet

One physical net: a maximal set of ports joined by real connectivity.

Distinct from vocab.connectivity.Net, which is declared intent. ports is sorted by id, so two closures over the same physical wiring compare equal regardless of which port the union-find happened to visit first.

Attributes: ports: The net's ports, sorted by id.

items.title: PinNet
items.text:
class PinNet

One net of a board, by the resolved pins it joins.

items.title: PinPosition
items.text:
class PinPosition

A unit's item or instance by structure alone: (key, scope, code), no text yet.

items.title: Placement
items.text:
class Placement

An item occupying an aspect node; at most one per item per aspect.

Example: the relay example's Item is placed at product node -K1 and location node +C1 (two Placements, different aspects). Guarded by validators.structure (PLACEMENT_DUPLICATE).

items.title: PlcChannelRow
items.text:
class PlcChannelRow

One pin of a PLC channel.

pin is its printed designation (-A2:5), channel_name the channel's own number, wired_to the printed far ends at that port joined with CELL_SEPARATOR (None for none). The device fields and signal_name are None for an unbound channel.

items.title: PlcRackChannel
items.text:
class PlcRackChannel

One channel of a rack module, bound or spare.

The field fields are None for a spare channel, as in PlcChannelRow; scaling is also None for a bound device that carries no scaling facet. name_stem is the text an output names the channel after, before its own character set: the field device and its signal name, else the module's designation and the channel's index in the module.

items.title: PlcRackModule
items.text:
class PlcRackModule

One PLC module of a rack with its channels, for an output that walks the rack in order.

mpn and description are the Part's, projected as BomLine does. position is the item's own position, None when it was never authored.

items.title: PlcTable
items.text:
class PlcTable

One table of the PLC list: the channels of one controller or module.

item carries the channels, designation is its printed designation, the table's heading; rows are its PlcChannelRows in list order, never empty.

items.title: Port
items.text:
class Port

A connection point on a Function.

Example: the coil Function of the relay example has ports A1 and A2. Guarded by part_conformance when template is set. marking is the part's own pin marking: None means "print the port's name", "" means "print nothing", any other string is printed as given. source_row is the part's stated wiring row for the pin, copied from its template, or None.

items.title: PortRole
items.text:
class PortRole

What a Port is for.

Example: a terminal's two ports are INTERNAL (panel wiring side) and EXTERNAL (field cable side); which side a wire lands on is this role, not a drawing side. A CONTACT_CO function's ports are COMMON, BREAK (the throw it closes at rest) or MAKE (the throw it closes operated), whatever the part's pin names.

items.title: PowerKind
items.text:
class PowerKind

What a physical net is on the drawing: a supply, ground, protective earth or none.

Example: a declared 24 V DC rail is SUPPLY, its 0 V rail GROUND, a net of class PE is PE, an AC rail or a net in no supply is NONE.

items.title: ProspectiveFault
items.text:
class ProspectiveFault

The prospective fault current of kind at one protective position.

current_a is the largest current a bolted fault at either terminal drives through it, over the item states: None when a source counted states none, 0 when no source is counted. Cable resistance is ignored and parallel runs add, so it errs high; an undeclared feed counts as no source. time_constant_ms is the largest DC time constant of the sources counted, over the states: None for AC, or when a counted source states none. functions and supplies are the source functions and the declared supplies counted, sorted.

items.title: Rating
items.text:
class Rating

What a function or a part is rated for; a field is None when the datasheet says nothing.

Example: Rating(voltage_ac_v=Decimal("250"), current_ac_a=Decimal("0.5")) is a contact rated 250 V AC and 0.5 A AC, with no DC rating. Voltages are RMS for AC and the highest permissible potential for DC; currents are the continuous rating, except min_breaking_current_a, the lowest current a partial-range fuse breaks. The model guarantees the types only; comparing a rating with what the plant does is a check's job.

items.title: ReadabilityPage
items.text:
class ReadabilityPage

What fr.readability measures of one schematic page.

drawing_set and number are as printed. text_height_mm is the profile's capital height of text and min_text_height_mm its floor. fill_percent is the share of the content box the drawn content covers, in whole percent. The four counts are the lint findings' own: wire_crossings (two wires of different conductors crossing), struck_labels (WIRE_OVER_LABEL), text_overlaps (TEXT_OVERLAP) and lone_cells (LONE_CELL). The references drawn on the page: contact images with the contacts they list, stars with the branches they name, and page cuts, which name one other page each. single_* counts the images with one contact and the stars with one branch; single_contact_images_other_page counts the single images whose contact is on another page. wire_bends and wire_length_mm read the page's routes. A loose symbol has no page. contacts_not_drawn counts image entries that print N/A; references_off_document counts references to another document that name none.

items.title: ReadabilityReport
items.text:
class ReadabilityReport

What fr.readability returns: a row for each schematic page, and for each unit.

loose_symbols counts the symbols of the whole build that no page draws.

items.title: ReadabilityUnit
items.text:
class ReadabilityUnit

One unit's pages together: counts add up, text_height_mm and fill_percent are the lowest.

unit is None for the design's own pages. min_text_height_mm is the highest floor of them. loose_symbols is the count of the unit's own loose symbols.

items.title: ReplicaOnlySet
items.text:
class ReplicaOnlySet

A drawing set dropped as holding only black-box replicas: its id and its location.

items.title: RevisionRow
items.text:
class RevisionRow

One revision-history entry, as the revision table prints it.

items.title: SeedRows
items.text:
class SeedRows

What a pin source seeds into one unit: assigned items, assigned instances, reserved texts.

reserved holds every pin gone or moved, plus the source's own retired.

items.title: SheetBackground
items.text:
class SheetBackground

One page background and the two boxes pdf fills, in mm from the page corner.

svg is the frame, grid and title block; counter_box and logo_box are x, y, width and height of the Page cell's value and of the logo cell, None when the band holds no title block; title_room_mm is the width a page title is cut to.

items.title: SheetFrame
items.text:
class SheetFrame

A sheet's frame in mm from the page corner: border, reference strips and title-block band.

border is x, y, width and height. The band is band high from band_top; the title block is title_width wide from the border's left, and the square logo cell starts at logo_x.

items.title: SheetGroup
items.text:
class SheetGroup

One sheet format a document's drawn pages name: its name and its pages' numbers.

items.title: SheetIndexRow
items.text:
class SheetIndexRow

One index row: the sheet text (3, 2.3, B1), its title forms and its destination label.

title is the longest form and shorter the others (page_title_forms): the PDF prints the first that fits, as the title block does. The page cell is not here: Typst reads the physical page at destination.

items.title: SheetKey
items.text:
class SheetKey

One page background's place: the document, the page kind and the page's ordinal in it.

ordinal is None for a document's no-drawings fallback page.

items.title: SheetPage
items.text:
class SheetPage

One page background: its key, paper and title-block fields (render draws it, pdf places it).

group and where name the page in a TITLE_BLOCK_TEXT_OVERFLOW message; group is "" for a page whose page-level fields are not checked (a diagram sheet, a no-drawings page).

items.title: SheetRow
items.text:
class SheetRow

A sheet's paper and content box in mm, and its grid module_mm: what a page is set on.

items.title: SidelessPins
items.text:
class SidelessPins

Both ends' pins in pin order, and problem, the text of why they cannot pair, else None.

Does not pick a port: the caller maps each template back to its own port.

items.title: SignalKind
items.text:
class SignalKind

The form and direction of a PLC signal.

items.title: Sizes
items.text:
class Sizes

The four roles' font sizes in mm, for one document's profile text_height_mm.

title_band_mm is the title-block band at which a label and its value clear each other.

items.title: StripNote
items.text:
class StripNote

A strip beside a level: terminals of it held (a box) or passed through (lines).

items.title: StripTerminal
items.text:
class StripTerminal

One terminal of an open strip, with its lines to the level's visible boxes.

items.title: StripView
items.text:
class StripView

An open strip: its terminals in strip order (group, then index).

items.title: StubBox
items.text:
class StubBox

The stub box of one far end end at the box at: its text lines.

by_others is set when end is an item that is by others: the box is dashed and its first line ends (by others), as the system level prints it.

items.title: StubLine
items.text:
class StubLine

The line from at to the stub box of end, for one kind and carrier, with its text.

items.title: StubPlace
items.text:
class StubPlace

Where a stub's far end lies: a group or box of the unit, a far unit, a location, one end.

items.title: StubWire
items.text:
class StubWire

A terminal's share of a stub it holds with the other terminals of the open strip.

stub is the shared stub, hung on the first terminal wired to its far end; part is the connections of one terminal to it, with box that terminal. Both name the same far end.

items.title: SupplySystem
items.text:
class SupplySystem

A named supply with its rails, a plant fact beside Net.

Example: SupplySystem(name="400V", current=Current.AC, rails=...) holds rails L1, L2, L3 and N, each named as Net.potential names it. Protective earth is not a supplied rail: a rail carried by a PE-class net is earth, at 0 V to earth in every supply. earthing says how the source is earthed. fault_current_a is the supply's prospective current into a bolted fault, fault_time_constant_ms its DC time constant (RATINGS-3 R3). unit is the unit that declares it, as Item.unit is; pins are the ports its call puts its rails on, sorted by id (RATINGS-3 R6). Not a Part, not an Item: it has no designation and no place.

items.title: TerminalRow
items.text:
class TerminalRow

One terminal of a strip's connection list.

An unused terminal has empty internal/external tuples; bridged terminals share one jumper_group number. internal_ends and external_ends are the rendered far-end port designations of those conductors, aligned index for index with internal and external: internal_ends[i] is where internal[i] goes. After those come the open cores landing there (-W1 GY spare), which have no conductor. Given a context location, terminal_rows prints an end outside it with its location path in front (+EXT-M1:U1) and one inside it short (-B12:2/T1).

items.title: TerminalStubs
items.text:
class TerminalStubs

The stubs of one terminal of an open strip: its connections that leave the unit.

items.title: Throws
items.text:
class Throws

One pole of a changeover: its common port and the throws a switched link joins to it.

breaks are the ports the common closes to at rest, makes those it closes to when operated; both sorted by id, so two computations over the same model compare equal. Example: the invented relay's co_1 with 11 common, 12 break and 14 make gives Throws(common=<11>, breaks=(<12>,), makes=(<14>,)).

Attributes: common: The pole's common port. breaks: The ports the common closes to at rest, sorted by id. makes: The ports the common closes to when operated, sorted by id.

items.title: TitleBlockFields
items.text:
class TitleBlockFields

One page's title-block content; sheet_counter "" off SCHEMATIC.

items.title: TitleBlockOverflow
items.text:
class TitleBlockOverflow

One one-line field whose text missed its cell: the field, where it sits and its base text.

items.title: TitleBlockStrings
items.text:
class TitleBlockStrings

What a title block prints, after the cut.

  • printed: slot id (title, number, revision, revision_date, customer, author, page_title, scope, sheet) to the shown text, cut with … when it missed.
  • notice: the notice's wrapped lines, no more than the cell holds.
  • unfit: each field that missed its cell; notice_unfit: the notice needs more lines.

items.title: TopLevelScope
items.text:
class TopLevelScope

The type of TOP_LEVEL: a bom_lines scope distinct from None and every Id[...].

items.title: TreeRow
items.text:
class TreeRow

One row of the parts tree: a unit or an item (the other None), its label.

parent is the index of the row it hangs under, None for a top row. Rows come in display order: units first, then items, strips last.

items.title: Unit
items.text:
class Unit

One instance of a released, independently-built component.

Example: io_board instantiates one Unit per call, all pointing at the one UnitRelease for demo-io-board, so a cabinet holding two boards has two Unit records and one release. release carries the name, version, revision, interface, title and number. parent is the unit this instance sits in; a subtree is the unit and every unit whose parent chain reaches it. Guarded by validators.structure (UNIT_CYCLE). release's own interface is now checked at release (INTERFACE_NOT_BUMPED). tag is the instance's written tag (U1), None to be numbered; derive.unit_tag reads the tag.

items.title: UnitMatrix
items.text:
class UnitMatrix

The system-level boxes against each other: the axis in text order, the pairs with cables.

items.title: UnitRelease
items.text:
class UnitRelease

A released, independently-built component: a product as a part is.

Example: UnitRelease(name="demo-io-board", version=1, revision=3, interface="7", title="Relay interface board", number="SKX-RIB-2") is one record however many Units instantiate it; its instances are placements, as items are. Its key is ("unit_release", name, str(version), str(revision)), so two releases that differ in another field conflict. version and revision are ints of 1 or more (release_version), printed as derive.revision_text (1.3). interface is the boundary's version, bumped by hand and checked at release against every other revision of the name (INTERFACE_NOT_BUMPED). title and number are the unit's own; class_code is the letter its floating instances number from (U); all default to "". Read through derive.unit_release.

items.title: UnitTagSeed
items.text:
class UnitTagSeed

An untagged instance a pin still matches and the pin's text; key is the instance's.

items.title: ViewBox
items.text:
class ViewBox

One box of a view: its key, its text lines and its dash.

members are a fold's member rows, which the page lists when the fold is open; empty for any other box.

items.title: ViewLine
items.text:
class ViewLine

One line of a view: its ends, kind, cable, strip and text; tab_a, tab_b end tabs.

tab_a and tab_b are the texts of the tabs the line ends on at its a and b box, else None.

items.title: ViewMember
items.text:
class ViewMember

One member of a fold: the far end, its text lines and its row text.

It has no position. text is the whole row as a stub label, carrier first (overview_member_text): -W11 → +EXT-M1:PE.

items.title: ViewRows
items.text:
class ViewRows

One view: its level (unit, level), mode, the one open strip, boxes and lines.

Boxes come in the level's text order, then the stub boxes; lines likewise.

items.title: WireRow
items.text:
class WireRow

One wire of the wire list: its two ends, colour, cross-section and printed label.

items.title: build
items.text:
def build(*drafts: Draft | Design, releases: Path | None=None) -> BuildResult

Output: merge, freeze and lay out drafts or a Design into a BuildResult.

Runs PLC allocation, numbering, every validator and layout, collecting each pass's findings. The schematic lays out only when no ERROR was found and a Document keeps a SCHEMATIC page; a layout SymbolPortError becomes one SYMBOL_PORT_MISSING ERROR. releases seeds numbering pins from that release root; None numbers freely. Raises FreezeError on a structural problem in the merged draft.

Does not write files, run check or raise on findings; does not seed pins when releases is None.

items.title: check
items.text:
def check(result: BuildResult) -> tuple[Finding, ...]

Output: collect every finding about a built model.

They are build's, plus the KiCad, PDF and render checks.

Findings come back ordered ERROR, WARNING, INFO, then by (code, subjects, message), each message already run through describe so subjects read file:line (key). The PDF and render checks run only on a laid-out model (no ERROR, at least one Document); the KiCad check always runs.

Does not raise on findings, write files or draw a page for a model that was never laid out.

items.title: design
items.text:
def design(*libraries: str | ModuleType, place: str | None=None, wiring: Mapping[WiringRow, RowValue] | None=None) -> Design

Core: start a Design from part libraries or generated parts modules.

Each library is checked fresh.

place names the first location, as a bare tag. wiring maps rows (fr.DC_SUPPLY, ...) to a colour or a (colour, size): it replaces those IEC 60204-1 default rows for the design.

Does not write files, build, or create devices.

items.title: diff
items.text:
def diff(result: BuildResult, baselines: Path, *, unit: object=None, against: str | None=None) -> str

Output: return the Markdown change list from a stored release to the model as it stands now.

By default a is the release stored at the model's current revision, else the previous released revision; against="1.3" names a sibling <version>.<revision> folder directly. unit resolves as in release. Raises FileNotFoundError when no release is found, TypeError or ValueError for a bad unit.

Does not write files; does not guess a release by likeness.

items.title: document
items.text:
def document(preset: DocumentPreset, subject: object, *, cover: Path, add: tuple[PageKind, ...]=(), remove: tuple[PageKind, ...]=(), logo: Path | None=None, notice: str='') -> Draft

Output: author a document record from a preset, a subject and a cover file.

Returns a Draft.

Reads cover (a missing file raises FileNotFoundError) and the optional <stem>.notes.md beside it (absent: no notes page); logo is an optional SVG for the title block (missing raises); notice is the title block's IP notice text. Texts are stored in the record. subject is what d.location(...) returns, a Device, a unit release name (str) or None (the system preset only); any other value raises TypeError. Key: the cover stem, preset and subject, so documents may share a cover path.

Does not build, render or read files at render time; has no notes argument.

items.title: export_names
items.text:
def export_names(result: BuildResult, *, unit: object=None) -> dict[tuple[str, Id[Any] | None], str]

Read: the path from out_dir that write gives each export of result, by (kind, subject).

A kind is "bom", "plc", "wires", "designations", "overview", "cables" or "cores" (subject None), "terminals", "connectors" or "wago" (the strip, board or rack id), or "pdf" (the document id). unit= is write's. Writes nothing and compiles no PDF; raises what write raises for a bad unit or a name two subjects share (ExportNameClash).

Does not write a file, compile a PDF or run check.

items.title: lint
items.text:
def lint(*libraries: str) -> tuple[Finding, ...]

Read: lint part libraries by import name and return their findings.

Each root resolves as in parts; findings come library by library, in the order given, with the part file and line already in the message. Zero libraries give ().

Does not build a model, load a library into a Draft or raise on findings.

items.title: parts
items.text:
def parts(*packages: str) -> Draft

Detail: load part libraries by import name and merge them into one Draft.

For a draft that holds only parts, to merge beside other drafts. Try fr.design(...) first: it loads its libraries itself.

Each name is an installed part-data package, loaded through fransys_parts.load. Zero names give an empty Draft. Pass the result to build beside other drafts.

Does not build, lint or freeze; does not accept a folder path (use an import name).

items.title: parts_module
items.text:
def parts_module(*sources: str) -> str

Detail: the text of the typed parts module for the libraries sources name.

For typed part classes in your editor. Try fr.design(...) with an MPN string first.

Does not write a file: python -m fransys parts-module does.

items.title: readability
items.text:
def readability(result: BuildResult) -> ReadabilityReport

Read: one row for each schematic page of result, and one for each unit.

A page row counts what a reader of the print feels: the profile's text height against min_text_height_mm, how much of the page the drawing fills, wires crossing wires, text struck by a wire, text overlaps, cells alone on a page, and the references the page makes. A unit row adds its pages up. Pure: the same model gives the same rows. The layout runs again on result.model, as build ran it, so the cost is about that of the layout.

Does not write a file, emit anything from write, or raise on findings.

items.title: rebaseline
items.text:
def rebaseline(result: BuildResult, baselines: Path, *, unit: str | Id[ModelUnit] | None=None) -> tuple[Path, ...]

Output: re-cut every stored baseline the current rules print differently, once.

Rewrites baseline/listing.json and baseline/manifest.json of each release under baselines that verify notes with BASELINE_RULES_MOVED or BASELINE_ROWS_UNCHECKED, children before parents, and returns those folders (() when nothing moved). The manifest keeps the old digest, listing version and fransys in a rebaselined record. unit=None covers every unit and the system with a stored baseline; a unit covers it and the units below. Raises BuildErrors and writes nothing when a real row changed (BASELINE_DIFFERS), a baseline is too old, or a release file is not as released.

Does not write an export, model.json or numbering.json.

items.title: release
items.text:
def release(result: BuildResult, into: Path, *, unit: object=None) -> Path

Output: release a unit, or the system, as a frozen baseline under into.

Writes <into>/<name>/<version>.<revision>/: the unit's exports as write makes them, baseline/ (listing, model, manifest) and, after a first release, changes.md and changes.csv. Runs the same gate as write plus the release checks: any ERROR raises BuildErrors and writes nothing. An identical stored listing text returns the existing path untouched. Files are built in a temporary sibling and renamed, so a failure leaves nothing behind.

Does not release when check finds an ERROR; does not overwrite an identical release.

items.title: releases
items.text:
def releases(root: Path) -> tuple[Release, ...]

Output: every release folder under root, read from its manifest.

They come in name, version, revision order.

root holds <name>/<version>.<revision>/ folders, as fr.release writes them. Versions and revisions sort as integers. A folder with no manifest is listed with empty interface, listing_digest, nested and files. A missing root gives ().

Raises: ValueError: a manifest does not parse or lacks a key; the message names its path.

Does not write files, check a file's hash or read any model.

items.title: report
items.text:
def report(result: BuildResult) -> str

Output: one text of fr.check(result).

It holds a summary line, each ERROR and WARNING, then the notes.

Each ERROR and WARNING prints its message, then an at: line per subject, its fix and its findings-row URL from the code's registry entry. INFO notes print counted per code on one line. The text only reads the findings and their CodeInfo; it adds no rule of its own.

Does not write files, raise on an ERROR, or drop a finding.

items.title: unit
items.text:
def unit(name: str, *, revision: int, interface_version: int | str, date: str, text: str, by: str, version: int=1, title: str='', number: str='', history: Sequence[Mapping[str, str | int]]=(), class_code: str | None=None, wiring: Mapping[WiringRow, RowValue] | None=None) -> Callable[[Callable[..., R]], UnitDef[R]]

Core: make a function the unit release name.

It takes a child design and returns its interface.

The interface is an instance of a typing.NamedTuple class, one field per boundary.

Does not build anything: d.add(fn, "U1") does. history entries take d.revision's keywords. class_code (1-3 uppercase letters) is the letter floating instances number from. wiring replaces IEC rows in the unit's body; a unit never takes its parent's rows.

items.title: verify
items.text:
def verify(result: BuildResult, baselines: Path) -> tuple[Finding, ...]

Output: return one BASELINE_DIFFERS ERROR per unit instance, or the system, that drifted.

Compares the rebuilt listing with the stored one under baselines, for every unit and for the system when the model holds a Project, under the rules of the fransys that cut it: a rule that moved since gives BASELINE_RULES_MOVED (INFO), one too old to know BASELINE_TOO_OLD. The model digest is never compared. Also re-hashes every release file: RELEASE_FILE_CHANGED, RELEASE_FILE_MISSING. Meant for a consumer's test, wherever they want it.

Does not write files, release or gate write; does not report a unit with no stored baseline.

items.title: write
items.text:
def write(result: BuildResult, out_dir: Path, *, unit: object=None, intermediates: Path | None=None, releases: Path | None=None) -> tuple[Path, ...]

Output: write a built model's exports into out_dir and return their paths, sorted.

Writes CSV reports, WAGO XML, overview HTML and one PDF per document; unit= restricts them to that unit's own set (no overview.html). Intermediates (SVGs, netlists, .typ sources) go only to intermediates, if given. releases is a release root as release's into: with a stored release of the system there, overview.html marks what changed since it (the release at the model's revision, else the previous one); None marks nothing. Any ERROR in check(result) raises BuildErrors and leaves out_dir without an export, whole-model, with no escape hatch. Also raises ExportNameClash, TypeError or ValueError for a bad unit.

Does not write when check finds an ERROR; does not touch files in out_dir it does not own.

items.title: AcSupply
items.text:
class AcSupply

An AC supply: L1, L2, L3 and N when it was given one.

Does not hold a voltage of its own: each rail's potential carries the declared voltage.

items.title: AuthorError
items.text:
class AuthorError

A design mistake, caught at the call or, for a layout hint, at build.

items.title: BuildErrors
items.text:
class BuildErrors

Raised by write or release when their own findings hold an ERROR.

No escape hatch: there is no allow_errors, force or draft parameter anywhere in this package, and none will be added. findings holds every ERROR of the run that raised; the exception's own message is each finding, then its fix and findings-row URL. write's own findings are resolved through describe first (check's own contract); release's interface-bump findings are never described -- their message is already self-contained, naming the unit, revision and differing sections in plain text.

items.title: BuildResult
items.text:
class BuildResult

A frozen, laid-out model plus every finding collected while building it.

items.title: Cable
items.text:
class Cable

One cable: W1.core(BN, a, b) wires a core by colour or number; a series lands it.

Does not guess a core: a doubled or missing colour raises and lists the candidates.

items.title: DcSupply
items.text:
class DcSupply

A DC supply: plus, minus and mid when the source has an M conductor.

Stands in a series whole, as a power path's poles, or by one rail, as a control path's. Does not have a mid rail unless the source has an M conductor.

items.title: Design
items.text:
class Design

One circuit under construction, built through one engine Design.

Does not start a design: call fr.design.

items.title: Detail
items.text:
class Detail

The detail calls of one design: d.detail.wire, star, net, busbar and rail_bond.

Each is for a case no core call writes; try d.series first. Does not pair poles or take the next free terminal, as d.series does.

items.title: Device
items.text:
class Device

One device: Q1. A function by name (Q1.coil), a pin by [ ] (Q1[2], Q1["A1"]).

Does not guess: an unknown function or pin raises and lists the candidates.

items.title: DocumentPreset
items.text:
class DocumentPreset

The kind of deliverable a Document defines.

Example: CABINET_SCHEMATIC is the document of one cabinet. A preset fixes the default page kinds; a new one needs a decision record.

items.title: Draft
items.text:
class Draft

The only mutable type in the repo. Collects records before freeze().

Accepts a duplicate add of identical content as a no-op; a conflicting add under the same id raises MergeConflict immediately, naming both origins. Nothing here depends on the order things were added in: the accessors sort. A draft that raised is to be discarded, not repaired.

items.title: Finding
items.text:
class Finding

One reported engineering problem: one shape for every domain validator.

code is a stable UPPER_SNAKE string (e.g. NET_UNREALISED), listed in the module that emits it. subjects names the ids the finding is about, stored in Id order so that neither the order a validator happened to find them in nor a repeat matters.

Attributes: code: A stable UPPER_SNAKE string identifying the kind of problem (e.g. NET_UNREALISED), listed in the module that emits it. severity: How much this finding should block a downstream output. subjects: The ids this finding is about, stored once each, in Id order. message: The human-readable text of the finding.

items.title: Fn
items.text:
class Fn

One function of a device: K1.coil; a pin by [ ] (Q1.main[2]) or by name (K1.coil.A1).

Does not accept a guessed name: an unknown pin raises and lists the pins it has.

items.title: FreezeError
items.text:
class FreezeError

Aggregates every error freeze() found.

So an author fixes a batch, not one error per run.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
class Layout

The drawing hints of one design, each written through the engine.

Does not draw or place anything itself: every hint only advises the layout engine.

items.title: MergeConflict
items.text:
class MergeConflict

Two drafts or models declare the same id with different content.

Nothing wins silently: both origins are named.

items.title: Model
items.text:
class Model

The immutable, validated result of freeze().

Not a @value: it is never nested in a record, and tables is keyed by Id, outside the closed set @value enforces on its fields.

Everything reachable from a Model is deeply immutable, checked at freeze, not assumed. tables stays generic here (kind -> id -> record); vocab adds typed accessors (items(model), ports(model), ...) over it. digests holds one digest per registered namespace, so a change to layout.* records leaves the core and facet digests alone; digest combines them (design/kernel-model.md 5.6).

items.title: PageKind
items.text:
class PageKind

A kind of page in a document, in the one canonical page order.

Declaration order is the canonical order: a document's pages are its preset's pages plus add, minus remove, in this order, so no project specifies one. The set is closed.

items.title: PartLibraryError
items.text:
class PartLibraryError

A part library failed lint; findings holds every finding of that run.

Warnings included, not only the ERRORs that triggered the raise: a caller fixing the library wants the whole report, not a partial one.

items.title: Pin
items.text:
class Pin

One port of one Fn, reached by its marking or role.

Attributes: id: This port's id. key: This port's authoring key. name: The marking __getitem__ matches it by. role: What this port is for (e.g. INTERNAL/EXTERNAL).

items.title: Release
items.text:
class Release

One release folder under a releases root, read from its manifest.

name, version and revision come from the folder's path. interface, listing_digest, nested and files (path, sha256 pairs) come from baseline/manifest.json; a folder with no manifest has them empty. path is the folder.

items.title: ReleasePin
items.text:
class ReleasePin

A release nested in another, as its manifest records it.

items.title: Run
items.text:
class Run

count terminals of a strip that count up inside their own label, from 1.

Does not share numbering with the strip or another run; a series may name it as a strip.

items.title: Severity
items.text:
class Severity

How much a Finding should block a downstream output.

Fransys, not this repo, decides which severities block which outputs.

Attributes: INFO: Worth noting; blocks nothing in the facade's own policy. WARNING: Worth a look; also blocks nothing in the facade's own policy. ERROR: Blocks every export: the facade's write raises and writes nothing while any Finding of this severity remains.

items.title: SignalType
items.text:
class SignalType

The electrical nature of a PLC channel or field request, read as fr.SignalType.

Example: a 4-20 mA transmitter requests AI_CURRENT; a Pt100 requests RTD. fr.DI, fr.DO, fr.AI and fr.AO stay the spelling for DI, DO, AI_CURRENT and AO_CURRENT; this enum is the home of every other signal, such as fr.SignalType.RTD.

items.title: SupplyRail
items.text:
class SupplyRail

One rail of a supply: its source pin, the potential it carries and its conductor mark.

Does not wire itself: it stands in a series as a one-conductor element.

items.title: Terminal
items.text:
class Terminal

One terminal of a Strip: one function, ports inner/outer.

Attributes: id: This terminal's id. key: This terminal's authoring key. function: This terminal's one function, whose ports inner and outer reach.

items.title: TerminalStrip
items.text:
class TerminalStrip

One strip: X1[3] is its terminal 3, made on first use and the same handle after.

A terminal joins the function block it is first taken in, else the strip's own group. Does not pick a terminal for X1[3]: a number is explicit; take picks the next free ones.

items.title: Throw
items.text:
class Throw

One throw of changeovers in a series: line at the common, load at the throw.

A selector (its throws on the line side, or a d.poles group with selector=True) is entered at the throws and left at the commons. Several functions are one pole each, in order.

Does not wire by itself: it stands in a d.series call.

items.title: TypedDevice
items.text:
class TypedDevice

The base a generated module subclasses for one part; mpn is its whole contract.

N is the part's function names and S the subclass itself: device types interface= by one and returns the other.

Does not add behaviour: its subclass only declares functions and pins.

items.title: TypedFn
items.text:
class TypedFn

The base a generated module subclasses for one function of one part.

Does not add behaviour: its subclass only declares pins for the type checker.

items.title: UnitDef
items.text:
class UnitDef

A function made a unit by @unit: the release facts d.add writes.

Does not run the function; d.add builds the child and calls it.
