        c.detail.wire(psu.output["+"], run[1], wire=(BU, 0.75))
        for i in range(1, 31):
            with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Lamp {i}"):
                lamp = c.device(f"H{i}", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
                c.detail.wire(run[i + 1] if own else run[1], lamp.lamp["1"], wire=(BU, 0.75))
            c.detail.wire(lamp.lamp["2"], psu.output["-"], wire=(BU, 0.75))

    return len(built(body).model.tables["layout.link_marker"])


assert markers(own=True) == markers(own=False)

items.title: Layout profile
items.text:
d.layout advises the drawing and connects nothing: chain, keep_together, break_before, order, symbol, draw_in, side, sheet, page_title and profile. Add it last, only where the structure leaves the drawing a choice. d.layout.side(u1.bus_in, fr.ABOVE) puts a unit's interface above its outline, and fr.BELOW below it. An interface with no harness line ignores it. d.layout.page_title(x1, "Field terminals") names the pages drawing a block, function, device or nested unit.

The profile keywords, and the rule that a unit sets its own, are in layout-numbers.md.

d.layout.chain(r1.lamp, k3.main, f3.element, beside=k1.main) draws the chain beside the element k1.main, joined by short unmarked horizontals. Wire first: the chain joins the element by each end net they share, one or two, else AuthorError names them.

import fransys as fr

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
with d.function("RUN", "Pump run") as run:
    d.device("K1", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
with d.function("LAMPS", "Lamps") as lamps:
    d.device("H1", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
d.layout.order(run, lamps)
d.layout.profile(hide_unused_pins=True)

items.title: Documents
items.text: A Document record is what turns an authored design into a printable deliverable. fr.document authors one such record as a Draft. Pass it to fr.build(d, doc) next to the design d; the model does the rest at layout and write time.

items.title: Presets, cover and notes text
items.text:
fr.document(preset, subject, cover=..., add=(), remove=(), logo=None, notice="") takes a fr.DocumentPreset (CABINET_SCHEMATIC, HARNESS_DRAWING, PCB_SCHEMATIC, SYSTEM), which fixes the deliverable's default page kinds; add and remove adjust that set for one document. cover is a required path to a Markdown file, read verbatim and stored on the model; any number of documents may share one cover path. A missing cover is a FileNotFoundError naming the path. A file beside it, named the cover's stem plus .notes.md, is read automatically when present and becomes the document's notes page; there is no separate notes parameter, and a missing notes file is not an error, it just means no notes page. logo is an optional path to an SVG for the title block's logo cell, read the same way; leaving it out (the default) leaves that cell empty. notice is the text of the title block's IP notice cell, printed on every page of that document; "" (the default) leaves the cell empty. On A3 the cell is about 92 mm wide and holds about 370 characters at the label size. A longer notice gives TITLE_BLOCK_NOTICE_OVERFLOW. Customer and Author are narrower than with no notice. A unit released alone needs no d.project for either; its Author cell prints created of the unit's current revision, a project document's the project's author. d.project(notice=...) raises: the notice moved here.

The page kinds each preset holds by default (add and remove change them).

page kind CABINET_SCHEMATIC HARNESS_DRAWING PCB_SCHEMATIC SYSTEM COVER yes yes yes yes NOTES yes yes yes yes SHEET_INDEX yes yes yes yes CONTENTS no yes no no SCHEMATIC yes no yes no BLOCK_DIAGRAM no no no yes HARNESS_DRAWING no yes no yes PLC_LIST yes no no no TERMINAL_LIST yes no no no CONNECTOR_LIST yes no yes no CABLE_LIST no no no yes BOM yes yes yes yes

Every preset also takes PageKind.SHEET_INDEX, a "Sheets" page after the notes that lists each sheet (3, 2.3, block diagram sheets B1, B2) with its title and PDF page. It prints from two sheets; remove=(fr.PageKind.SHEET_INDEX,) drops it. The PDF is navigable and prints the same. Cross references and Sheets rows are invisible links. The outline lists sheets and devices. The viewer numbers a sheet by its sheet number and other pages in roman.

from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BK



class Cabinet(NamedTuple):
    pass


@fr.unit(
    "terminal-cabinet",
    revision=1,
    interface_version=1,
    date="2026-02-02",
    text="First",
    by="XX",
    title="Terminal cabinet",
    number="TC-1",
)
def terminal_cabinet(c):
    x1 = c.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 2, description="Field strip")
    k1 = c.device("K1", "DEMO-CO-4P-24")
    c.series(x1, k1.coil, x1, wire=(BK, 1.5))
    return Cabinet()


d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.add(terminal_cabinet, "U1")

cover = Path("cabinet.md")
cover.write_text("# Cabinet\n", encoding="utf-8")
Path("cabinet.notes.md").write_text("Site notes for the installer.\n", encoding="utf-8")

cabinet_document = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "terminal-cabinet", cover=cover)
result = fr.build(d, cabinet_document)
findings = fr.check(result)
assert not [f for f in findings if f.severity in (fr.Severity.ERROR, fr.Severity.WARNING)]
written = fr.write(result, Path("out"))
assert any(p.suffix == ".pdf" for p in written)

out/ now holds one PDF for the cabinet, with the cover and notes text on their own pages ahead of the schematic.

items.title: Subjects
items.text:
A document's subject is a unit, an item, or a place where units stand. It is one of:

  • A location handle, what d.location(...) returns: a place where units stand.
  • A device handle, what d.device(...) or d.harness(...) returns.
  • A unit release's name, a plain str, such as a cabinet's: resolved to the one instance of that release at build and write time, not at the fr.document call itself.

Any other value, such as a bare design, is a TypeError at the call. The cabinet example above passes its release name. A unit added with d.add(fn, "U1") is named by its release name:

class Io(NamedTuple):
    X1: fr.Device


@fr.unit("demo-io-board", revision=1, interface_version=1, date="2026-02-02", text="First", by="XX")
def board(u):
    x1 = u.device("X1", "DEMO-CONN-2P", interface=True)
    return Io(x1)


d2 = fr.design("demo_parts")
d2.add(board, "U1")
board_document = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "demo-io-board", cover=cover)
board_result = fr.build(d2, board_document)
assert not [f for f in fr.check(board_result) if f.severity is fr.Severity.ERROR]
assert any(p.name == "demo-io-board-v1.1.pdf" for p in fr.write(board_result, Path("out1")))

The PDF is named after the unit and its release, demo-io-board-v1.1.pdf.

items.title: List pages
items.text:
The terminal, PLC, connector, wire-label and designation lists flow in two columns. The cable list and the BOM take the full width. A row never splits. A table that reaches a column foot continues in the next column or page under its heading with " (cont.)". A split leaves at least two rows on each side, else the table moves whole. A long token breaks only at a hyphen or a slash. The cover's revision table stands one padding above the title block.

The connector list prints one table per connector, headed by its designation and the item's description, with a row per pin: Pin, Net, Mate and Ends. The CABINET_SCHEMATIC preset carries it. A pin no wire inside the unit reaches is not drawn on the unit's own pages, and its row in the connector table is where it shows. A cabinet document with no connector reports an INFO DOCUMENT_EMPTY_LIST, as it does for terminals.

items.title: Cable drawings
items.text: A HARNESS_DRAWING page draws each cable as one block, and a harness of two or more cables as one block around its cables. A block has its end boxes with their pins, a box per cable with its heading, and one wire per core. A core whose two ends stand in one row is a short link at that row. Two cores on one pin stand side by side in the pin's cell. A harness whose cables interleave is not drawn yet. A document that shows it stops with DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS.

items.title: A unit's own cable drawings
items.text:
A CABINET_SCHEMATIC document leaves out the cable pages. To print a unit's own cable drawings and cable list in its document, add their page kinds: add=(fr.PageKind.HARNESS_DRAWING, fr.PageKind.CABLE_LIST). remove= wins over add=: a kind named in both is left out.

from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BN


class Cabinet(NamedTuple):
    pass


@fr.unit("cable-cabinet", revision=1, interface_version=1, date="2026-02-02", text="First", by="XX")
def cable_cabinet(c):
    k1 = c.device("K1", "DEMO-CO-4P-24")
    k2 = c.device("K2", "DEMO-CO-4P-24")
    w1 = c.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5", length_m=2)
    w1.core(BN, k1.coil["A1"], k2.coil["A1"])
    return Cabinet()


d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.add(cable_cabinet, "U1")
cover = Path("cabinet.md")
cover.write_text("# Cabinet\n", encoding="utf-8")
pages = (fr.PageKind.HARNESS_DRAWING, fr.PageKind.CABLE_LIST)
own = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "cable-cabinet", cover=cover, add=pages)
result = fr.build(d, own)
assert not [f for f in fr.check(result) if f.severity is fr.Severity.ERROR]
assert any(p.suffix == ".pdf" for p in fr.write(result, Path("out")))
pdfs = {key: name for key, name in fr.export_names(result).items() if key[0] == "pdf"}
assert list(pdfs.values()) == ["cable-cabinet-v1.1.pdf"]  # the key is ("pdf", <document id>)

A TERMINAL_LIST page lists the terminal strips of each unit and location. A document whose design has no unit and no location lists nothing, so declare a unit or a location to get the page.

items.title: Block diagrams
items.text:
A BLOCK_DIAGRAM page draws a reading as boxes joined by one line per cable. The line carries the cable's designation, and a tab names the strip or connector it lands on. The SYSTEM preset carries the page after the notes: its boxes are the top-level units and items, its lines the top-level cables. A unit document does not carry it by default; add=(fr.PageKind.BLOCK_DIAGRAM,) puts it there, and the page shows that unit's own cables and its child units, never what lies inside them. A reading with no cable line gets no page.

The page is A2 landscape, 594 x 420 mm, with a 12 x 8 frame; the other pages keep the document's sheet. A diagram wider than one sheet continues on the next, and a line cut between sheets ends in a marker naming the other sheet. A kept page whose diagram cannot be drawn stops the export with DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS.

items.title: One PDF is one drawing
items.text:
Each fr.document(...) call, and each resulting PDF, is one drawing: a cabinet schematic, a harness drawing, or a PCB schematic, never several combined into one file. A unit follows the same rule at the unit's own level: a unit is one physical thing in one place, so its own items make one drawing set. A unit's drawings take the unit as subject; an item inside a unit is not a drawing. Places only split drawing sets at the top level, outside any unit.

Concretely: naming the unit's release (as "demo-io-board" above) draws that unit's one schematic. Naming a device that sits inside a unit (X1, not the unit) matches no drawing set at all, because the layout that device belongs to is attributed to the unit, not to the bare device. A schematic with nothing to draw adds no page and no finding while the document has another content page (a list with rows, a harness drawing, a block diagram). With none, check reports DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS (an ERROR), and write turns any ERROR into fr.BuildErrors with no export written. The harness and diagram messages of DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS stay ERRORs whatever else the document holds.

d3 = fr.design("demo_parts")
io = d3.add(board, "U1")
inner_document = fr.document(
    fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC,
    io.X1,
    cover=cover,
    remove=(fr.PageKind.PLC_LIST, fr.PageKind.TERMINAL_LIST, fr.PageKind.BOM),
)
inner_result = fr.build(d3, inner_document)
inner_findings = fr.check(inner_result)
assert "DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS" in {f.code for f in inner_findings}

try:
    fr.write(inner_result, Path("out2"))
except fr.BuildErrors as error:
    assert any(f.code == "DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS" for f in error.findings)
else:
    raise AssertionError("expected BuildErrors")

The fix is never to add pages or merge drawings by hand: it is to name the unit's release as the document's subject, as the unit example on this page does.

items.title: Drawing well
items.text: Layout draws the structure you author and invents none. This page says what layout reads, how to author a cabinet that draws readably, which numbers change its size, and which findings mean the design lacks structure.

items.title: How layout reads the model
items.text:
• Function blocks. with d.function("P1", "Pump 1"): groups the devices made inside it. Layout packs whole blocks onto pages, left to right, in order, and never reorders them to fill a gap. A block wider than a page is split between columns and reports GROUP_SPLIT. d.layout.order, keep_together, break_before and the profile's group_ranks set the order.
  • Page ends. A page holds the blocks whose widths sum to the content width, 1312 grid units on the house A3 sheet. A column's width is the room it took when placed: symbols, pin labels, link markers and the column gap. In the twelve-relay example below, the first relay blocks each take 176 units, so the first page holds the supply and six relays. A page ends at the first block that does not fit, at a break_before, at a keep_together set that does not fit, or at the end of a drawing set.
  • Current paths. Layout finds a current path where each net between two devices holds exactly two poles. A pole is the pair of pins a symbol passes current through, such as a coil or one contact. The path stands as one column, top to bottom, with straight wires. A net of three or more poles ends a path.
  • How to author a path. Author each path with d.series. Hand-wired d.detail.wire hops form a path only while each net keeps to two poles. d.series(a, b, c, wire=...) wires every hop pole to pole, so its elements form a path. d.layout.chain(...) names a path outright, and a named path wins over discovery.
  • Block edges end a path. A path never crosses from one function block into the next. When the two blocks land on different pages, the wire between them is cut into a marker pair and CHAIN_BROKEN warns. Keep each circuit inside one block. A device with two or more functions can split across blocks, a coil here and a contact there. A function of such a device, written in another block's d.series, draws in that block, and its coil's contact table names that page. d.layout.draw_in overrides this.
  • Tall paths. A path taller than the page continues at the top of the next column, on the same sheet while there is room, then on the next sheet. The wire across each cut becomes a marker pair. The path keeps its order, and nothing runs off the page.
  • Coils on PLC channels. A coil that a PLC channel drives stands under that channel's pin, always, whatever the row spacing. A column too tall for the page continues as tall paths do.
  • Box pins in marking order. A box prints its pins in marking order, whatever order its wired partners stand in, and the columns hung under it follow those pins.
  • Device chains. Some devices draw no symbol of their own, such as modules with an IN and an OUT connector. When such devices in one block are wired hop to hop, each wire alone, they form a chain. Each device then draws as one box with its wired pins only, and the chain stands as one column. A box's top pins face the device above and its bottom pins the device below, so each hop's wires run straight down. A chain starts at its end that sorts first by designation. A ring opens at its device that sorts first, and the wire that closes the ring becomes a marker pair.
  • Supplies. A declared DC supply (d.dc_supply) draws a power symbol at each pin on its rails, with no wire or marker. d.ac_supply keeps AC rails as terminals, drawn at each pin they feed. An undeclared rail is a plain net: wires and link markers.
  • Markers. A marker pair stands where one wire's two ends land on different pages. A net of three or more ports that is not drawn as wires gets one marker per port. A terminal is drawn at each of its wires instead. A net reference is filled with one of eight colours; every reference of the same net in the PDF has the same colour, and the text is the reference.
  • Nothing connected, nothing drawn. A symbol with nothing connected is not drawn; its list holds it.
  • One actuator per device. With actuator_each_contact=False, a manually operated device draws its actuator once, at its lead contact: the first contact its contact list prints. Its other contacts draw plain, with the device's designation and a reference to the actuator, and a contact list sits under the actuator.
  • Flat designs. A design of devices joined by point-to-point d.detail.wire calls is drawn from its nets alone. Circuits that share no net fill pages one after the other. One large connected circuit with no declared supply piles onto a single page and overflows it. Declare the supply and write each path as a series (see detail.md).

The draw helper below builds a cabinet and reads its findings. The block after it builds twelve relays on one declared 24 V supply.

from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU


class Cabinet(NamedTuple):
    pass


Path("cover.md").write_text("# Cabinet\n", encoding="utf-8")


built = {}


def rows(model, table):
    """The rows of a layout table: `Record` values, whose fields are read by name."""
    return model.tables[table].values()


def draw(body, top=None):
    """Build one cabinet with a schematic; return its finding codes and its page count."""

    @fr.unit(
        "cab", revision=1, interface_version=1, date="2026-01-01", text="First", by="XX",
        title="Cabinet", number="C-1",
    )
    def cabinet(c):
        body(c)
        return Cabinet()

    d = fr.design("demo_parts")
    d.add(cabinet, "U1")
    if top:
        top(d)
    doc = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "cab", cover=Path("cover.md"))
    result = fr.build(d, doc)
    built["model"] = result.model
    return [f.code for f in fr.check(result)], len(result.model.tables["layout.page"])

def relays(c):
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    for i in range(1, 13):
        with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Relay {i}"):
            k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
        c.series(dc.plus, k.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))


declared, _ = draw(relays)
assert "OUT_OF_CONTENT_BOX" not in declared


def coil_x(model, n):
    return next(p.x for p in model.tables["layout.symbol_placement"].values() if p.key[-3:-1] == (f"F{n}/K{n}", "fn"))


assert coil_x(built["model"], 2) - coil_x(built["model"], 1) == 184
assert coil_x(built["model"], 7) < coil_x(built["model"], 1)

items.title: A checklist for a readable cabinet
items.text:
The pump-station example in the examples repository has this shape.

  1. One unit per cabinet, and one function block per circuit: incoming supply, control supply, PLC, one block per motor starter.
  2. Keep every device of a circuit inside its block, so no path crosses a block edge.
  3. Declare each supply where it starts: d.ac_supply on the incoming terminals, d.dc_supply on the 24 V strip.
  4. Distribute through terminal strips with named, bridged runs, and give each consumer its own terminal.
  5. Wire each circuit as a path, source first: supply, protection, switching, load. Layout stands the bands in that order, with the first terminal on top and the last at the bottom.
  6. Set the page order once with d.layout.profile(group_ranks=...). A rank map replaces the house one whole, and an unranked block sorts last.
  7. Set hide_unused_pins=True to leave unwired pins of box-drawn devices off the drawings. The lists keep them.
  8. A terminal that only the parent wires is left off the unit's own pages; its table lists it.
  9. Build, then read fr.check(result). The last part of this page lists the findings that point at a missing item above.

Take each consumer's terminal inside the consumer's own block, since a terminal joins the block it is first taken in. A terminal shared by blocks adds no marker.

items.title: Printed sizes and grid pitch
items.text:
Authored numbers live on the sheet and the profile. A unit sets its own in its body, and a unit with none uses the house values. layout-numbers.md lists every sheet number and profile keyword with its house value and effect.

  • module_mm, on the sheet (see layout-numbers.md). This is the grid pitch. One grid unit is module_mm / 8 millimetres, and symbols and spacing scale with it; text and line widths are fixed in mm. The house value is 2.5. A smaller value fits more on a page, and a larger one fits less. Pitch is the reader's choice, not a fix: content that does not fit is split into function blocks.
  • text_height_mm, on the profile (see layout-numbers.md). A style choice: the capital height in mm (ISO 3098) of the smallest text on every page kind, 1.8 in the house profile, which takes 8 G. A larger role prints at its ISO size (2.5, 3.5 or 5 mm) or this height, whichever is larger. Nothing shrinks text to fit. A value past what the symbols leave room for leaves tags without a place.
  • min_text_height_mm, on the profile. This is the floor under the text, a capital height in millimetres: Decimal("1.8") in the house profile, the height the house text_height_mm prints. The floor changes no drawing. A profile that prints text under it gets one TEXT_TOO_SMALL.
  • column_gap, on the profile (see layout-numbers.md). This is spacing: grid units between columns, 48 in the house profile. Change it to give wires and tags room, not to fit a page.
def circuits(c, module_mm, text_height_mm=Decimal("1.8")):
    psu = c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", psu.output)
    for i in range(1, 34):
        with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Relay {i}"):
            k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
            c.series(dc.plus, k.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    sheet = c.layout.sheet(
        "A3 compact", width_mm=420, height_mm=297, content_x_mm=5, content_y_mm=5,
        content_width_mm=410, content_height_mm=267, frame_columns=8, frame_rows=6,
        module_mm=Decimal(module_mm),
    )
    c.layout.profile(sheet=sheet, text_height_mm=text_height_mm)


_, house_pages = draw(lambda c: circuits(c, "2.5"))
_, compact_pages = draw(lambda c: circuits(c, "1.5"))
assert compact_pages < house_pages

items.title: Which hint to use
items.text:
Each hint advises the layout and invents nothing. Every name below is a method of d.layout.

You want Tool What it does to the drawing These items in one column d.layout.chain(a, b, c) Stands them in one column, top to bottom, source first. These groups on one sheet d.layout.keep_together(g1, g2) Moves the later groups beside the first, so they share a page when their widths fit. This order d.layout.order(g1, g2) Moves g2 after g1. The other groups keep their places. This group starts a new sheet d.layout.break_before(g) Starts a new page at g. This page title d.layout.page_title(thing, text) Prints text as the title of the pages that draw the block, function, device or nested unit.

d.series is a wiring call, not a layout hint, so it has no row.

The block below applies each row to three relay blocks and reads the result.

def drawn(body):
    """Build one cabinet; return the block names on each page, and the x of each named function."""
    handles = {}

    @fr.unit(
        "cab", revision=1, interface_version=1, date="2026-01-01", text="First", by="XX",
        title="Cabinet", number="C-1",
    )
    def cabinet(c):
        handles.update(body(c))
        return Cabinet()

    d = fr.design("demo_parts")
    d.add(cabinet, "U1")
    doc = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "cab", cover=Path("cover.md"))
    result = fr.build(d, doc)
    names = {handle.id: name for name, handle in handles.items()}
    pages = sorted(rows(result.model, "layout.page"), key=lambda p: (p.drawing_set, p.number))
    x = {names[p.function]: p.x for p in rows(result.model, "layout.symbol_placement") if p.function in names}
    return [[names[g.group] for g in p.groups] for p in pages], x


def blocks(c, hint=None, count=3):
    groups = {}
    for i in range(1, count + 1):
        with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Relay {i}") as group:
            k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
            feed = c.terminal_strip(f"X{i}", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 2)
            c.series(feed, k.coil, feed, wire=(BU, 0.75))  # a symbol with nothing connected is not drawn
        groups[f"F{i}"] = group
    if hint:
        hint(c.layout, groups)
    return groups


def coils(c, chain):
    psu = c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", psu.output)
    ks = [c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24") for i in (1, 2, 3)]
    lamp = c.device("H1", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
    c.series(dc.plus, *(k.coil for k in ks), dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    c.series(ks[0].coil, lamp.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    if chain:
        c.layout.chain(ks[0].coil, ks[1].coil, ks[2].coil)
    return {f"K{i}": k.coil for i, k in enumerate(ks, 1)}


_, loose = drawn(lambda c: coils(c, chain=False))
_, chained = drawn(lambda c: coils(c, chain=True))
assert len(set(loose.values())) > 1
assert len(set(chained.values())) == 1
assert drawn(blocks)[0] == [["F1", "F2", "F3"]]
together, _ = drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, lambda hints, g: hints.keep_together(g["F1"], g["F3"])))
assert together == [["F1", "F3", "F2"]]
ordered, _ = drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, lambda hints, g: hints.order(g["F3"], g["F1"])))
assert ordered == [["F2", "F3", "F1"]]
broken, _ = drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, lambda hints, g: hints.break_before(g["F2"])))
assert broken == [["F1"], ["F2", "F3"]]

items.title: What overrides what
items.text:
The profile sets the numbers and the page order, and the hints then act on that order.

  • A sheet needs a profile. d.layout.sheet(...) changes nothing until d.layout.profile(sheet=...) names it. A profile that leaves sheet out draws on the house A3 sheet.
  • A profile reaches only its own unit. The top design's profile does not reach a unit, and a unit with no profile of its own uses the house numbers. A unit or the top design has at most one profile, and a second one with other numbers raises AuthorError.
  • A keyword left out keeps its house value. A rank map you give replaces the house one whole.
  • order beats group_ranks. The ranks sort the blocks first, then each order hint moves blocks from that order.
  • keep_together beats order. It runs after the order hints, pulls its groups next to the first, and reports ORDER_HINT_UNDONE when that reverses an order hint.
  • break_before on a later group of a keep_together set leaves the set unkept and reports KEEP_TOGETHER_UNMET. On the set's first group it changes nothing.
  • Order hints that form a cycle make the build raise fr.AuthorError naming the cycle.
  • A chain names a box-drawn function only at its head or its tail. A PLC channel or a supply output stands there and anchors the path at its pin. In the middle the build raises fr.AuthorError that says where box-drawn functions may stand.
def compact_sheet(scope):
    return scope.layout.sheet(
        "A3 compact", width_mm=420, height_mm=297, content_x_mm=5, content_y_mm=5,
        content_width_mm=410, content_height_mm=267, frame_columns=8, frame_rows=6,
        module_mm=Decimal("1.5"),
    )


def numbers(c):
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    for i in range(1, 34):
        with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Relay {i}"):
            k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
            c.series(dc.plus, k.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))

assert draw(lambda c: (numbers(c), c.layout.profile(sheet=compact_sheet(c))))[1] < house_pages

ranked = lambda hints, g: hints.profile(group_ranks={"F3": 1, "F2": 2, "F1": 3})
assert drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, ranked))[0] == [["F3", "F2", "F1"]]


def ranked_then_ordered(hints, g):
    ranked(hints, g)
    hints.order(g["F1"], g["F3"])


assert drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, ranked_then_ordered))[0] == [["F2", "F1", "F3"]]


def kept_and_ordered(hints, g):
    hints.keep_together(g["F1"], g["F3"])
    hints.order(g["F2"], g["F3"])


assert drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, kept_and_ordered))[0] == [["F1", "F3", "F2"]]


def kept_and_broken(hints, g):
    hints.keep_together(g["F1"], g["F2"])
    hints.break_before(g["F2"])


unkept = lambda c: blocks(c, kept_and_broken)
assert "KEEP_TOGETHER_UNMET" in draw(lambda c: unkept(c))[0]
assert drawn(unkept)[0] == [["F1"], ["F2", "F3"]]


def cycle(hints, g):
    hints.order(g["F1"], g["F2"])
    hints.order(g["F2"], g["F1"])


top_only = draw(lambda c: numbers(c), top=lambda d: d.layout.profile(sheet=compact_sheet(d)))[1]
assert top_only == house_pages

try:
    draw(lambda c: (c.layout.profile(text_height_mm=Decimal("1.8")), c.layout.profile(text_height_mm=Decimal("2.0"))))
except Exception as error:
    assert type(error).__name__ == "AuthorError"
else:
    raise AssertionError("a second profile must raise")

try:
    drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, cycle))
except Exception as error:
    assert type(error).__name__ == "AuthorError" and "cycle" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("an order cycle must raise")

items.title: Findings that mean missing structure
items.text:
• FUNCTION_UNPLACED_IN_COLUMN. No current path reaches the function, so it stands alone in a column. A box-drawn device, such as a power supply or a lamp, has no pole of its own. It stands in a path only when a path ends on it. A lamp wired straight across two rails is on none, and wired after a contact it ends that contact's path. Many of these in one unit mean many devices hang on no path.
  • LABEL_UNPLACED. A tag, marking or cross-reference found no free place. A text_height_mm above the house value is one cause. Put it back to 1.8.
  • CHAIN_BROKEN. A path was cut by a page break between two blocks. Keep the circuit in one block.
  • PAGE_OVERFULL and OUT_OF_CONTENT_BOX. A circuit is too big for its page. Declare its supply, wire it as paths, or split it into blocks. Else send the smallest model. PAGE_PAD frames the ink.
  • Readability. Five findings tell you whether the printed pages can be read. TEXT_TOO_SMALL says the profile prints text under min_text_height_mm. PAGE_UNDERFILLED says a page's content covers under half of its content box. TEXT_OVERLAP, WIRE_OVER_LABEL and LABEL_UNPLACED say text collides with text or a wire, or has no place. Those two are INFO: Fransys defects, report with the smallest model.

The next block counts the first two. Lamps wired across the rails stand alone, lamps after a contact do not, and a text height of 24 leaves tags without a place.

def lamps(c, after_contact):
    psu = c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", psu.output)
    for i in range(1, 6):
        k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
        h = c.device(f"H{i}", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
        if after_contact:
            c.series(dc.plus, k.co_1.no, h.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
        else:
            c.series(dc.plus, h.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))


across, _ = draw(lambda c: lamps(c, after_contact=False))
after, _ = draw(lambda c: lamps(c, after_contact=True))
assert across.count("FUNCTION_UNPLACED_IN_COLUMN") > after.count("FUNCTION_UNPLACED_IN_COLUMN")

big_text, _ = draw(lambda c: circuits(c, "2.5", text_height_mm=Decimal("5.4")))
assert "LABEL_UNPLACED" in big_text

The numbers behind the readability findings are in fr.readability: readability.md.

items.title: Examples
items.text: Worked examples of whole circuits, each shown the easy way and the efficient way, and a pointer to a full build script outside this repository. All parts are from demo_parts.

items.title: A motor starter with a start/stop latch
items.text:
S1 and S2 are two contact blocks: S1's break contact (nc) stops, S2's make contact (no) starts. The power circuit runs from the three-phase supply through a breaker, the contactor's make contacts (main) and an overload relay to a terminal strip. A cable carries it to the motor. The power supply G1 takes its mains from L1 and N of the same supply. The control circuit runs from the 24 V rail through the stop contact, a latch and the overload's break contact to the contactor coil. The latch is the start contact in parallel with the contactor's own auxiliary make contact.

d.series(a, b, ...) is the one spelling for a chain of connections, and d.parallel(...) puts branches between two neighbours. The design is a plain top design: no place and no cabinet.

# easy: motor starter
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BK, BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", x0[1], x0[2], x0[3], n=x0[4])
g1 = d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", g1)
q0 = d.device("Q0", "DEMO-MCB-3P")
q1 = d.device("Q1", "DEMO-CTR-3P-24")
f1 = d.device("F1", "DEMO-OVERLOAD-3P")
s1 = d.device("S1", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
s2 = d.device("S2", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")
d.series(ac, q0.element, q1.main, f1.main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(ac.L1, g1.input, ac.N, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(dc.plus, s1.nc, d.parallel(s2.no, q1.aux), f1.aux, q1.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))

The efficient version builds the same model. The devices come from one table of tag and part number, so adding a device is one more line in the table.

# efficient: motor starter
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BK, BU

PARTS = {
    "G1": "DEMO-PSU-24",
    "Q0": "DEMO-MCB-3P",
    "Q1": "DEMO-CTR-3P-24",
    "F1": "DEMO-OVERLOAD-3P",
    "S1": "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC",
    "S2": "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC",
}

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", *(x0[n] for n in (1, 2, 3)), n=x0[4])
i = {tag: d.device(tag, mpn) for tag, mpn in PARTS.items()}
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", i["G1"])
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")
d.series(ac, i["Q0"].element, i["Q1"].main, i["F1"].main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(ac.L1, i["G1"].input, ac.N, wire=(BK, 2.5))
latch = d.parallel(i["S2"].no, i["Q1"].aux)
d.series(dc.plus, i["S1"].nc, latch, i["F1"].aux, i["Q1"].coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))

items.title: Sixteen sensors to a terminal strip
items.text:
Each sensor is one device, wired by its signal pin to its own terminal on a strip. The strip takes its terminals in number order: each series that names the strip takes the next free one. A series from a sensor's function to the strip wires its load pin B to that terminal. The first sensor added lands on terminal 1, so the sensors are added from B16 down to B1.

# easy: sensors to a strip
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
with d.function("SENS", "Sensors"):
    x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
    b16 = d.device("B16", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b16.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b15 = d.device("B15", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b15.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b14 = d.device("B14", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b14.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b13 = d.device("B13", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b13.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b12 = d.device("B12", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b12.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b11 = d.device("B11", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b11.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b10 = d.device("B10", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b10.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b9 = d.device("B9", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b9.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b8 = d.device("B8", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b8.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b7 = d.device("B7", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b7.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b6 = d.device("B6", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b6.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b5 = d.device("B5", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b5.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b4 = d.device("B4", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b4.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b3 = d.device("B3", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b3.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b2 = d.device("B2", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b2.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b1 = d.device("B1", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b1.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))

The efficient version is a list of sensor tags in the order the strip hands out terminals, and one loop.

# efficient: sensors to a strip
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

SENSORS = [f"B{n}" for n in range(16, 0, -1)]

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
with d.function("SENS", "Sensors"):
    x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
    for tag in SENSORS:
        sensor = d.device(tag, "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
        d.series(sensor.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))

items.title: The whole shape of a build script
items.text:
The examples above build small pieces of a design. For a real build script end to end, see examples/pump-station/build.py in the public fransys repository, at the tag you pinned. It has its own parts library (example_parts), so it cannot run as a block on this page. It shows:

  • The project and its revision history, set up once at the top.
  • A cabinet unit with a second unit, the relay-interface board, mated to it through headers.
  • Locations and functions built section by section: incoming supply, control supply, a PLC rack, and a per-pump circuit written once as a function and called for each pump.
  • Several documents for several audiences from one design, then one fr.build and a fr.write per audience.

Consumer bugs become permanent tests in tests/field_cases/ of the Fransys repository. Each module's docstring states the engineering shape and the decision that fixed it.

items.title: Finding codes: KiCad
items.text:
Codes the KiCad import emits. Who acts is explained in findings.md.

Code Severity Stage Who acts Meaning Fix NET_NAME_DUPLICATE ERROR kicad consumer Two or more KiCad netlist nets share a name, so KiCad would merge them on import. Give each net a distinct name. NET_SINGLE_PIN INFO kicad note A KiCad netlist net has one pin. Nothing is wrong; wire a second end only if one was meant. NODE_WITHOUT_COMPONENT WARNING kicad consumer A netlist pin belongs to an item with no footprint (or is the board's own pin), so KiCad drops it on import. Give the item a footprint, or model the connector as a child item with one. PAD_ON_MULTIPLE_NETS ERROR kicad consumer One component pad is in more than one KiCad netlist net. Fix the wiring so each pad is on exactly one net. PART_WITHOUT_FOOTPRINT WARNING kicad consumer A board item's part has no footprint, so the KiCad netlist omits it. Add a footprint to the part. REFERENCE_DUPLICATE ERROR kicad consumer Two board parts share one reference designation in the KiCad netlist. Give each part a distinct designation. UNCONNECTED_PIN INFO kicad note A pin of a board part is in no net in the KiCad netlist. Usually nothing to fix unless a connection was meant.

items.title: Finding codes: part files
items.text:
Codes the part-file lint emits, at fr.lint and when fr.design or fr.parts loads a library. Who acts is explained in findings.md.

Code Severity Stage Who acts Meaning Fix BAR_SYMBOL ERROR library load part author A bar function names a symbol; a bar is never drawn. Remove the function's symbol key. BOARD_WITHOUT_PCB WARNING library load part author A part with category = "board" has no [pcb] table. Add a [pcb] table with a revision string, or change category to the part's real category. CABLE_PAIR_INVALID ERROR library load part author A [cable_product] pairs entry breaks a pair rule: a core is out of range, in two pairs, or SH, or a screen is not a unique SH core. Give each pairs entry two integer cores in range, none SH and none in another pair, and a screen that is one unique SH core. CABLE_WITHOUT_PRODUCT ERROR library load part author A part with category = "cable" has no [cable_product] table, or a part with another category has one. Add a [cable_product] table to a cable part, or remove [cable_product] from a part whose category is not cable. CHANGEOVER_LINK ERROR library load part author A switched link of a contact_co function joins two ports whose roles are not common with break or make. Make each switched link of the contact_co function join a common port to a break or make port. CHANGEOVER_ROLE ERROR library load part author A port of a contact_co function has a role other than common, break or make. Set that port's role to common, break or make. CHANGEOVER_SYMBOL_PORT ERROR library load part author A port of a contact_co function sets symbol_port. Remove symbol_port from the contact_co port; the drawing binds a changeover by its throw roles. CLASS_CODE ERROR library load part author class_code is not 1 to 3 uppercase letters, starts with A, I or O, or starts with D, L, V, Y or Z. Set class_code to 1 to 3 uppercase letters, first letter as in IEC 81346-2, such as K or QA. CONNECTOR_MARKING_REUSED ERROR library load part author Two connector functions of one part print the same label, their marking or else their name. Give one connector function a different marking under [function.connector], or a different name. CONTACT_WITHOUT_SWITCHED_LINK ERROR library load part author A contact_no, contact_nc, contact_co or switch function has no switched link in its links. Add a links entry with kind = "switched" joining its ports, or change the function's kind. ENERGY_ON_NON_POWER ERROR library load part author A function whose kind is not supply or load sets energy. Remove energy from the function, or change its kind to supply or load. ENUM_VALUE ERROR library load part author A field typed as an enum holds a string that is no member of that enum. Set the field to one of the values the message lists, such as a kind or role value. FACET_KIND_MISMATCH ERROR library load part author A [function.connector] sits on a function whose kind is not connector, or a [function.plc_channel] on one whose kind is not plc_channel. Change the function's kind to match the sub-table, or move the sub-table to the right [[function]]. FIELD_MISSING ERROR library load part author A required key is absent: the file's schema, its [part] table, or a required field of a table. Add the schema = 1 line, the [part] table, or the required field the message names. FIELD_TYPE ERROR library load part author A value has a TOML type the contract does not allow there, such as an integer for a quantity or a table where a list belongs. Write the value as the type the message names, such as a quoted string for a rating or an integer for schema. FIELD_UNKNOWN ERROR library load part author A table holds a key the part-file contract does not name for that table. Remove the key, or correct its spelling to a field the part-file contract names. FILE_NAME WARNING library load part author A part file's name has characters other than lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. Rename the file using only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. FUNCTION_NAME_DUPLICATE ERROR library load part author Two [[function]] entries of one part have the same name. Give one of the functions a different name. FUNCTION_WITHOUT_PORTS ERROR library load part author A [[function]] other than a bar has an empty ports list. Add at least one entry to the function's ports array, or remove the function. JOIN_INTO_CONNECTOR ERROR library load part author A header pin's joins names a port of a connector function. Point joins at a port of a non-connector function of the same part. JOIN_PORT_TWICE ERROR library load part author Two header pins of one part both joins the same function port. Remove the joins from one of the two header pins, or point it at a different port. JOIN_PORT_UNKNOWN ERROR library load part author A header pin's joins value does not name a port of a function in this part, or is not <function>.<port>. Set joins to <function>.<port> naming an existing port of another function of this part. LIBRARY_FILE_MISSING ERROR library load part author The library root has no library.toml file. Add library.toml at the library package root with schema, name and version. LINK_DUPLICATE ERROR library load part author Two links entries of one function join the same pair of ports, in either order. Remove the repeated links entry. LINK_PORT_UNKNOWN ERROR library load part author A links entry's a or b is not a name in the function's ports. Set a and b to names from the function's ports, or add the missing port. LINK_SELF ERROR library load part author A links entry has the same port as a and b. Set b to a different port from a. PART_DUPLICATE ERROR library load part author Two part files declare the same manufacturer and mpn pair. Remove one of the files, or correct the mpn or manufacturer of the one declared in error. PINCOUNT ERROR library load part author A [function.connector] has a pincount below 1. Set pincount to 1 or more. PLC_CHANNEL_DUPLICATE ERROR library load part author Two [function.plc_channel] tables of one part have the same channel and signal. Give one of the channels a different channel number, or a different signal. PORT_NAME_DUPLICATE ERROR library load part author Two ports of one function have the same name. Rename one of the ports so each port name in the function is unique. PORT_NAME_SHARED ERROR library load part author Two functions of one part give a port the same name, and their printed designations would be the same. Rename the port on one of the two functions so the printed designations differ. POWER_LOSS_TWICE ERROR library load part author power_loss_w is set both in the part's [rating] and in a function's [function.rating]. Keep power_loss_w in one place: remove it from [rating] or from the [function.rating] it repeats. PROTECTION_LINK_KIND ERROR library load part author A switched link sits on a protection function, or a through link's kind does not fit its protection type. Use kind = "protective" for fuse, mcb, motor_breaker and rcd, and kind = "conductive" for overload; never switched. PROTECTION_TYPE_ON_NON_PROTECTION ERROR library load part author A function whose kind is not protection has a [function.protection] table with a type. Remove the [function.protection] table, or change the function's kind to protection. PROTECTION_WITHOUT_TYPE WARNING library load part author A protection function has no type in its [function.protection] table. Add type to [function.protection], one of fuse, mcb, motor_breaker, overload or rcd. RATING_TABLE_EMPTY ERROR library load part author A [rating], [function.rating] or [function.operating] table has no field. Add at least one value to the table, or delete the table. RATING_VALUE_INVALID ERROR library load part author A rating value is not a plain decimal string, is zero where a rating needs a positive value, or a breaking point list is malformed. Write each value as a quoted plain decimal such as "24", above zero in ratings, and each breaking point with voltage_v and current_a. REST_DISAGREES_WITH_KIND ERROR library load part author A switched link's rest disagrees with its function's kind: contact_no is open at rest, contact_nc is closed. Set rest to match kind, open for contact_no and closed for contact_nc, or change kind. REST_ON_UNSWITCHED_LINK ERROR library load part author A link whose kind is not switched sets rest. Remove rest from the link, or change its kind to switched. SCHEMA_MIXED ERROR library load part author A part file's schema differs from the schema in its library's library.toml. Set the file's schema to the value library.toml names, or change library.toml and every file in one commit. SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED ERROR library load part author A schema value is not in SUPPORTED_SCHEMAS, which today holds only 1. Set schema = 1, the only supported value today. SWITCHED_LINK_WITHOUT_REST ERROR library load part author A switched link of a switch or generic function sets no rest. Add rest = "open" or rest = "closed" to the link. SYMBOL_PORT_WITHOUT_SYMBOL ERROR library load part author A port sets symbol_port, but its function has no symbol. Add a symbol to the function, or remove symbol_port from the port. SYMBOL_REST_MISMATCH ERROR library load part author A function's symbol implies a rest state (make-contact open; break-contact and emergency-stop closed), and its switched links, stated or implied by its kind, are all at the other one. Change the symbol, or the rest of the switched links, so both name the same rest state. SYMBOL_SLUG ERROR library load part author A function's symbol is not a lowercase, hyphenated slug. Rewrite symbol in lowercase letters and digits, joined by single hyphens, such as change-over-contact. SYMBOL_TYPE_MISMATCH ERROR library load part author A protection function's symbol is fuse or circuit-breaker, but its protection type is another one. Make type match the symbol: fuse for fuse, mcb for circuit-breaker, or change the symbol. TABLE_UNKNOWN ERROR library load part author The file has a top-level table that is neither schema nor a part-file table the contract names. Remove the table, or rename it to a table the part-file contract names.

items.title: Finding codes: PDF
items.text:
Codes the PDF output emits. Who acts is explained in findings.md.

Code Severity Stage Who acts Meaning Fix COVER_OVERFLOW ERROR write, release consumer A document's cover text plus revision table, measured by Typst at write, are taller than the content box; the write raises and writes nothing. Shorten the cover or the revision text. DOCUMENT_EMPTY_LIST INFO pdf note A document's list page (PLC, terminal, connector, wire-label, designation, cable or BOM) has no rows and is left out. Usually nothing to fix (pdf-0019); add records to show it. DOCUMENT_MIXED_SHEET_FORMATS ERROR pdf consumer A document's pages use more than one sheet format. Give the document (or its unit/layout profile) one sheet format for all pages. DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS ERROR pdf consumer A SCHEMATIC page has no drawing set and the document has no other content page, or a HARNESS_DRAWING or BLOCK_DIAGRAM page has no cable or diagram, or a drawing is missing, too large or not drawable yet: interleaved harness cables, or a block diagram whose tallest column is taller than one sheet (a known limit of the system diagram; DIAGRAM_COLUMN_TOO_TALL names the column). Add the missing content, remove the page kind or shorten the texts. DOCUMENT_NO_TOP_LEVEL_CABLES INFO pdf note A SYSTEM document's HARNESS_DRAWING section has nothing to draw: the model has no top-level cable. Usually nothing to fix: add a top-level cable if one was expected. DRAWING_SET_REPLICA_ONLY INFO pdf note A document's drawing set holds only black-box replicas of another unit's boundary. Usually nothing to fix; add content if a page is intended. MARKDOWN_UNSUPPORTED ERROR pdf consumer A document's cover or notes text uses a Markdown construct the PDF renderer does not support. Rewrite it using only the supported Markdown subset. TITLE_BLOCK_UNIT_IDENTITY_MISSING WARNING pdf consumer A unit document's unit has an empty title or number, so that title-block cell will print empty. Give the unit release a title and/or number.

items.title: Finding codes: layout and render
items.text:
Codes the layout and the drawing stage emit. Who acts is explained in findings.md.

Code Severity Stage Who acts Meaning Fix ALIGN_DROPPED WARNING render consumer Symbols of a row group or a band rank, mated pins, or the legs of a trunk, cannot stand level because the stacks in their columns contradict it; layout dropped the alignment. Shorten the stack, move the members to the same end of their columns, or take the band or mate off one of them (Drawing well). BLOCK_NOT_PLACED ERROR render Fransys A block stands in no row of any page, or a whole block in more than one, so layout draws it by no rule; the message names the block and the stage. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. CARD_OVERFULL WARNING render consumer A box has more attached columns than its card holds; the columns that do not fit stand free of the card. Split the box into two boxes, or attach fewer columns to it, so every column fits its card (Drawing well). If it still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. CHAIN_BROKEN WARNING render consumer A connection between two "pole" cells was severed into a marker pair though its net has only those ports. Keep the whole circuit in one function block, so no page break falls inside it (Drawing well). CHAIN_NOT_DRAWN WARNING render consumer A box that is one hop of a chain of boxes that CHAIN_REFUSED turned away is drawn on no page; the message names it. Fix the shape CHAIN_REFUSED names, so the chain draws as one column of boxes. CHAIN_REFUSED WARNING render consumer Boxes wired box to box do not make a chain that draws as one column: a ring, a box joined to three boxes, a box also wired by a trunk, or pins that do not face. The message names the boxes and the reason. Wire each box only to the next, with the pins toward the previous box on the north side and those toward the next on the south side. CONNECTION_DRAWN_TWICE ERROR render consumer A connection (or net-group edge) is drawn by more than one route, or also contradicted by a cut decision. Remove the duplicate so the connection is drawn or cut once. CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN ERROR render consumer A conductor or net-group edge is neither routed on a shared page nor cut with a marker. Give both ends a location so layout can route or cut them; check layout.route, layout.symbol_placement and layout.page. CONNECTION_TO_UNDRAWN WARNING render consumer A connection, net group or rail has an end whose function layout never draws. Put the missing end's item in a drawn unit or location, or remove the connection. DIAGRAM_BOX_OVERLAP ERROR render Fransys Two boxes of a block diagram or of an overview view, or a tab and a box, overlap. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. DIAGRAM_CABLE_FANOUT INFO render note A cable reaches three or more boxes, so the block diagram draws a line from its first box to each other. Nothing is wrong; split the cable only if a line per pair is not wanted. DIAGRAM_CABLE_ONE_BOX INFO render note A cable's ends reach one box or none, so the block diagram draws no line for it. Usually nothing to fix: the cable runs inside one box, or an end is an unmated plug. DIAGRAM_COLUMN_TOO_TALL INFO render note A block diagram gets no page because its tallest column holds more boxes than one sheet holds; the message gives the column, its boxes and how many fit. A known limit of the system diagram: no setting changes it. DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS is the error that stops the write. DIAGRAM_LABEL_STRUCK INFO render Fransys A line of a block diagram or an overview view passes through a line label. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model DIAGRAM_LINES_SHARE_TRACK INFO render Fransys Two cables of a block diagram or an overview view run along one track. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model DIAGRAM_LINE_OFF_BOX ERROR render Fransys A line of a block diagram or an overview view does not end on its box's outline or tab. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. DIAGRAM_LINE_THROUGH_BOX ERROR render Fransys A line of a block diagram or an overview view crosses a box other than its own two. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. DIAGRAM_LOOSE_WIRE INFO render note In the system reading, a wire with no cable joins two boxes and is not drawn. Usually nothing to fix: the unit pages show it as stubs. Put it in a cable to give it a line. DIAGRAM_TEXT_OVERLAP ERROR render Fransys Two texts of a block diagram or an overview view overlap. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. DRAWING_SHORTS_NETS INFO render Fransys A page draws two nets joined that the wiring keeps apart: a stub, a wire end or a power symbol lies on, or crosses, another net's wire or symbol. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. Check first that no authored hint crowds the nets. FILL_UNDER_MIN WARNING render consumer A page is filled less than the minimum because no cut of the blocks fills it more. Merge the group with its neighbour or drop its page break, so the page fills (Drawing well). FUNCTION_UNPLACED_IN_COLUMN INFO render consumer A function is on no current path, authored or found from the wiring, so layout placed it alone in its own column. Wire the function into a current path (d.series, or d.detail.wire with two poles per net), or name the path with d.layout.chain; see drawing.md. GROUP_SPLIT WARNING render consumer A group of columns is wider than one page, so layout split it between columns. Split the block into function blocks that each fit one page (Drawing well). HEAD_OFF_LEGS WARNING render consumer A trunk is cut by a page and its head stands on the page with fewer of its legs. Reorder the groups so the head and most of its legs share a page (Drawing well). JOIN_UNALIGNED INFO render Fransys Same-net, same-facing ports at one end of neighbouring columns could not be aligned onto one row, so layout drew references. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model KEEP_TOGETHER_UNMET WARNING render consumer An authored keep_together set could not be kept on one page (it does not fit, its groups sit on different drawing sets, or break_before is invalid). Shrink the set, move its groups onto one drawing set, or drop the hint. LABEL_UNPLACED WARNING render consumer A tag, marking or cross-reference found no free spot and sits at its default. Use the house text_height_mm 1.8; give the design structure (Drawing well). If it still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. LAYOUT_MISSING ERROR render consumer The model has connected functions to draw, but layout made no page for them. A function with nothing connected is drawn on no page and does not count. Add a document so layout runs, and check the drawn location or unit holds the connected content. LIBRARY_VERSION_MISMATCH WARNING render consumer A placement was laid out against a symbol library version other than the installed one. Re-run layout (build) with the installed electrical_symbols version. LINE_ON_OUTLINE INFO render Fransys A harness line runs along a unit outline's edge, so the two read as one stroke. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model LINK_FANOUT WARNING render consumer More than one severed link crosses between the same two pages on one net. Join the net once with a terminal instead of severing it repeatedly between the same two pages. LINK_PARTNER_UNLOCATED WARNING render consumer A signal crosses into a drawing set with no authored location, so its marker has no located prefix. Name the drawing set's unit or location. LONE_CELL WARNING render consumer A symbol has nothing connected, so it is drawn on no page; the message names the pins to wire and no page. Or a symbol stands alone on a page though its column has cells elsewhere. Wire the named pins, or remove the device if it is not used; or move the column's cells onto one page. A unit's own open boundary functions and the item box standing under them, spare contacts and spare terminals never give it (decisions layout-0077, layout-0202 and layout-0218). MARKER_UNPAIRED ERROR render Fransys A severed connection's owner or user marker is missing, or a page marker matches no severed decision. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. Check first that the cut decision and its markers agree. NO_BLOCK WARNING render consumer A box is drawn but belongs to no block, or to more than one, so layout places it by no rule; the message names it. Wire the box, or remove it. If it is wired and still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. NO_CELL WARNING render consumer A symbol is drawn but stands in no cell of any column, or in more cells than it has elements, so layout places it by no rule; the message names it. Attach the symbol to a lane or a box pin, or remove it. If it is wired and still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. ORDER_HINT_UNDONE WARNING render consumer An authored keep_together set pulled a group across an authored order hint, so the page order is not the one the order hint asked for. Drop the keep_together hint or the order hint, or order both hints to agree; keep_together wins when you keep both. ORDER_HINT_UNMET WARNING render consumer An authored order hint names two groups that are not on the same drawing set, so no page order can honour it. Move both groups onto one drawing set, or drop the hint. OUT_OF_CONTENT_BOX WARNING render consumer A symbol's keep-out box, label, marker box or route vertex sits outside the page's content box; the message ends " at p:", with the drawing set before the page (p<set>.<page>) only when the layout has more than one. Declare the supplies, wire each circuit as a current path, or split it into function blocks (Drawing well). If it still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. OVERVIEW_UNPLACED ERROR render Fransys The overview placer found no room plan for one view of the system overview, so the page would have no positions for it. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. PAGE_OVERFLOW WARNING render consumer A row of one block is taller than the page, so it stands on a page of its own. Split the block into smaller groups, or use a larger page (Drawing well). If the block is small, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. PAGE_OVERFULL WARNING render consumer A page's rows are taller than the content box; nothing is scaled. Declare the supply, or split the circuit into function blocks (Drawing well). If it still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. PAGE_UNDERFILLED INFO render note A schematic page whose drawn content covers under half of the content box; its message gives the share and the page reference (+C<set>p<page> or (p<set>.<page>), from the naming pass). Nothing is moved or scaled. No action is needed. The page is mostly empty; a larger module_mm spreads the content (Drawing well). PIN_MAP_INCOMPLETE ERROR render consumer A symbol node has no model port bound to any of its symbol ports at all. Add the missing model port or a port_map/symbol choice. POWER_SYMBOL_UNPLACED INFO render Fransys No lead of up to 12 grids kept a power symbol clear of its neighbours, so it keeps one grid and may touch. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model REDUNDANT_JOG INFO render Fransys A drawn route leaves a straight line and returns to it where a straight run was free. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model REFERENCE_BOX_EXCEEDS_ROOM WARNING render consumer A drawing set has 100 or more cross-reference numbers (#n) or pages; a reference box then exceeds layout's room. Keep each drawing set under 100 pages and 100 #n numbers: split the design into units. REFERENCE_OFF_DOCUMENT WARNING render consumer A printed reference points to a page that no page of its own document holds, and its text prints no location, so a reader cannot tell which document to open. The message names the reference, its page and the target page. Print both drawing sets in one document, or give the target's drawing set a location so the reference names it. ROUTE_FAILED ERROR render consumer No orthogonal path on the wiring grid could be found between the two ports of a connection. Usual causes: a redundant conductor between two points already on one net (rewire to a point already routed), or crowded geometry around the ports. ROUTE_NEAR_FLAG_STUB INFO render note No path kept a wire off every link marker's stub, rail and branch (layout-0243), so it was drawn in the old room, which ignores that ink. It may touch another net's marker. The message names the page and the wire. Send the smallest model that shows it: Fransys could not draw this cleanly. ROUTE_SHORTS_NETS ERROR render Fransys A drawn route touches a port of another physical net, or two routes of different physical nets touch on the page. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. Check first that no authored hint crowds the nets. ROUTE_WRONG_PORT ERROR render Fransys A route does not run between the two ports it claims to join. A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. SHEET_FORMAT_UNUSED WARNING render consumer An authored sheet format is named by no layout profile, so pages use the house sheet (or the profile's format). Name it in the layout profile, or remove it. STUBS_NOT_STACKED INFO render note Leaving-line stubs of one page whose texts meet found no free staircase (layout-0256): the room, a shape or another line was in the way. They stay as drawn and their texts overlap. The message names the page. Move a unit or cable so the lines leave apart, or send the smallest model showing it. SYMBOL_DEFAULTED INFO render note A function matched no symbol rule or choice, so it was drawn as a plain labelled box. Add a symbol rule or choice for the function's kind or category if a real symbol is wanted. SYMBOL_OVERLAP INFO render Fransys The keep-out boxes of two symbols on one page overlap. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model SYMBOL_PORT_MISSING ERROR render consumer A model port matches no port on its drawn symbol by any of the three binding rules. Fix the part's port names, or add a port_map/symbol choice. TEXT_CROSSED_BY_ROUTE INFO render Fransys A link marker's stub runs through a text box (a label or another marker's box). Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model TEXT_OVERLAP INFO render Fransys Two texts on a page overlap, or a text overlaps a symbol body it does not belong to. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model TEXT_TOO_SMALL WARNING render consumer A layout profile's text_height_mm is under its min_text_height_mm. Once per profile; nothing is shrunk or grown. Raise text_height_mm, or lower min_text_height_mm if the small text is intended (Drawing well). TITLE_BLOCK_NOTICE_OVERFLOW WARNING render consumer The notice text passed to fr.document(notice=) does not fit the notice cell and would be cut. Shorten the notice text in fr.document(notice=). TITLE_BLOCK_NO_ROOM WARNING render consumer The sheet format's title-block band is under the required 20mm, or its title block is under the required 97.5mm wide. Use a sheet format with a taller title-block band or a wider sheet. TITLE_BLOCK_STACK_OVERLAP ERROR render consumer The profile's text height needs a taller title-block band than the sheet format has, so a title-block label overlaps its value. Use a sheet format whose title-block band is at least the named height, or the house text height. TITLE_BLOCK_TEXT_OVERFLOW WARNING render consumer A one-line title-block field (title, number, customer, revision, date, author, page title, scope or sheet counter) does not fit its cell. Shorten the text; for a page title, set a shorter one with d.layout.page_title. UNIT_GROUP_SPLIT WARNING render consumer A unit group is wider than one page, so layout split it; each page keeps an outline for its own interfaces. Even the edges with side hints (d.layout.side), or give the unit fewer harness interfaces. UNKNOWN_SYMBOL_KEY ERROR render consumer A placement's symbol key is not in the installed symbol library. Fix the symbol key (rule, choice, or part data), or install a library version with it. WIDER_THAN_PAGE WARNING render consumer A row of columns is wider than the page even at its closest spacing. Shorten the row, lower the column count of the block, raise the page width or set Options.short_height (Drawing well). WIRE_NOT_ORTHOGONAL INFO render Fransys A drawn route has a non-orthogonal segment (not purely horizontal or vertical). Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model WIRE_OVER_LABEL INFO render Fransys A drawn route runs through a label's (or link marker's) box. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model WIRE_THROUGH_SYMBOL INFO render Fransys A drawn route runs through the keep-out box of a symbol it does not end at. Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model

items.title: Finding codes: validators, build and release
items.text:
Codes the model checks, the build, release and verify and the library load emit. Who acts is explained in findings.md.

Code Severity Stage Who acts Meaning Fix ASPECT_CROSS_PARENT ERROR validators consumer An aspect node's parent belongs to a different aspect (function, location or product). Move the node under a parent of the same aspect, or fix its authored parent. ASPECT_CYCLE ERROR validators consumer An aspect node's parent chain loops back on itself. Correct the parent authored on one of the looping nodes. BAR_NOT_PE ERROR validators consumer A port of a bar function has a role other than pe. A bar carries protective earth only, until the copper bar drawing (owner question) is ruled. Set role = "pe" on the port in the part file. BASELINE_DIFFERS ERROR release, verify consumer A unit instance in the released subtree, or checked by verify, has a listing differing from its released baseline. Release the nested unit's new revision, then the containing unit again, or find why its content changed. BASELINE_ROWS_UNCHECKED INFO or ERROR release, verify consumer A stored baseline cut before fransys 0.18.2 holds rows for a contact block that today's numbering cannot print. Every other row is unchanged, and those rows were left out of the comparison. verify notes it (INFO); release of a unit nesting it refuses (ERROR). Run fr.rebaseline(result, baselines), which records them under today's rules. BASELINE_RULES_MOVED INFO or ERROR release, verify consumer A stored baseline's content is unchanged, but a later fransys prints its listing differently. verify notes it (INFO); release of a unit nesting it refuses (ERROR). Run fr.rebaseline(result, baselines), which re-cuts it under today's rules. BASELINE_TOO_OLD ERROR release, verify consumer A stored baseline was cut by a fransys older than the oldest release whose listing rules this build knows, or its manifest records no fransys version. verify with the fransys release that cut this baseline, or release a new revision of the unit, which stores a baseline under today's rules. BOUNDARY_NOT_IN_UNIT ERROR validators consumer A unit's boundary function belongs to an item outside that unit's subtree. Declare the boundary on a function whose item is in the unit, or fix the item's unit/parent. BOUNDARY_UNCONNECTED ERROR validators consumer A unit's boundary function is not connected across the unit nor declared unused. Wire the boundary, or leave it open: unused= on d.add for one instance, on d.device for all. A unit alone in its design never fires it, nor an interface passed up from a nested unit. CABLE_CORE_COUNT WARNING or ERROR validators consumer A cable item's core count differs from its product's core-colour count (WARNING when fewer, ERROR when more). Wire the missing cores, mark a core you leave unused with w.spare(colour) (or w.spare() for all the rest), or correct the product's core_colours list. A spare or one-ended screen counts as a core. CHANGES_BY_NAME INFO build note The release the next change list starts from was cut before listing version 2, so it names no item key. The change list matches by printed designation, and a renamed item shows as one removed and one added row. The next release's change list follows renames; fr.rebaseline re-cuts the old release now. CONDUCTOR_ON_UNINSTALLED WARNING validators consumer A conductor lands on an item that is not marked installed. Mark the item installed, or remove the conductor if it is absent. CONNECTOR_WIRED_WITHOUT_MATE WARNING validators consumer A conductor from outside a nested unit lands directly on its boundary connector, whose part gender is male or female (neutral or unstated passes). Mate a plug to the boundary connector (u.mate(plug, connector)) and wire the plug's pin instead. CONTAINMENT_CYCLE ERROR validators consumer An item's physical-containment parent chain loops back on itself. Correct the parent authored on one of the looping items. CORE_INDEX_PAST_PRODUCT ERROR validators consumer A cable core is numbered past the core count of the cable's product. Use a core from 1 to the product's core count, or choose a part with more cores. DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE ERROR build consumer Two items or unit instances under one parent print one designation: a tag equal to a sibling's text, or a retired or moved released one. Give the item a distinct tag, or none. A tag a released revision reserved needs a new version. DESIGNATION_MOVED ERROR release consumer An item or unit instance pinned in the previous release now prints a different designation, written or numbered. Restore the released tag; only a new version may change it. DESIGNATION_NEW_IN_REVISION INFO build, release note A new untagged item or unit instance took the next free number in a later revision. Nothing is wrong; tag it if its number must stay fixed. DOCUMENT_UNIT_UNRESOLVED ERROR validators consumer A document's unit_name matches no unit, or more than one. Make the unit name unique so unit_name resolves to one instance. EXPORT_NAME_CLASH ERROR build consumer Two different subjects (documents, items) would write to the same file name in out_dir. Give the colliding units, items or documents distinct names (or locations/fragments); two instances of one release name need one document per release. FILE_UNREADABLE ERROR library load consumer A part-file could not be read (missing file, permission error, or bad encoding). Fix the path, permissions or encoding (UTF-8). FLOAT_FORBIDDEN ERROR library load consumer A part-file has a bare TOML float, which the contract forbids (quote values as strings). Quote the numeric value as a string. FUNCTION_HALF_CONNECTED WARNING validators consumer A two-port coil, load, contact, switch, protection or actuator is connected at one port and open at the other. Wire the open port, or remove the half-wired function. GNYE_NOT_PE ERROR or WARNING validators consumer A green-yellow conductor is on a net that is not PE: an ERROR on a net a declared net lists, a WARNING on a net none lists (IEC 60445 keeps green-yellow for PE). Recolour it, or connect it to the PE net and declare it with d.earth. HARNESS_END_AMBIGUOUS ERROR build consumer Two or more ends of one cable print the same text in its drawing. Place the colliding unit instances at distinct locations, or tag the strips apart. HARNESS_HOLDS_PLC_MODULE ERROR validators consumer A PLC module sits under an item made with d.harness. Build the rack with d.rack, so its modules print flat. HARNESS_WITHOUT_TAG ERROR validators consumer A harness (marked, or with a cable child) has no tag or assigned designation, so it has no label. Give it a tag: d.harness(tag=...), or tag= on the item. INTERFACE_NOT_BUMPED ERROR release consumer The previous released revision of this unit (the highest below this one) has the same interface string but a different boundary. Bump the interface string if the boundary changed, or restore the previous boundary. ITEM_PART_MISMATCH ERROR validators consumer An item's functions or ports do not match its part's templates (missing, extra, duplicated, or differing in name, kind, role or marking). Fix the item's authored functions and ports (or the part's templates) so they agree. ITEM_WITHOUT_PART INFO validators note A non-external item has no part, so its functions are authored directly, not checked against templates. Usually nothing to fix: assign a part to check against templates. LOADS_ABOVE_LIMIT WARNING validators consumer The loads one limit bounds sum above it; none is above it alone. If they run together, raise the limit or split the loads. LOAD_ABOVE_LIMIT ERROR validators consumer A load's stated draw is above the limit that bounds it. Lower the draw or raise the limit. MATE_NOT_CONNECTOR ERROR validators consumer A mate end is not a connector or terminal (a relay coil, say). Mate a connector or terminal. MATE_PORT_MISMATCH WARNING validators consumer A mate's two functions have different port names, so some ports have no counterpart. Example: a lettered inlet (L1, L2, L3, N, PE) mated to a numbered plug. Rename the ports to match. MULTILINE_STRING ERROR library load consumer A part-file string contains a line break, which the contract forbids. Use a single-line string, or TOML's escaped \n. NET_POTENTIAL_CONFLICT ERROR validators consumer One physical net joins two declared nets that are rails of different supply potentials. Fix the wiring or net declarations so no net joins two potentials. NET_SHORTED ERROR validators consumer One physical net joins declared nets of different names. Fix the wiring, or give the nets one name if they are one signal (same-name nets join silently). NET_UNREALISED WARNING validators consumer A declared net's ports fall into more than one physical net, and no single board holds them all. Not for the PE net. Wire the missing conductors, or remove the ports that should not share the declared net. PART_LIBRARY_VERSION_CONFLICT ERROR library load consumer Two PartLibrary records share a name but declare different versions. Load only one version of each named part library. PE_NOT_GNYE WARNING validators consumer A single wire on a PE net is not green-yellow (an empty colour is not a finding). Colour the wire GNYE. PE_PORT_OFF_PE WARNING validators consumer A port with role PE is on a net that is not PE. Wire the port to the PE net. PLACEMENT_DUPLICATE ERROR validators consumer One item is placed more than once in the same aspect (function, location or product). Remove the duplicate placement so the item is placed once per aspect. PLC_BINDING_SIGNAL_MISMATCH ERROR validators consumer A PLC binding's channel does not have the signal type the request asked for (or is not a declared channel at all). The message names the asked kind, the channel, its kind and both fixes. Rewire the request to a channel of the asked kind, or ask for the channel's kind. PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH ERROR validators consumer A PLC binding disagrees with the wiring: the request or channel function is wired to a different channel or request than its binding. Rebind the request/channel to match the wiring, or rewire it to match the binding. PLC_CHANNEL_CONTESTED ERROR build consumer Two or more PLC requests of the channel's signal are wired to the same channel. The finding names the channel's pins and every request; none of them binds, and none goes to the free queue. One channel reads one signal: keep one request, or wire each request to its own channel. PLC_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS ERROR build consumer A PLC request is wired so that several free channels of its signal tie: its net reaches them all, or all by a direct conductor. It gets no binding. Wire the request to one channel directly, or free the other channels. PLC_REQUEST_UNSERVABLE ERROR build consumer No free PLC channel of the requested signal type on the request's unit chain (its unit declares none, or every one is taken).
