Add a channel of that signal type to the unit (or a parent unit), or move another request off one. PORT_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE ERROR build consumer Two or more ports of one item print the same designation text, so a drawing or list cannot tell them apart. Give the part's pin markings distinct names so each port prints a unique text. POTENTIAL_IN_TWO_SUPPLIES ERROR validators consumer One potential name is a rail of two differently named supplies. Rename one of the potentials, or merge the two supply declarations if they are the same supply. POTENTIAL_WITHOUT_SUPPLY WARNING validators consumer A net potential no supply declares: its pins get no rank and no power symbol. Declare the supply with that rail. PRODUCT_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE ERROR build consumer Two items print the same product designation (location plus own label): both at one location or, unplaced, both unnumbered alike in one unit instance. Place one item at a distinct location, or tag it. RATING_BREAKING_BELOW_FAULT ERROR validators consumer A protective device breaks less current than the prospective fault at its position. Fit a higher-breaking device. RATING_BREAKING_NO_DATA WARNING validators consumer A device states breaking points, but none covers the circuit voltage or time constant. Add a point for that voltage or time constant. RATING_CURRENT_BELOW_BRANCH ERROR validators consumer A function's rated current is below the current its branch can carry. Fit a part rated for the branch's current, or reduce the limit that sets the bound. RATING_CURRENT_KIND_UNSTATED WARNING validators consumer A function's part states a voltage rating for AC or for DC only, and the function stands on rails of the other current kind. State the missing voltage rating in the part, or use a part rated for that kind. RATING_VOLTAGE_BELOW_CIRCUIT ERROR validators consumer A function's rated voltage is below the voltage that stands across it. Fit a part rated for the circuit's voltage, or change the supply or wiring to lower it. REFERENCE_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE ERROR build consumer Two items in the function or location aspect print the same full reference designation (e.g. two unit instances at one location). Place one of them at a distinct location so the designations differ. RELEASE_FILE_CHANGED ERROR verify consumer A released file's hash differs, the folder holds a file its manifest omits, or the manifest does not parse. A CRLF-only change in a text file passes. Restore the file from version control; a released revision never changes. RELEASE_FILE_MISSING ERROR verify consumer A file its manifest lists, or the manifest itself, is gone from a release folder. Restore it from version control. RELEASE_HISTORY_UNRELEASED ERROR release consumer A history entry after the first released one names a revision with no folder under into, in its own version. Remove the entry, or release that revision first. Older entries are free text. RELEASE_NESTED_UNRELEASED ERROR release consumer A unit anywhere in the subtree being released (not only direct children) has no baseline folder yet. Release that nested unit first, then release the containing unit. RELEASE_NO_HISTORY ERROR release consumer The revision being released has no matching Revision history entry. Add the missing entry: history= on @fr.unit, or Design.revision(...) for a system release. REVISION_ALREADY_RELEASED ERROR release consumer The unit (or system) being released already has a baseline folder whose listing differs from the one to be written. Bump the version or revision, or find why a frozen revision changed. REVISION_CURRENT_MISSING ERROR validators consumer A unit's (or the project's) current revision has no matching Revision history entry, so a title block prints no date. Add the missing entry: history= on @fr.unit, or Design.revision(rev, date=, text=, created=). REVISION_DATE_FORMAT ERROR validators consumer A revision entry's date is not in YYYY-MM-DD format. Rewrite the date as YYYY-MM-DD. REVISION_INITIALS_MISSING ERROR validators consumer A revision entry has no created (author initials). Add the author's initials to the revision entry's created field. SIDE_HINT_NO_HARNESS_LINE WARNING build consumer A d.layout.side hint names an interface that has no harness line, so the hint does nothing. Remove the hint, or connect the interface through a harness line. STRIP_WITHOUT_TAG ERROR validators consumer A part-less top-level item, usually a floating strip, has no tag and no class code (no terminals, or disagreeing ones). Give it a part, a tag, or terminals of one class code. SUPPLY_DIFFERS ERROR validators consumer Two declarations of one supply name disagree in current, earthing or rails, or two source declarations in fault current or time constant. Make them agree, or give the differing declarations distinct names. TOML_INVALID ERROR library load consumer A part-file is not valid TOML. Fix the TOML syntax error named. UNIT_BOUNDARY_BYPASSED ERROR validators consumer A conductor or mate crosses out of a unit at a function that is not declared that unit's boundary. Declare it the unit's boundary, or route it through an existing boundary function. UNIT_CYCLE ERROR validators consumer A unit's parent chain loops back on itself. Correct the parent authored on one of the looping units. UNUSED_CONTRADICTED WARNING validators consumer A boundary declared unused names a function that is no unit's boundary, or is connected across the unit the declaration is on. Remove unused= if the function is wired, or fix the unit/function it names. WIRE_COLOUR_UNKNOWN ERROR validators consumer A wire or cable-product core colour is not a recognized IEC 60757 colour code (or combination). Use a base code, a combination of two, a base code with a core number, or shield code SH. WIRE_ON_TWO_HARNESSES ERROR validators consumer A wire joins plugs of two harnesses. Wire to a plug of one harness, or use a cable. WIRE_ROW_UNRESOLVED ERROR build consumer A series or detail wire was written without a row, and at build end its net carries no rail of its unit, states no source_row and holds no PLC channel signal, or carries rails of two rows. The message names the net and the wire's two pins. Give wire= on that series: a (colour, size), or a size with a row table. A rail never reaches a wire across a unit boundary from its container.
path: Finding codes: validators, build and release

items.title: Finding codes
items.text:
Every code Fransys can emit, with severity, stage, who acts, meaning and fix, on five pages by source.

A finding's message names each thing as the drawings print it. An item reads as its designation, a port as its port designation, a wire as its ends and a tagged unit as the word unit and its tag, unit -U1. A unit with no tag reads as its name and revision alone, as its title block prints them. A thing with no printed text reads as its kind alone. A message never prints a name= key or an Id. A renamed key changes no message (decision overview-0003).

"Who acts" is one of four. consumer: change your design as the fix says. part author: the part library's author fixes the part file as the fix says. Fransys: a defect in layout or an output, so send the smallest model that shows it. note: nothing is wrong.

  • findings-validators.md: the model checks, the build, release, verify and the library load.
  • findings-render.md: layout and the drawing stage.
  • findings-pdf.md: the PDF output.
  • findings-kicad.md: the KiCad import.
  • findings-parts.md: the part-file lint.

items.title: Harnesses
items.text: This page teaches how to add a harness to a design with d.harness, and how its cables and plugs print. It follows authoring.md, which holds the rest of the authoring calls.

items.title: Add a harness
items.text: d.harness("W5") adds a part-less harness item and returns its handle, which a document can take as its subject (see documents.md). A harness holding a cable needs a tag: d.harness(name="loom") with no tag builds, then fails with HARNESS_WITHOUT_TAG. A part-less harness holding exactly one cable prints that cable as its own designation (-W5, its cores -W5:1); its plugs stay -W5-J1. With two cables they print -W5-W1 and -W5-W2. A harness with one cable prints the cable with the harness's designation. The cable's own tag is not printed.

items.title: Wires on a harness
items.text: d.harness("W1") marks the item as a harness, so plugs and plain wires need no cable. A wire with an end on a plug of W1 is a wire of W1: fransys.derive.harness_wires(model, w1_id) lists its rows. A wire between plugs of two harnesses is the ERROR WIRE_ON_TWO_HARNESSES. A cable beside a wire prints -W1-W1; a cable that is the whole harness prints -W1. A harness of plain wires draws on a harness drawing as one block, with its end boxes and one line per wire, and no cable box.

items.title: Fit a housing on a part's leads
items.text: d.device("J1", "DEMO-HSG-4F", parent=k1, joins={"1": k1.coil["A1"], 2: k1.coil["A2"]}) fits the housing on the leads of K1. Each pair joins a pin of the new device to a pin of K1, with no wire and no cable (a LEAD link). The housing prints -K1-J1. joins= needs a parent device and refuses a pin twice or a pin of another device with an AuthorError.

items.title: Add crimp contacts
items.text:
d.device("P1", "DEMO-HSG-4M", parent=w1, contacts="DEMO-CRIMP-M") fits that contact part in every used pin of a connector item: a plug, a housing, or any part with a connector function. A mapping gives mixed contacts: contacts={"1": "DEMO-CRIMP-M", "2": "DEMO-CRIMP-F"}.

A used pin is one where a wire or a core lands. The BOM gets one line per contact part. Its count is the used pins, and its designations are the housings, so one more wire adds one contact. contacts= on a part with no connector function, an unknown pin name or an unknown part raises AuthorError, and the call adds nothing. The contact part is a part file with no function.

items.title: Read a harness line's texts
items.text:
A cable or harness draws as a harness line when its line carries two or more conductors, cores and single wires together. A cable on a harness answers for its harness. Read the conductors from fr.derive.conductors.

fransys.derive.harness_line_ends(model, subject) returns one HarnessLineEnd per end of a harness or cable line. It holds branch (the n of -W13.n), plug or ports, and the function plug mates. Cable ends and single-wire ends merge into one order, plugs first by designation. Read the branch number from it; never number ends yourself.

fr.derive.line_designation(model, harness, branch) prints -W13 between two ends and -W13.n on a branch of three or more. A leaving line prints one stub, -W3 → +EXT-M1 p2:4A: the line designation, then each far device with where it is drawn in the same drawing set. A one-conductor cable keeps the per-core form. A schematic page prints no wire label but a harness line's designation (-W13), with one leg per wire where no plug stands. line_designation takes the unit of the document that prints it: on a unit's own document no text names that unit's tag.

items.title: Keywords of the d calls
items.text:
This page has one table for each d.* and d.detail.* call: each named keyword, its default, its effect and an example fragment. A call that takes only *args has no table, and one sentence says what it takes.

place= is the same on every call that takes it: the place= table in authoring.md says what it changes. The fr.* functions are in keywords-output.md, the handle methods and layout hints in keywords-handles.md.

items.title: d.device
items.text: keyword default effect example tag required The printed tag, bare and with no lowercase letter. None numbers the device from its class code and needs name=. d.device("Q1", P.Q) part required A part class or an MPN string. None makes an external=True box of pins=, with a tag and no BOM line. d.device("Q1", "DEMO-MCB-3P") pins None Names the pins of a part-less box (part=None); each is an attribute too, ext.U as ext["U"]. Ignored for a real part. d.device("A1", None, pins=("1", "2"), external=True) place ... Where the device stands. See the place= table in authoring.md. d.device("Q1", P.Q, place="HOLD") parent None The device, strip or cable that holds this one. An accessory prints its holder's designation and uses no number. d.device("J1", P.HSG, parent=k1) name None The key a released number holds to. A floating device, with tag=None, raises without it. d.device(None, P.Q, name="main-breaker") interface False Marks the device's functions as the unit's boundary: True marks all, a tuple of function names marks those. d.device("X1", P.CONN, interface=True) unused False Marks functions as unused, so no unused-pin finding is raised for them: True marks all, a tuple marks those. d.device("X1", P.CONN, unused=("x2",)) mounted_on None Mounts the device on a carrier device or function, as a contactor on a protective switch. The carrier's load pins join this device's line pins pole by pole. d.device("K1", P.CTR, mounted_on=q1) joins None Maps the housing's pins to the parent's pins. A housing fitted on a parent's own leads joins them with no wire. Needs parent= to be a device. d.device("J1", P.HSG, parent=k1, joins={1: k1.coil["A1"]}) description '' Text for the designation list in place of the part's description. Empty falls back to the part's. d.device("Q1", P.Q, description="Pump breaker") position None The physical order within the parent, such as the slot of a PLC module or a place on a rail. It orders the rack and the lists. d.device("A2", P.DI8, parent=rack, position=2) installed True False keeps the device in drawings and reservations but drops it from the BOM. d.device("Q9", P.Q, installed=False) external False True marks the device as supplied by others: no BOM line, and every drawing marks it dashed "(by others)". d.device("M1", P.MOTOR, external=True) contacts None Fits a contact part in every pin of a housing, or a mapping of pin name to part for mixed contacts. d.device("P1", P.HSG, parent=w1, contacts="DEMO-CRIMP-M")

items.title: d.terminal_strip
items.text: keyword default effect example tag required The printed tag. None numbers the strip and needs name=. d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, 10) part required The terminal part. None makes part-less terminals with only .outer, and needs external=True. d.terminal_strip("X9", None, external=True) count None The number of terminals. X1[3] takes terminal 3 and makes it on first use. d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, count=10) name None The key a released number holds to. A floating strip, with tag=None, raises without it. d.terminal_strip(None, P.TB, name="field") description '' Text for the strip in the designation list. Empty falls back to the part's. d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, description="Field strip") place ... Where the strip stands. See the place= table in authoring.md. d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, place="HOLD") pe None The part of the strip's protective-earth terminals. A run labelled "PE" takes it, and raises without one. d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5") interface False Marks terminals as the unit's boundary: True marks all, a tuple of terminal numbers marks those. d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, 4, interface=(1, 2)) unused False Marks terminals as unused: True marks all, a tuple of terminal numbers marks those. d.terminal_strip("X1", P.TB, 4, unused=(3, 4)) bridged False Bridges plain terminals with jumpers: True bridges all, (first, last) a range, a tuple of ranges several. d.terminal_strip("X4", P.TB, 6, bridged=(2, 6)) external False True flags the strip and its terminals as supplied by others. d.terminal_strip("X9", P.TB, 4, external=True)

items.title: d.cable
items.text: keyword default effect example tag required The printed tag. None numbers the cable and needs name=. d.cable("W1", P.CBL) part required The cable part. Its cores come from the part. d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5") length_m None The length in metres, stored as whole millimetres. It prints in the cable list. None leaves the length out. d.cable("W1", P.CBL, length_m=5) place ... Where the cable stands. See the place= table in authoring.md. d.cable("W1", P.CBL, place="HOLD") parent None The harness that holds the cable. d.cable("W5", P.CBL, parent=h1) name None The key a released number holds to. A floating cable, with tag=None, raises without it. d.cable(None, P.CBL, name="motor-cable") external False True flags the cable as supplied by others. Its cores carry no flag. d.cable("W1", P.CBL, external=True)

items.title: d.add
items.text: keyword default effect example definition required The unit made by fr.unit. The call builds it as an instance and returns the unit function's result. u1 = d.add(board, "U1") tag required The instance's printed tag, bare and capitals. None numbers it from the unit's class code and needs name=. d.add(board, "U1") place ... Where the instance stands. See the place= table in authoring.md. d.add(board, "U1", place="HOLD") name None The identity a released number holds to. A floating add raises without it. d.add(board, None, name="module1") unused () Names interface fields or functions the instance leaves unused, such as "X1" or "X1.x1". d.add(board, "U1", unused=("X1.x1",))

items.title: d.ac_supply
items.text:
d.ac_supply(name, voltage, *phases, ...) takes the phase pins in phase order as phases: one or three.

keyword default effect example name required The supply's name. Its rails are ac.L1 and so on. d.ac_supply("230V", 230, x0[1], n=x0[2]) voltage required Each phase's RMS voltage to the star point. It is not read from a part. d.ac_supply("400V", 400, q1["L1"], q1["L2"], q1["L3"]) n None The neutral pin. A series joins N only where an element has a pole for it. n=q1["N"] names None Renames the potentials: one name per phase pin in order, then one for n. The rails keep their ac.L1 names. names=("A", "B", "C") earthing fr.EARTHED fr.IT declares a floating supply. earthing=fr.IT fault_current_a None The prospective fault current in amps, positive. The supply becomes a source for the breaking-capacity check. fault_current_a=10000

items.title: d.dc_supply
items.text: keyword default effect example name required The supply's name. Its rails are dc.plus and dc.minus. d.dc_supply("24VDC", psu.output) source None A device or function whose L+ and L- pins and nominal voltage are the supply. With none, plus, minus and voltage are required. d.dc_supply("24VDC", g1.output) plus None The plus pin, with no source. plus=x1[1] minus None The minus pin, with no source. minus=x1[2] mid None A middle conductor. With it, mid is 0 V and plus and minus are plus and minus the voltage. mid=x1[3] voltage None The voltage, required with no source or a source whose part states none. voltage=24 names None Renames the potentials, in the order plus, minus, mid. names=("P24", "M24") earthing fr.EARTHED fr.IT declares a floating supply. earthing=fr.IT fault_current_a None The prospective fault current in amps, positive. A source refuses it, since the part states its own. fault_current_a=500 fault_time_constant_ms None The fault time constant in milliseconds, positive. A source refuses it. fault_time_constant_ms=5

items.title: d.earth
items.text: d.earth(*pins) takes the pins to join to protective earth, one PE net. It has no named keyword, and a terminal lands on its inner side. Example: d.earth(x1[3], q1["PE"]).

items.title: d.function
items.text: keyword default effect example name required The function block's name, printed =name. The devices made inside the with block belong to it, which sets their designation; the d.series a function is written in sets where it draws. with d.function("RUN", "Pump run"): text required The block's description. It prints on the pages that draw the block. with d.function("RUN", "Pump run"):

items.title: d.location
items.text: keyword default effect example name required The place's bare tag, printed +name. d.location("HOLD", "Engine hold") text required The place's description. d.location("HOLD", "Engine hold") within None The outer place, which must exist. The place then prints +outer+name. None puts it at the root. d.location("BATT", "Batteries", within="HOLD")

items.title: d.harness
items.text: keyword default effect example tag None The part-less harness's printed tag. None numbers it and needs name=. d.harness("H1") name None The key a released number holds to. d.harness(None, name="main-loom") place ... Where the harness stands. None gives it no place. See the place= table in authoring.md. d.harness("H1", place=None) external False True flags the harness as supplied by others. d.harness("H1", external=True)

items.title: d.rack
items.text: keyword default effect example tag required The part-less PLC rack's printed tag. Modules go under it with parent=. d.rack("U1") name None The key a released number holds to. d.rack("U1", name="plc") place ... Where the rack stands. None gives it no place. See the place= table in authoring.md. d.rack("U1", place="HOLD") external False True flags the rack as supplied by others. d.rack("U1", external=True)

items.title: d.mate
items.text: keyword default effect example a required The connector to plug in: a device with one function, or that function. d.mate(j1, j2) b required The connector a plugs into. d.mate(j1, j2)

items.title: d.series
items.text:
d.series(*elements, ...) takes the elements to wire end to end, each one's load to the next one's line. A pin or a tuple of one device's pins starts or ends it (keywords-handles.md).

keyword default effect example wire None The wire of every pole: a size, a table of rows that replaces only those rows, one (colour, size), or a tuple of them, one per pole in pole order and as long as the series is wide. None uses the rows' defaults, and a row with no size is WIRE_ROW_UNRESOLVED. A series through a cable whose part has a core table needs no wire=. d.series(dc.plus, k1.aux, h1.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75)); d.series(x1[1:4], q1.element, wire=((BN, 1.5), (BK, 1.5), (GY, 1.5)))

items.title: d.pair
items.text:
d.pair(a, cable, b) joins two ends through a cable pin for pin: core i runs from a's pin i to b's pin i, with no line or load direction. It takes no keyword: the cores are the wires.

keyword default effect example a required The first end: terminals (x8[1:3], x8[1]; their field side), a function (b1.sig, its pins in connector order), or pins: one (b1.sig[1]) or a tuple (b1.sig.pins[:2]), as d.series reads them. x8[1:3] cable required The cable between the ends, from d.cable. w3 b required The second end, with as many pins as a. A strip or a device raises. b1.sig

Example: d.pair(x8[1:3], w3, b1.sig).

items.title: d.parallel
items.text: d.parallel(*members) takes the members to group, so a series puts each between the previous load and the next line. It has no named keyword and connects nothing alone. Example: d.series(dc.plus, d.parallel(h1.lamp, h2.lamp), dc.minus).

items.title: d.poles
items.text:
d.poles(*functions, ...) takes one-pole contacts of one device, in pole order, as one element drawn multi-pole. It wires nothing: a series wires the group.

keyword default effect example selector False True turns a changeover group's throws to the line side, so a series enters at the throws and leaves at the commons, and the group draws turned. False keeps the line at the commons. It raises on a part that already states a selector, and on a group that is not changeovers. q = d.poles(k1.co_1, k1.co_2, k1.co_3, selector=True)

items.title: d.project
items.text: keyword default effect example title required The project title. It prints in every document's title block. d.project(title="Pump", ...) number required The drawing number, printed in the title block. number="DC-1" customer required The customer, printed in the title block. customer="Demo Ltd" revision required The current revision, an integer from 1. Its date is that of the matching d.revision entry. revision=2 author required The author. A project document's Author cell prints it. author="AB" notice None Not accepted: passing it raises AuthorError. The notice moved to fr.document(notice=). fr.document(preset, None, cover=c, notice="...") version 1 The project's release version. d.revision without version= writes entries of it. Set it before any d.revision. version=2

items.title: d.revision
items.text: keyword default effect example revision required The revision number of this history entry. d.revision(1, date="2026-01-01", text="first", created="AB") date required The entry's date. The title block shows it for the current revision. date="2026-01-01" text required What the revision changed. text="first issue" created required Who made the revision. created="AB" checked '' Who checked it. Empty leaves the field empty. checked="CD" approved '' Who approved it. Empty leaves the field empty. approved="EF" version None The version the entry belongs to. None takes the project's version, or 1 before d.project. version=2

items.title: d.rating
items.text: keyword default effect example part required A part class or MPN string. An MPN made by two makers raises. d.rating("DEMO-MCB-3P") function None A function template of the part. None reads the part's own rating. d.rating("DEMO-MCB-3P", "main")

items.title: d.operating
items.text: keyword default effect example part required A part class or MPN string. An MPN made by two makers raises. d.operating("DEMO-PSU-24", "output") function required The function template whose operating envelope is read. Returns None if the part states none. d.operating("DEMO-PSU-24", "output")

items.title: d.draft
items.text: d.draft() takes nothing. It returns the records written so far, and it does not freeze them or merge the library: fr.build does both.

items.title: d.detail.wire
items.text:
d.detail.wire(*pins, ...) takes the pins to wire: two make one wire, more make a daisy chain.

keyword default effect example wire None The wire as (colour, size), a size, or a table of rows, as d.series reads it, except a per-pole tuple. d.detail.wire(x1[1], h1[1], wire=(BU, 0.75)) label None Text printed on the wire. None prints none. label="L1" n None n=2 draws a second wire in parallel between the same two pins. None draws one. n=2

items.title: d.detail.star
items.text:
d.detail.star(src, targets, ...) wires src to each of targets, a tuple or list: one wire per target, none between targets.

keyword default effect example src required The pin every wire starts at. A strip stands for one terminal, shared by all targets. d.detail.star(x2[17].outer, (x7[1], x7[4])) targets required A tuple or list of the pins to wire to. One target is d.detail.wire(src, target). (x7[1], x7[4], x7[7]) wire None The wire as (colour, size), a size, or a table of rows, as d.detail.wire reads it. d.detail.star(x2[17].outer, (x7[1], x7[4]), wire=(BU, 0.75))

items.title: d.detail.net
items.text:
d.detail.net(name, *pins, ...) takes the pins the net spans as pins.

keyword default effect example name required The net's name. It prints on the net in the drawings and the wire list. d.detail.net("CAN", a[1], b[1]) kind fr.CONTROL The NetClass of the net. It cannot make a PE or POWER net, which earth and supplies own. d.detail.net("CAN", a[1], b[1], kind=fr.SIGNAL)

items.title: d.detail.busbar
items.text: keyword default effect example a required The first pin of the busbar, a conductor of kind bus. d.detail.busbar(x1[1], x1[2]) b required The second pin. The same pin twice raises. d.detail.busbar(x1[1], x1[2])

items.title: d.detail.rail_bond
items.text: keyword default effect example a required The first pin of the bond, a conductor of kind rail. d.detail.rail_bond(x1[1], x1[2]) b required The second pin, of the same rail. The same pin twice raises. d.detail.rail_bond(x1[1], x1[2])

items.title: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints
items.text:
This page has one table for each handle method and each d.layout.* hint: each named keyword, its default, its effect and an example fragment. A call that takes only *args has no table, and one sentence says what it takes.

The design calls are in keywords-design.md, the fr.* functions in keywords-output.md. d.layout.profile and d.layout.sheet keep their tables in layout-numbers.md.
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Fn.plc
items.text: keyword default effect example signal required The fr.SignalType of the PLC channel this function needs, such as fr.DI. It picks the channel kind allocated. k1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run") name required The channel's name. It prints in the PLC lists and on the channel's address. k1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run") priority 0 A lower number is served first when channels are short. Ties go by the requesting function's key, then its id. k1.coil.plc(fr.DO, "pump-run", priority=1)
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Fn.pole
items.text:
fn.pole(n) takes one pole number, counted from 1 in pole order, and gives that one pole of the function as a series element: d.series(s1.main.pole(2), f2.element, wire=(BK, 1.5)).

A pin, or a tuple of one device's pins, is a series element at the start or the end only. First, its pins are the load ends: d.series(k1.coil["A1"], a1.di_1, wire=(BK, 1.0)) leaves from A1, where d.series(k1.coil, a1.di_1) leaves from A2. Last, they are the line ends. In the middle a pin raises; use d.detail.wire.

fn.pins is the function's pins as a typed tuple in the connector list's order (1, 2, 10, A1): a.pins[i] is the i-th pin from 0, and a loop over it types as fr.Pin.
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Fn.scale
items.text: keyword default effect example unit required The engineering unit of the scaled value. It prints in the PLC list. ai.scale("bar", (0, 27648), (0, 10)) raw required The raw range as two integers. raw=(0, 27648) eng required The engineering range as two strings or Decimals. Floats are refused. eng=("0", "10")
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Fn.limits
items.text: keyword default effect example rating None The rating the unit states about this boundary function. None states none. q1.line.limits(rating=r) operating None The operating envelope the unit states about this boundary function. None states none. q1.line.limits(operating=o)
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Terminal.limits
items.text: keyword default effect example rating None The rating the unit states about this terminal. None states none. The terminal must be in a unit. x1[1].limits(rating=r) operating None The operating envelope the unit states about this terminal. None states none. Giving neither value raises. x1[1].limits(operating=o)
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: TerminalStrip.run
items.text:
keyword default effect example label required The run's label. It prints on each terminal of the run. A run labelled "PE" takes the strip's pe= part. x1.run("24V", 4) count None The number of terminals in the run. With none, the run is bridged and grows as it is used. x1.run("24V", 4) bridged False Bridges the run's terminals with jumpers: True bridges all, (first, last) bridges a range. x1.run("24V", 4, bridged=True) interface False Marks the run's terminals as the unit's boundary: True marks all, a tuple of terminal numbers marks those. x1.run("24V", 4, interface=True) unused False Marks the run's terminals as unused: True marks all, a tuple marks those. x1.run("SPARE", 2, unused=True)

TerminalStrip.label is the strip's label as the design printed it ("X5"); Run.label is the run's own label ("PE"). Both are read-only.
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Cable.core
items.text:
Use d.series through the cable first: it takes the next free core. Use core to choose one core.

keyword default effect example which required The core, by colour or by 1-based number. w1.core(BN, a, b) a required The first pin of the core. With no b, the core is a shield core. w1.core(1, x1[1], m1["U"]) b None The second pin of the core. None is for a shield core only. w1.core(BN, x1[1], m1["U"])
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Cable.spare
items.text:
Cable.spare(*cores, ...) takes the cores to mark spare, by colour or number. With none, it marks every core not wired or marked so far, so wire first.

keyword default effect example at None A pin that parks one spare core. None leaves it unparked. An SH core refuses it: use core(which, a). w1.spare(BK, at=x1[9])
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: d.layout.break_before
items.text: keyword default effect example group required The function group that starts a new page. d.layout.break_before("pumps")
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: d.layout.chain
items.text:
d.layout.chain(*functions, ...) takes the functions to draw as one current path, source first.

keyword default effect example beside None A host function: the chain is drawn next to it, joined at each end net it shares. It raises AuthorError when no end net is the host's. None draws the chain alone. d.layout.chain(a, b, beside=c)
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: d.layout.draw_in
items.text: keyword default effect example function required The function or device to draw in the group, whatever its device's place says. d.layout.draw_in(run, "pumps") group required The function group whose pages draw it. d.layout.draw_in(run, "pumps")
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: d.layout.keep_together
items.text: d.layout.keep_together(*groups) takes the function groups that share a page when they fit. It has no named keyword. Example: d.layout.keep_together("pumps", "valves").
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: d.layout.order
items.text: d.layout.order(*groups) takes function groups: each neighbour pair is drawn in this order. It has no named keyword. Example: d.layout.order("pumps", "valves").
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: d.layout.page_title
items.text: keyword default effect example thing required The group, function, device, strip or nested unit (what d.add returned) whose drawing pages get the title. One thing takes one title. d.layout.page_title("pumps", "Pump circuits") text required The title text. The page prints it before its blocks' texts. Empty raises AuthorError. d.layout.page_title("pumps", "Pump circuits")
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: d.layout.side
items.text: keyword default effect example target required A field of a unit's interface, as u1.bus_in. An interface with no harness line ignores it. d.layout.side(f1, fr.ABOVE) side required fr.ABOVE or fr.BELOW: the edge the interface stands on. d.layout.side(f1, fr.BELOW)
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: d.layout.symbol
items.text: keyword default effect example target required A function, a device, or a FunctionKind such as FunctionKind.X, passed as a name. A string raises. d.layout.symbol(P.Q, "breaker") symbol required The library symbol to draw. d.layout.symbol(P.Q, "breaker") port_map None Maps a model port name to a symbol port name where they differ. A port not listed keeps its name. These names are strings, the last place a typed part's pin is still one. port_map={"13": "1.in"}
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Keywords a consumer never passes
items.text:
• engine on Layout: the design's engine. d.layout builds the layout around it, so you never pass it.
  • pe_mpn on TerminalStrip: the strip's PE terminal part. Pass pe= to d.terminal_strip instead.
path: Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints

items.title: Keywords of the fr functions
items.text:
This page has one table for each fr.* function: each named keyword, its default, its effect and an example call fragment. A call that takes only *args has no table, and one sentence says what it takes.

The tier of each call is the first word of its docstring (index.md, Tiers). The design calls are in keywords-design.md, the handle methods and layout hints in keywords-handles.md.

items.title: fr.design
items.text:
fr.design(*libraries, ...) takes the part libraries or generated parts modules as libraries.

keyword default effect example place None Names the first location as a bare tag. With None the design has no location until you call d.location. fr.design("demo_parts", place="C1") wiring None Replaces the default wire colour and size of the rows it names, for this design. Rows not named keep the IEC 60204-1 default. fr.design("demo_parts", wiring={fr.DC_SUPPLY: (BU, 1.5)})

items.title: fr.unit
items.text: keyword default effect example name required The unit release name. Instances print it, and the release folder under fr.release carries it. @fr.unit("pump-board", revision=2, ...) revision required The current revision. It is the last entry of the unit's history. revision=2 interface_version required The unit's boundary version. You bump it by hand when the interface changes. interface_version=1 date required Date of the current revision, as written in its history entry. date="2026-01-01" text required What the current revision changed, as written in its history entry. text="added the fuse" by required Who made the current revision. It prints in the history as created. by="AB" version 1 The release version. Revisions count within a version, and fr.release names the folder <version>.<revision>. version=2 title '' The unit's own title-block title. Empty gives a TITLE_BLOCK_UNIT_IDENTITY_MISSING warning on its document. title="Pump board" number '' The unit's own title-block number. Empty gives a TITLE_BLOCK_UNIT_IDENTITY_MISSING warning on its document. number="DWG-101" history () Earlier revisions of the unit. Each entry is a mapping of the d.revision keywords revision, date, text and created. history=[{"revision": 1, "date": "2025-12-01", "text": "first", "created": "AB"}] class_code None One to three capital letters. A floating d.add(fn, None, name=...) numbers from this class. None gives no class, so a floating add raises. class_code="B" wiring None Replaces wire colour and size rows inside this unit's body only. A unit never takes its parent's rows. wiring={fr.DC_SUPPLY: (BU, 1.5)}

items.title: fr.document
items.text:
fr.document(preset, subject, ...) takes the preset and the subject as positional arguments.

keyword default effect example preset required The fr.DocumentPreset that fixes the deliverable's default page kinds (documents.md). fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.SYSTEM, None, cover=Path("cover.md")) subject required What the document is about: what d.location(...) returns, a Device, a unit release name, or None for the system preset. Another value raises TypeError. fr.document(preset, "pump-board", cover=cover) cover required The Markdown cover file, stored verbatim. Its stem is the document's key. A missing file raises FileNotFoundError. A <stem>.notes.md beside it becomes the notes page. cover=Path("cover.md") add () fr.PageKind values added to the preset's default pages. add=(fr.PageKind.OVERVIEW,) remove () fr.PageKind values removed from the preset's pages. remove=(fr.PageKind.NOTES,) logo None An SVG file for the title block's logo cell. None leaves the cell empty. A missing file raises. logo=Path("logo.svg") notice '' The title block's IP notice text, printed on every page of this document. Empty leaves the cell empty. notice="Property of Demo Ltd"

items.title: fr.readability
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The BuildResult to measure. The layout runs again on its model, and the call returns one row per schematic page and one per unit. fr.readability(result)

items.title: fr.build
items.text:
fr.build(*drafts, ...) takes the drafts or Design objects to merge as drafts.

keyword default effect example releases None A release root. Numbering pins are seeded from the releases stored there, so a released unit keeps its numbers. None numbers freely. fr.build(d, releases=Path("releases"))

items.title: fr.check
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The BuildResult to check. Returns its findings plus the KiCad, PDF and render checks, errors first. fr.check(result)

items.title: fr.report
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The BuildResult to report. Returns one text: a summary line, each ERROR and WARNING with its fix, then counted notes. print(fr.report(result))

items.title: fr.write
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The built model whose exports are written. Any ERROR in fr.check(result) raises BuildErrors and writes nothing. fr.write(result, Path("out")) out_dir required The folder that receives the exports: the CSV reports, WAGO XML, overview and one PDF per document. fr.write(result, Path("out")) unit None Writes only that unit's own set, with no overview.html. None writes the whole model. fr.write(result, out, unit="pump-board") intermediates None A folder for SVGs, netlists and .typ sources. None keeps them in memory. intermediates=Path(".fransys") releases None A release root. With a stored release of the system there, overview.html marks what changed since it. None marks nothing. releases=Path("releases")

items.title: fr.export_names
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The BuildResult. Returns the file name fr.write gives each export, keyed by kind and subject. Writes nothing. fr.export_names(result) unit None Names only that unit's exports, as fr.write(unit=) would. None names the whole model's. fr.export_names(result, unit="pump-board")

items.title: fr.release
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The built model to release. Any ERROR raises BuildErrors and writes nothing. fr.release(result, Path("releases")) into required The release root. The call writes <into>/<name>/<version>.<revision>/. An identical stored listing returns the existing path. fr.release(result, Path("releases")) unit None Releases that unit instead of the system. fr.release(result, into, unit="pump-board")

items.title: fr.releases
items.text: keyword default effect example root required The release root to read. Returns each release folder in name, version, revision order. A missing root gives (). fr.releases(Path("releases"))

items.title: fr.diff
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The built model to compare. Returns the Markdown change list against a stored release. fr.diff(result, Path("releases")) baselines required The release root that holds the stored release. A missing release raises FileNotFoundError. fr.diff(result, Path("releases")) unit None Compares that unit instead of the system. fr.diff(result, root, unit="pump-board") against None A <version>.<revision> folder to compare with. None takes the release at the model's revision, else the previous one. against="1.3"

items.title: fr.verify
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The rebuilt model. Returns one BASELINE_DIFFERS ERROR per unit instance, or the system, whose listing drifted, and an INFO (BASELINE_RULES_MOVED, BASELINE_ROWS_UNCHECKED) for a release cut by an older fransys: fr.rebaseline clears it. fr.verify(result, Path("releases")) baselines required The release root with the stored baselines. A unit with no stored baseline is not reported. fr.verify(result, Path("releases"))

items.title: fr.rebaseline
items.text: keyword default effect example result required The rebuilt model. Re-cuts each stored listing the current rules print differently, in listing.json and the manifest only, children before parents. Returns the folders rewritten, () when none. A real change raises BuildErrors with BASELINE_DIFFERS and writes nothing. fr.rebaseline(result, Path("releases")) baselines required The release root with the stored baselines. fr.rebaseline(result, Path("releases")) unit None None covers every unit and the system with a stored baseline. A unit covers it and the units below. fr.rebaseline(result, root, unit="pump-board")

items.title: fr.parts
items.text: fr.parts(*packages) takes part-data package import names. It has no named keyword and returns one Draft. Zero names give an empty Draft. Example: fr.parts("demo_parts").

items.title: fr.parts_module
items.text: fr.parts_module(*sources) takes the library names to generate a typed parts module for. It has no named keyword and returns the module's text. Example: fr.parts_module("demo_parts").

items.title: fr.lint
items.text: fr.lint(*libraries) takes part-library import names. It has no named keyword and returns their findings, library by library. Zero libraries give (). Example: fr.lint("demo_parts").

items.title: Keywords and handles
items.text: This page lists the public names of the facade's handles and signal types, then the keyword arguments of the record constructors. The keywords of the d.* calls are in keywords-design.md, those of the handle methods and layout hints in keywords-handles.md, those of the fr.* functions in keywords-output.md.

items.title: Signal types and short names
items.text:
A signal type says what kind of PLC channel or field signal a function asks for. The facade gives the common ones short names. fr.DI, fr.DO, fr.AI and fr.AO are all members of fr.SignalType, and each is passed as the signal of plc.

  • DI: a digital input, SignalType.DI.
  • DO: a digital output, SignalType.DO. DO belongs with DI, AI and AO as one of the four short names.
  • AI: an analog input, the 4-20 mA current loop, SignalType.AI_CURRENT. Analog voltage inputs have no short name.
  • AO: an analog output, the 4-20 mA current loop, SignalType.AO_CURRENT. Analog voltage outputs have no short name.

The short names cover only the current loops and the two digital kinds. Use the full member, fr.SignalType.<NAME>, for the rest:

  • fr.SignalType.AI_VOLTAGE and fr.SignalType.AO_VOLTAGE: analog voltage inputs and outputs.
  • fr.SignalType.RTD: a resistance temperature detector, such as a Pt100.
  • fr.SignalType.RELAY: a relay signal.
import fransys as fr

assert fr.DI is fr.SignalType.DI
assert fr.AI is fr.SignalType.AI_CURRENT
rtd = fr.SignalType.RTD  # no short name; pass it as the `signal` of `plc`

items.title: Handle types
items.text:
Handles are the objects a design returns and the reader holds. A consumer does not build them.

  • Device: one device, such as Q1. It reaches a function by name (Q1.coil) and a pin by brackets (Q1[2]). An unknown function or pin raises and lists the candidates. Q1.tag is the tag the call gave, or None.
  • Fn: one function of a device, such as K1.coil. It reaches a pin by brackets (Q1.main[2]) or by name (K1.coil.A1). An unknown pin raises and lists the pins it has. Fn.plc requests a PLC channel.
  • Pin: one port of one Fn. It has an id, an authoring key, a name that brackets match, and a role, such as INTERNAL or EXTERNAL.
  • Run: a run of terminals on a strip, from x1.run(...). It reaches a terminal by brackets (run[1]).
  • Cable: one cable from d.cable. w1.core(BN, a, b) wires a core.
  • AcSupply: what d.ac_supply returns. It holds the rails L1, L2, L3 and N when it was given one.
  • DcSupply: what d.dc_supply returns. It holds the rails plus, minus and mid.
  • SupplyRail: one rail of a supply, such as supply.L1 or supply.plus.
  • UnitDef: what @fr.unit returns, the release of one unit. d.add(definition, "U1") builds it; a function that takes build arguments returns one.
  • Throw: one throw of a changeover, k1.co.no or k1.co.nc. It stands in a d.series call as an element. A consumer does not build one (its fns are the changeover functions). A generated parts module declares it on every changeover function.
  • TypedDevice: the base a generated parts module subclasses once for each part. Its mpn is its whole contract. It adds no behaviour: the subclass only declares functions and pins.
  • TypedFn: the base a generated parts module subclasses for one function of one part. It adds no behaviour. Its subclass declares pins for the type checker.
  • BuildResult: the result of fr.build. It holds model, the frozen and laid-out Model, and findings, every finding collected while building it.

items.title: Type checking
items.text:
A script written in this guide's spellings type-checks with no ty: ignore and no Any. Your ty settings need nothing.

  • For full checking, generate a parts module (fr.parts_module, parts.md) and pass its classes to d.device. Each function and pin is a typed attribute, brackets take only the part's pin names, and a misspelt name is a type error.
  • A device made from an MPN string is checked only at run time: a call on it checks nothing. Annotate it fr.Device to check the calls on it.
  • On a fr.Device, a device-level pin by attribute (q1.A1) types as fr.Fn and is a ty error where a pin is needed. Write q1["A1"]; both run.
  • Every handle in "Handle types" has a name on fr, so fr.Device, fr.AcSupply or fr.UnitDef[Io] annotates a parameter or a return.
  • A function of a device is a fr.Fn: k1.coil and q1.main type as fr.Fn. A pin by brackets is a fr.Pin: k1.coil["A2"], q1["2"] and k1.coil.A1. k1.co.no and k1.co.nc are changeover throws (fr.Throw); a generated changeover function declares both.
  • A pin chosen by an int loop variable is a ty error against a typed part's pin names: loop over fn.pins. A computed name, f"CH {n}", is a ty error too.
  • A wrong function or pin name is a run-time error. It raises and lists the names the part has. A pin named + or - is the attribute _plus or _minus.
  • A unit with build arguments is a factory that returns fr.UnitDef (units.md, "Variants and revised copies").

items.title: Severity
items.text:
Severity says how much a Finding blocks a downstream output. The facade alone decides which severities block which outputs.

  • ERROR: blocks every export. write raises and writes nothing while any error finding remains. There is no escape hatch.
  • WARNING: worth a look. It blocks nothing under the facade's policy.
  • INFO: worth noting. It blocks nothing under the facade's policy.

items.title: Model and Finding
items.text: The facade builds these records. A consumer reads them and does not construct them. freeze builds a Model, and the domain validators and the facade build the Finding values.

items.title: Model
items.text:
Model is the immutable, validated result of freeze. Everything reachable from it is deeply immutable, and freeze checks that.

  • schema_version: the model schema number. freeze stamps the number this build knows. Reading data with a number this build does not know raises an error.
  • aliases: a map from a retired id to the id that replaces it. freeze rewrites every reference to a retired id into one to its replacement. Draft.alias fills it.
  • origins: a map from an id to its Origin, the file, line and note where the record was authored. It sits outside the tables. Moving a line does not change the digest.
  • digests: one digest for each registered namespace, such as core, facet or layout. A change to layout records leaves the core and facet digests alone.
  • digest: one digest that combines the digests. A generated parts module records it as its library digest. fr.design refuses a stale module, so a library change must be regenerated before use.
  • Model.origin_of and Model.key_of read origins and the tables. See target below.

items.title: Finding
items.text:
Finding is one reported engineering problem. Every domain validator emits this one shape. All four fields are required keyword arguments.

  • code: a stable UPPER_SNAKE string, such as NET_UNREALISED. The module that emits it lists it. The reader sees it in the findings list. The order is error, warning, then info, and inside each band by code, then subjects, then message.
  • severity: a Severity. Only ERROR stops an export. See the Severity section above.
  • subjects: the ids the finding is about. They are stored once each, in id order, so the order a validator found them in does not matter.
  • message: the text a reader sees. For a write finding the facade's describe turns it into printed text first. A release finding prints its message as written.

items.title: Draft calls
items.text:
A Draft collects records from input files before freeze. Inputs call these methods. A consumer rarely does.

  • origin on Draft.add and Draft.extend: the Origin the records are attributed to. It is required, with no default. An identical record already present keeps the smaller origin by (file, line, note), so call order does not matter. A different record under the same id raises a merge conflict. extend is not atomic: a conflict leaves the records before it in place.
  • old on Draft.alias: the id that has been retired. The new argument is its replacement. It raises when old is new, the two are of different kinds, or old is already retired in favour of another id. The input decoder and the merge both call it.
  • target on Draft.key_of, Draft.origin_of and Draft.record_of: the id to look up. key_of returns the record's authoring key, origin_of returns its Origin, and record_of returns the record itself. Each returns None when nothing is held. record_of does not follow an alias.
  • target on Model.key_of and Model.origin_of: the same lookup on a frozen Model. key_of returns None when no record holds the id. origin_of returns the Origin or None. The describe function asks it where an id was written.

items.title: KiCad
items.text:
Fransys writes a KiCad netlist for each board in your model. This page shows how to import it into a KiCad 9 board, which settings to use, and how to start a part file from a KiCad symbol.

The model is the schematic. Use KiCad for the board only: no KiCad schematic file, and no "Update PCB from Schematic". The board gets its parts and nets from the netlist, through the PCB editor's File > Import > Netlist. The import is a manual step.

items.title: Get the netlist
items.text:
fr.write(result, out_dir, intermediates=...) writes one netlist per board into the intermediates folder, named netlist-<board>.net. A netlist is not an export, so it never lands in out_dir.

fr.check(result) reports the KiCad findings. Read them first. An ERROR (REFERENCE_DUPLICATE, NET_NAME_DUPLICATE, PAD_ON_MULTIPLE_NETS) means do not import yet. Each code is in findings-kicad.md.

items.title: Import settings
items.text:
Open File > Import > Netlist in the PCB editor, pick the file, and set the dialog like this.

Setting Choice Why Link Method Link footprints using component tstamps (unique ids) Each part's id comes from the model, not from its designation. A renumbered part (R1 becomes R7) keeps its footprint, position and routing. Delete footprints with no components in netlist On The model decides what is on the board. A part you remove from the model leaves the board. Replace footprints with those specified in netlist On The footprint comes from the part file. A footprint changed by hand on the board is drift. Delete/replace footprints even if locked Off A lock is a deliberate choice. The import reports the locked footprint, and you resolve it by hand. Delete tracks shorting multiple nets Off It silently removes routing. Run DRC after the import and fix reported shorts by hand.

Never switch the link method on a board that already has footprints. Footprints imported by reference designator carry no matching ids, so a later import by id sees every part as new.

items.title: Import steps
items.text:
1. Build the project and write it, so the netlist is current.
  2. Read the KiCad findings and fix every ERROR.
  3. In the PCB editor, open File > Import > Netlist, pick the file, and set the settings above.
  4. Click Load and Test Netlist first. It is a dry run. Read "Changes to Be Applied" and check that the deletions and replacements are the ones you expect. Errors must be 0.
  5. Click Update PCB, place the new footprints, and route.
  6. Run DRC. Commit the board file together with the model change that caused it.

items.title: Footprints that only exist on the board
items.text: Mounting holes, fiducials and logos have no part in the model. Set the footprint attribute Not in schematic on each one, in its footprint properties. KiCad then leaves them alone when "Delete footprints with no components in netlist" is on.

items.title: Parts that are not installed
items.text: A part with installed = False stays in the netlist and on the board, marked do-not-populate. The BOM report leaves it out. You do not remove it from the board.

items.title: Start a part file from a KiCad symbol
items.text:
python -m fransys_kicad <file.kicad_sym> <symbol> reads one symbol's pins from a .kicad_sym library and prints a part-file skeleton to stdout. It has one [[function]] of kind generic, with one port per pin.

uv run python -m fransys_kicad my-library.kicad_sym DEMO-RLY-2U > parts/demo-rly-2u.toml

Open the new file and fill in mpn, manufacturer, description, category and class_code under [part]. Each is an empty string marked # TODO. Then run fr.lint over the library (see parts.md). The skeleton lints clean once those five fields are filled.

items.title: Layout numbers
items.text: This page lists every keyword of d.layout.profile and every number of d.layout.sheet: what it does, its house value, its effect on the drawing, and when to change it. A gap is in grid units G; eight G make one symbol module. A sheet number is in millimetres, except module_mm.

items.title: Sheet numbers
items.text:
d.layout.sheet(name, **numbers) records a sheet format and returns its handle. Pass the handle to d.layout.profile(sheet=handle). A profile with no sheet uses the house sheet: A3 landscape, 420 by 297 mm, content box 410 by 267 mm at (5, 5), an 8 by 6 frame, module_mm 2.5. A sheet takes all nine numbers and has no defaults. A missing number or an unknown one raises AuthorError. The title-block band is the sheet's height minus twice content_y_mm minus content_height_mm: 20 mm on the house sheet. A smaller content_height_mm gives a taller band. Text of 2.5 mm or more needs a band over 20 mm. A document with no schematic page takes the profile's sheet too.

number what it is effect on the drawing when to change it width_mm Sheet width. The size of the printed page. A different paper size. height_mm Sheet height. The size of the printed page. A different paper size. content_x_mm Left edge of the content box, from the sheet's left edge. Where drawings start; the margin on the left. A different margin. content_y_mm Top edge of the content box, from the sheet's top edge. Where drawings start; the margin on top. A different margin or title block. content_width_mm Width of the content box. Page capacity: a page holds content_width_mm * 8 / module_mm G across, rounded down. A wider box fits more columns before a block is split. A different paper size. content_height_mm Height of the content box. Page capacity down the page, by the same rule. A taller box fits more rows. A different paper size. frame_columns Columns of the reference grid printed on the frame. The content box is divided evenly. Cross references and findings name a position as a column and a row. Rarely; more columns on a wide sheet. frame_rows Rows of the reference grid. The same, for rows. Rarely. module_mm Millimetres of one symbol module. Number or Decimal. The grid pitch. Symbol bodies and gaps scale with it; text sizes and line widths do not, they are fixed in mm. A smaller module fits more on a page; a larger one splits sooner. The reader's choice of size, not a fix for a crowded page. 
from decimal import Decimal

import fransys as fr

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
a4 = d.layout.sheet(
    "A4 landscape",
    width_mm=297,
    height_mm=210,
    content_x_mm=5,
    content_y_mm=5,
    content_width_mm=287,
    content_height_mm=170,
    frame_columns=6,
    frame_rows=4,
    module_mm=Decimal("2.0"),
)
d.layout.profile(sheet=a4)

items.title: Profile keywords
items.text:
d.layout.profile(...) sets the layout numbers of the design, or of the unit whose body calls it. At most one per unit. A keyword left out keeps its house value. A value given replaces it whole. A unit with no profile uses the house values, never its parent's. d.layout.profile does not draw anything: it advises the layout engine.

keyword house value what it does effect on the drawing when to change it sheet the house sheet The sheet format the pages use, a handle from d.layout.sheet. Paper size, margins and module_mm. A paper size other than A3. column_gap 48 Clear width between two adjacent columns of blocks. Wider gaps spread columns and leave room for wires between them. Wires cramp between columns, or columns waste width. row_gap 32 The smallest clear height between two blocks stacked in a column. A column too tall for its page closes its spacing down to this value and no further. Rarely; lower it to fit a tall column. row_spacing 88 The clear height a block keeps below the one above it, when the page has room. Looser spacing reads easier; it falls back toward row_gap on a full page. A sparse page that wastes height, or a crowded one. route_margin 64 How far outside the box spanned by a wire's two ends the router may look first. A larger margin finds a detour round a block; a smaller one keeps wires short. A wire takes a long way round, or cannot find a way. text_height_mm 1.8 The smallest text on every page kind, a capital height in mm (ISO 3098); a larger role keeps its own size or this one, whichever is larger. Sets text size, and with it the room texts take: font size over one G, rounded up. A style choice only. See below. min_text_height_mm 1.8 The smallest capital height in mm the text may print at. Changes no drawing. A profile printing under the floor gets one TEXT_TOO_SMALL warning, and nothing is shrunk or grown. The recommended floor is the house 1.8. Lower it only when the small text is intended. Otherwise raise text_height_mm. marker_padding 2 Clear space between a link marker's text and its outline, on every edge. Larger padding makes markers and their boxes bigger. Markers look cramped. route_turn_penalty 4 The cost of one bend in a wire. A higher cost makes wires straighter and longer. Wires zigzag. route_crossing_penalty 16 The cost of one wire crossing another. A higher cost avoids crossings at the price of longer wires. Too many crossings. hide_unused_pins False Hide a box-drawn pin with no conductor, and a function with none, on drawings only. Drawings are shorter; every list still shows every pin. A box in a chain draws only its wired pins (LONG-CHAIN D2). An interface with many unused pins. actuator_each_contact True Draw the operated symbol on every contact of a manually operated device, with no reference and no contact list. False draws the actuator once at the lead contact, with the contact list under it. A design that wants one push button per device. The choice is per unit: set it in each unit's profile, or in a shared helper every unit calls, to set it once. band_ranks supply 0, terminal.first 0, protection 1, switch and contacts 2, sensor 3, coil, load, actuator and terminal 4, terminal.last 5 A map of function kind to the horizontal band it sits in, top first. terminal.first and terminal.last sit beside terminal. Moves kinds up or down the column. The map replaces the house map whole: restate every kind you want ranked. A circuit reads better with another top-to-bottom order. group_ranks empty A map of an aspect group's label to its page rank. Orders the groups of pages. A group with no rank sorts last. You want the pages in your own order.

items.title: Grid pitch and printed sizes
items.text: module_mm sets the grid pitch, not the printed size of text or lines, which are fixed in mm. It is the reader's choice of size, never a fix for a crowded page. Split the content into function blocks (drawing.md). A well-formed design that still overflows is a Fransys defect: send the smallest model. text_height_mm sets the smallest text on every page, as a capital height in mm. Never use it to make a page fit: a page that is too full needs less on the page, split into function blocks.

items.title: Moving to 0.14
items.text: This page lists every fr.derive name 0.14 removes, and what to use instead. fr.derive now holds the names a consumer needs to read a model, and every one has a guide entry. The rest stay in the workspace for layout, render and the outputs. A consumer script that used a removed name changes as below.

items.title: Removed names
items.text: removed use instead why location_node_designation node_designation It prints any aspect node's signed path, + or =, so the name no longer says location. number, allocate_plc fr.build(d) They are passes; the facade runs them. ext_usage, ExtUsage none A migration diagnostic with no consumer use. overview_graph, OverviewGraph, OverviewLink, OverviewLinkKind, OverviewNode, OverviewPort, OverviewSignal none; use fr.derive.items, ports and conductors The overview output is being reshaped; its graph types are not stable. box_pairs, BoxPair, draws_as_line, supply_share, connector_box_lines, connector_at_line_end, line_conductors, line_stub_line, check_side_hints the model records: fr.derive.conductors, harness_line_ends, line_designation Drawing helpers. The model records hold the facts they read. black_box_unit, drawing_set_is_replica_only, is_black_box_item, schematic_functions, own_nodes, enclosing_boards, first_leg, rail_pairs, link_state, LinkState, changeover_throws, Throws, owned_contacts, Indexes, build_indexes none, or fr.derive.functions and aspect_nodes Layout internals. profile_of read the layout.profile table of the model The profile is a record. physical_nets, unused_terminals fr.derive.net_of, fr.derive.port_is_unused One net, one port at a time. terminal_strips fr.derive.terminal_items, fr.derive.unit_strips The kept pair covers a model and a unit. unit_items, unit_subtree filter fr.derive.items by item.unit A plain filter of a kept table. current_revision, same_version fr.derive.revision_history, fr.derive.release_order Compare the ordered pairs. document_unit document.unit A field of the document record. list_context pass the location node you want to a row function's context A value the caller passes. connector_label, connector_segments, designation_holder, takes_parents_designation, is_own_unit_root, is_sole_unit_root, standalone fr.derive.item_designation, printed_designation The designation functions print the text; the helpers behind them are internal. core_colour, conductors_on_item fr.derive.cable_rows, fr.derive.conductors The rows carry the colour; the conductors table carries the rest. cell_parts, cell_text, column_rows, column_values, pin_lines read the fields of a row and order them by the *_COLUMNS constant Output formatting.

items.title: Moving to 0.15
items.text: This page lists each call, name and finding that 0.15 changes, with the old spelling and the new one. A consumer script that used an old spelling changes as below. The version is read with importlib.metadata.version("fransys"); there is no fr.__version__.

items.title: Renamed and changed names
items.text: old new why text_height in layout.profile(...), an int in G, default 8 text_height_mm, a Decimal in mm, default 1.8 The text size is a capital height in mm (ISO 3098), not a count of grid units. min_text_mm in layout.profile(...) min_text_height_mm, default 1.8 It is the floor for text_height_mm, in the same unit. text_mm and min_text_mm on a readability page row text_height_mm and min_text_height_mm The same two quantities under the new names. A unit row takes the smallest text_height_mm. module_mm scales symbols, gaps and text module_mm sets the grid pitch only Text and line widths are fixed in mm. Set the text size with text_height_mm. TEXT_TOO_SMALL reads text_height and min_text_mm reads text_height_mm and min_text_height_mm The finding compares the same two values under the new names.

items.title: New keyword
items.text: old new why fr.write(result, out_dir) fr.write(result, out_dir, releases=into) releases is the folder you pass to fr.release. It defaults to None, which marks nothing.

items.title: The system overview
items.text:
fr.write writes overview.html beside the PDFs. The page is one file and needs no network. Its switches are Colour by, Find, Parts, Select and Theme, and View inside a unit.

  • Changes is new. It appears only when releases holds a release of the system, the one at the model's revision or else the previous one.
  • Without releases, or with no release there, the page has no Changes switch.
  • The Changes switch applies only to a whole-system write; a unit write gets no Changes page.

items.title: Drawing and readability
items.text:
• d.ac_supply no longer draws power symbols at its pins; it keeps AC rails as terminals and references.
  • The readability rows have a new column, single_contact_images_other_page, counting the single-contact images whose one contact is on another page.

items.title: Checks and findings
items.text:
• check now places overview.html and returns its findings, so a whole-system or unit write meets them at the same gate. build does not.
  • OVERVIEW_UNPLACED is new. It is an ERROR, raised when the overview placer finds no room for a view.
  • The DIAGRAM_BOX_OVERLAP, DIAGRAM_LINE_OFF_BOX, DIAGRAM_LINE_THROUGH_BOX and DIAGRAM_TEXT_OVERLAP findings also check the views of the overview.

items.title: Moving to 0.16 and 0.17
items.text: This page covers a move from 0.15 to 0.16, to 0.17, or across both. If you are on 0.16, read the 0.17 section only. Nothing in fr.__all__ is removed or renamed. A stored model written by 0.15 or 0.16 no longer loads.

items.title: Moving from 0.16 to 0.17
items.text:
Each change below has the old spelling, the new one and the fix.

where 0.16 0.17 what to change Stored models Schema 17. Schema 18: facing is stored on every link marker. An older model raises SchemaVersionError. Rebuild with fr.build. A layout golden or digest you keep moves by the schema stamp. PlcChannelRow (PLC-PIN-ROWS, model-0209) One row per channel, with channel_designation. One row per pin, with port, pin and channel_name, and no channel_designation. wired_to holds the far ends of that pin alone. Read pin and channel_name where you read channel_designation. PLC_COLUMNS and plc_list_rows Built on channel_designation. pin, channel_name, signal, signal_name, wired_to. Update code that picks a column by name or position. UNIT_CONNECTOR_DANGLING (DANGLING-RETIRE, model-0219) A WARNING for a spare terminal or port of a unit. Retired: the code no longer exists. A filter that names it now matches nothing; remove it. PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH message Names each channel by its module. Names each channel by its pins, such as -A1:1. Code that matches the old text must match the pin form.

Other 0.17 changes need no code change:

  • The PLC list prints one row per pin, spare pins included.
  • A PLC request binds the channel it is wired to even when that channel's net holds other devices. A request of the wrong kind yields the channel to one of the right kind (model-0211).
  • Several requests wired to one channel give PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH. Request that channel once, on one of the devices. 0.18 gives one clear finding.
  • A finding message names an untagged unit by its name and revision, as its title block prints it. unit unit no longer appears (overview-0003).
  • A coil switched by a channel pin stands under that channel (layout-0208).
  • A beside branch under a host pin no longer fails with ROUTE_FAILED. That was a 0.16.0 regression (layout-0174).
  • A terminal whose part has a protective link, such as a fuse terminal, is no longer a rail terminal (model-0215).
  • PDF navigation: link markers and sheet-index rows link, viewer page labels show the sheet text, and the outline lists sheets and devices (pdf-0029, pdf-0034).
  • A new package, fransys-el, comes in with fransys. A lock file gains one package (layout-0192).
  • Cable page texts come out in reading order (render-0011).

items.title: What may newly stop your build
items.text:
change what you see the fix Stored models use schema 17 (0.15: 15) SchemaVersionError: "this build reads schema version 17" Rebuild the model with fr.build. A layout golden or digest you keep moves by the schema stamp. PLC_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS is a new ERROR A PLC request whose wiring ties several channels of its signal kind, none on a direct conductor, used to take the first one silently. Now it binds none. Wire the request to one channel. The message names the request and every tied channel (model-0211). PLC_BINDING_SIGNAL_MISMATCH message It now names the asked kind, the channel, the channel's kind and both fixes. The severity is unchanged. Ask for the channel's kind, or rewire to a channel of the asked kind. CABLE_PAIR_INVALID is a new part-file ERROR A [cable_product] pairs entry names a core out of range, a core in two pairs, a screen that is not SH, or an SH core as a pair core. Correct the pair list in the part file. CABLE_CORE_COUNT counts open cores A cable with spare or one-ended screen cores now counts them toward its part's core count, so a warning can clear or appear. The message names the remedy. HintError for a group with no column It names the group that took the devices, the loop and the d.layout.chain fix. It is still an error. Apply the d.layout.chain(...) it prints (layout-0195). TITLE_BLOCK_TEXT_OVERFLOW names d.layout.page_title The =F1 =F2 group-label fallback is gone. A title that fits no form is cut with "…". It stays a WARNING. Give the page a short title with d.layout.page_title.

These findings no longer fire, so a script that expects them changes:

  • DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS is an ERROR for a SCHEMATIC page only when the document has no other content page. A list with rows, a HARNESS_DRAWING with a cable or a BLOCK_DIAGRAM with a sheet is enough (pdf-0033). Harness and diagram errors are unchanged.
  • UNUSED_CONTRADICTED is checked at the unit that declares unused=. Declaring a passed-up interface unused on the outer unit no longer warns (model-0210).
  • LONE_CELL skips an item box over a unit's open boundary functions (layout-0202).

items.title: Output changes
items.text:
Drawings and PDFs change byte for byte. Re-check any golden you keep.

  • Page pad. Schematic ink keeps two wiring lanes (PAGE_PAD) inside the frame line, so every page moves (layout-0187).
  • Idle pins and terminals. A connector pin or terminal that no wire inside the unit reaches is not drawn on the unit's own pages. The parent's black box keeps it, and its table still lists it (layout-0197, layout-0202). A unit with nothing left to draw adds no schematic page.
  • Connector tables. CONNECTOR_LIST prints one table per connector with Pin, Net, Mate and Ends. Style, pin count and gender leave the PDF table. connectors.csv keeps them and gains an ends column (pdf-0030).
  • Boundary boxes. A boundary box prints its landed pins, not the interface field name (model-0206).
  • Cable names. A cable end that is a connector names it (+C1-A1-X1) on the cable page and in the cable list.
  • Spare cores and pairs. Cable.spare(...) and a one-ended screen from Cable.core draw as open rows with a blank stub. A part file's pairs draw pair brackets. The cable list shows pairs (model-0213, layout-0207).
  • Beside chains. d.layout.chain(beside=...) joins its host by one or two end nets, a one-pin box or a box head, with no marker. A box-pin run stands a grid off the pin.
  • Titles. The title block prints the first form of derive.page_title_forms that fits. A strip terminal reads as its strip once ("-X1") (pdf-0028, pdf-0032).
  • Sheets page. PageKind.SHEET_INDEX is in every preset, after the notes. It lists Sheet, Title and Page. Block diagram sheets read B1, B2 (pdf-0031). remove=(fr.PageKind.SHEET_INDEX,) drops it.
  • cores.csv. It lists every cable core with both ends, its pair and its spare mark (CORES-CSV).
  • PLC list. Signals print in datasheet words (DI, AI (mA), DO (relay)). A channel with no device and no wire prints spare. The CSV keeps the enum values.
  • A bridged run outside a block takes no terminals, so its terminals join the block of their first circuit wire (author-0037).

items.title: API names
items.text:
fr.__all__ gains no name and loses none. fr.__version__ is new, read from importlib.metadata. It is not in __all__, so from fransys import * skips it.

where new authoring d.layout.page_title(thing, text); Cable.spare(*cores, at=...); Cable.core for an SH core earthed at one end part file [cable_product] pairs, and the demo part DEMO-CBL-2X2X0.75-SP fr.PageKind SHEET_INDEX fr.derive rows OpenCoreRow, SheetIndexRow, open_core_rows, sheet_index_rows, plc_list_rows, connector_rows_of, CONNECTOR_LABELS fr.derive facts function_is_reached, port_is_reached, connector_items, unit_connector_items, signal_word, cores_text fr.derive titles page_title, page_title_forms, short_title, sheets, diagram_sheets, sheet_text, set_page_text, sheet_counter_text, sheet_title_text records layout.page_title, layout.open_core_wire, facet.open_core, and CableProductFacet.pairs with CorePair

d.layout.chain(beside=) now accepts one end net on the host and a one-pin box at the chain's end.

items.title: Moving to 0.19
items.text: This page lists each call that 0.19 moves or changes, with the old spelling and the new one. A consumer script that used an old spelling changes as below.

items.title: The detail calls
items.text:
Four calls moved to d.detail, with their keywords unchanged. The old names raise an AuthorError that names the new home. There is no alias: one task has one spelling.

old new why d.wire(a, b, wire=...) d.detail.wire(a, b, wire=...) A path is d.series. A hand-wired hop is for a case no series writes (detail.md). d.net(name, *pins, kind=) d.detail.net(name, *pins, kind=) A named net that no wire joins is a detail case. d.busbar(a, b) d.detail.busbar(a, b) A busbar joins two fixed pins, a detail case. d.rail_bond(a, b) d.detail.rail_bond(a, b) A rail bond joins two fixed pins, a detail case.

A unit body's design moves the same way: u.wire(...) becomes u.detail.wire(...). d.earth, d.mate and W1.core keep their spellings.

items.title: Grouped contacts
items.text: before after one series per contact: d.series(a.A_L1, k1.co_1.no, ...), and again for co_2 and co_3 q = d.poles(k1.co_1, k1.co_2, k1.co_3), then one d.series(a, q.no, m1, ...) three single-pole changeover symbols one three-pole symbol; with selector=True its throws face the line

items.title: From d.wire to d.series
items.text:
Most d.wire calls were a current path written hop by hop. Write the path as one series instead: it pairs the poles and takes the next free terminal or core.

A control path from rail to rail:

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
s1 = d.device("S1", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
k1 = d.device("K1", "DEMO-CTR-3P-24")

# before: d.wire(dc.plus.pin, s1.no["13"], ...), d.wire(s1.no["14"], k1.coil["A1"], ...), ...
d.series(dc.plus, s1.no, k1.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))

A power path through a strip and a cable to a motor:

from fransys.colours import BK

x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", *(x0[n] for n in (1, 2, 3)))
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")

# before: one d.wire per pole to X1, one W1.core per core, one d.wire per motor pin
d.series(ac, k1.main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
