A fixed terminal, as an as-built cabinet numbers them. x1[3] takes the place of the next free terminal. x1[1:4] is terminals 1, 2 and 3 as one three-pole element, the end excluded. A tuple puts one terminal on each pole when they sit on different strips. A fixed terminal counts as taken, so a strip passed whole later skips it. A tuple that runs in order on one strip raises and names the slice to write:

x2 = d.terminal_strip("X2", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
h1 = d.device("H1", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
x3 = d.terminal_strip("X3", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 6)

# before: d.wire(dc.plus.pin, x2[3]), d.wire(x2[3].outer, h1.lamp["1"]), ...
d.series(dc.plus, x2[3], h1.lamp, x2[4], dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
# three phases on terminals 1, 2 and 3, and one terminal per pole across strips
d.series(ac, k1.main, x3[1:4], wire=(BK, 2.5))
x4, x5 = d.terminal_strip("X4", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 4), d.terminal_strip("X5", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 4)
d.series(d.device("Q9", "DEMO-MCB-3P").element, (x2[5], x4[3], x5[3]), wire=(BK, 2.5))

items.title: Behaviour that changed
items.text:
before now why fr.derive.takes_energy is True for a load only True for a load, an actuator and a coil A motor or coil draws from its supply, so load_limits counts its nominal_current_a. A part may still state energy. A series through a cable landed the GNYE core only when the strip before it had a pe= part, else it raised. The core lands on the load's PE port. The near end is the strip's PE terminal, else earthed open. A cable's protective core reaches its load without a hand wire (author-0044). A wire to the load's PE port after such a series built a GNYE_NOT_PE ERROR. It raises an AuthorError that names the series. The core is already landed; a second landing is refused at the call (author-0044). d.series(j1.x1, w5, j2.x1, ...) between two connectors raised has no poles: name its pins; each pin pair was a d.wire call. The series pairs the two connectors' pins in pin order. A function with no line side in the middle, or at one end against a supply, a rail or a function with poles, still raises. Unequal pin counts raise and name both counts. One derive fact orders a sideless end's pins (model-0242). ## Channels a series takes

A series now takes a PLC channel itself. Pass the module whole and it takes the lowest free channel (authoring.md, how channels are numbered). A script that fixes every channel, a1.di_7, still works.

A package that keeps the channel map of existing software checks it once. Build the package both ways, with the channels fixed and with the module passed whole, and compare the PLC list. If the two lists are equal, use the core form. Where they differ, keep the fixed form for those channels.

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU


def plc_list(fixed: bool) -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """The PLC list of a two-sensor package, the channels fixed or taken by the series."""
    d = fr.design("demo_parts")
    dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    a1 = d.device("A1", "DEMO-PLC-DI-4P")
    for number in (1, 2):
        sensor = d.device(f"S{number}", "DEMO-PB-NC")
        sensor.sw.plc(fr.DI, f"Sensor {number}")
        target = getattr(a1, f"di_{number}") if fixed else a1
        d.series(dc.plus, sensor.sw, target, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    return [(r.pin, r.signal_name) for r in fr.derive.plc_channel_rows(fr.build(d).model)]


assert plc_list(fixed=True) == plc_list(fixed=False)  # equal: use the core form

items.title: Moving to 0.20
items.text: This page lists each call that 0.20 adds or changes, with the old spelling and the new one.

items.title: A baseline cut by an older fransys
items.text:
fr.verify compares a stored listing under the rules of the fransys that cut it. When a later release printed a rule differently, it gives BASELINE_RULES_MOVED (INFO) for that release, and fr.release refuses over it. fr.rebaseline is the new call that clears it: it re-cuts the stored listing.json and the manifest under today's rules and leaves every export as it was.

Run fr.rebaseline(result, Path("releases")) once and commit the rewritten files. The worked example is in build.md, after "Checking a baseline stays true".

items.title: Renames in the change list
items.text: A listing now carries item keys (version 2), so the change list follows a rename: "Renamed -A1 → -A2" replaces a removal and an addition, and changes.csv writes renamed in the change column. A release cut before 0.20 has no keys: its diff pairs by name and CHANGES_BY_NAME says so. fr.rebaseline writes version 2.

items.title: Moving to 0.6
items.text: This page lists every change a 0.5 consumer script or part file must make for 0.6. Each entry gives the 0.5 spelling, the 0.6 spelling and one line of why. The 0.5 spellings sit in text blocks: they no longer run.

items.title: Imports and build
items.text:
0.5 0.6 Why fr.author and from fransys.author import ... d = fr.design("demo_parts", place="C1"), then calls on d fransys.author left __all__: the engineer surface is the one spelling. fr.build(parts, d.draft()) fr.build(d) A design holds its library, so the build needs no second argument. fr.build(parts, d.draft(), doc) fr.build(d, doc) The same reason, with a document.

Pass fr.design the generated parts module or the import-name strings that fr.parts takes.

items.title: Tags and units
items.text: 0.5 0.6 Why location("-C1"), "=M1", "+X1" d.location("C1", text) A tag is a bare key. A prefixed tag raises. unit("-A1", ...) @fr.unit("A1", ...) A unit name is a key, with no -, + or = prefix. unit release interface= interface_version=; boundary values are fn.limits(...) interface now means only the boundary marking, interface=True. d.add(fn, "io"), the second argument a lowercase key d.add(fn, "U1"), a printed tag; or d.add(fn, None, name="io") with class_code= on the unit The argument is the instance's tag and key, and a container prints it: -U1-J1. A lowercase letter raises. d.location called twice for one tag, order mattering one call per tag, in any order A location is order-free, and its text is set once.

items.title: Devices and terminal strips
items.text:
0.5 0.6 Why item(mpn, tag=, at=, group=) d.device("Q1", mpn, place=) The electrotechnical word is device, and its tag is the first argument. strip.terminal(3) X1[3] A terminal strip is indexed by terminal number. strip.take(...) X1[3] or X1.run(label, n) take had no surface spelling. Indexing and runs cover it. bridge(t1, t2) X1.run(label, n, bridged=True) A bridge joins the adjacent terminals of one run. A run may be two terminals. two parts of one MPN in a library no surface spelling The surface names a part by its MPN, which then names both makers.

d.device and d.terminal_strip raise on such an MPN and name both makers. The surface has no spelling for either part. Report the case, as a consumer case brings a form back.

items.title: Wires
items.text: 0.5 0.6 Why Wire(colour, mm2, label) wire=(BU, 0.75) and d.wire(a, b, label="L1") Wire is gone. The tuple is the one form, and the label belongs to the call. wiring(a, b, n=2) d.wire(a, b, n=2) One spelling for a wire between two pins.

items.title: Groups, supplies and ids
items.text: 0.5 0.6 Why a terminal's group argument, d.interface(fn, ...) the d.function block where the terminal is first taken; X1.x1.limits(rating=, operating=) One spelling each: the block names the group, and interface means the boundary marking. a supply with no source device d.dc_supply(name, plus=, minus=, voltage=) The pins and the voltage stand in for the source. a DC supply's M rail named M the rail is named 0V The 0 V conductor carries its potential as its name. derive.unit_ids(model) sorted(fr.derive.units(model)) It listed the keys of the units table. a unit function returning a dict, d.add(...) returning AddedUnit a typing.NamedTuple instance, returned by d.add as it is A misspelt boundary is a type error. fr.Run and fr.Terminal type the fields that hold strips, runs and terminals. Design.unit_id a unit is named by its release name: unit="pump-cabinet" in fr.write, fr.release, fr.verify There is no successor; the release name is the one name. derive.wire_label_rows derive.wire_rows and <set>-wires.csv WIRE-LIST removed it on purpose (bf2d3968). a per-terminal part on a strip one strip part; a run labelled "PE" takes pe= The strip has no per-terminal part.

items.title: Findings that change
items.text: 0.5 0.6 Why Net.potential with no supply declared declare the supply system: d.ac_supply(...) or d.dc_supply(...) Without it the model gets POTENTIAL_WITHOUT_SUPPLY (WARNING) and no rank. Profile.potential_ranks removed: ranks follow the declared supply A rank keyed by rail name left a rail named L or 12V unranked, and its pins swapped sides.

items.title: Part files
items.text:
0.5 0.6 Why a switched link with no rest rest = "open" or rest = "closed" SWITCHED_LINK_WITHOUT_REST is an ERROR. conductor = "PE" on a pin role = "pe" A PE pin is named by its role. The pole-side conductor value is refused. a protection type on a non-protection function remove the type A load ERROR in 0.6.

A changeover contact (contact_co) needs no rest line. Its throw roles imply it: break is closed at rest and make is open. Its ports must still carry common, break and make, as in 0.5. Only switch and generic functions with a switched link need rest.

items.title: Stored models
items.text: The model SCHEMA_VERSION went from 2 to 7. Rebuild every stored model with fr.build.

items.title: Moving to Fransys
items.text: This page lists every change a script written for version 0.6.1 under the old name must make for Fransys 0.7.0. Each entry gives the old spelling, the new one and one line of why. The old spellings sit in text blocks: they no longer run.

items.title: Import and alias
items.text:
import schematika as sk
from schematika.colours import BU

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.device("Q1", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
model = fr.build(d)

Every sk. call becomes fr. with the same name and arguments. The distribution and the import name are both fransys now, so no schematika module remains.

items.title: The pin line
items.text:
schematika @ git+<the old repository>@v0.6.1#subdirectory=packages/schematika

fransys @ git+https://github.com/OleJBondahl/fransys@v0.7.0#subdirectory=packages/fransys

Pin the exact tag, as before. The repository is the public one, and the subdirectory is the fransys package.

items.title: The parts module command
items.text:
old new python -m schematika parts-module python -m fransys parts-module

The arguments are the same. Regenerate the parts module with the new command, then rebuild. The generated file records the library's digest, which the rename does not change.

items.title: The intermediates folder
items.text:
old new .schematika/ .fransys/

Per-page SVGs and other intermediates go to .fransys/. Replace the .schematika/ line in your .gitignore with this one.

.fransys/

Stored baselines verify unchanged: the rename moves no listing text.

items.title: The system overview
items.text:
overview.html is one file that fr.write(result, out_dir) puts beside the PDFs. It needs no network and no server: open it in a browser. This page says how to read it.

The page starts at the system: each cabinet unit is a box, each cable a line. Double-click a unit, or select it and press Enter, to open it; the crumbs above the drawing and "Up one level" go back. A unit opens as its function groups, as all devices with strips drawn through, as lanes when it has them, or as plain boxes: pick one under "View". A stub opens its far side in place.

  • Colour by a unit, a function group, an item kind or a location. The legend counts the boxes of the level shown; click a class to hide it, and a chip above the drawing brings it back.
  • Find an item by designation in the search box; Enter opens its level and selects it.
  • Parts on the left lists every item as a tree; the boxes hide an item and what it holds.
  • Select a box or line to dim the rest and list its facts and the signals through it on the right. An item drawn on a PDF page lists its pages, each a link to that page. Keep the HTML and the PDFs together in the folder write made.
  • Theme is light, dark or your system's. The address holds the whole view, so Back, Forward and a copied link return to it.

With no document in the build there is no PDF, so the page has no links. The page holds no internal id, so a rename that changes no printed text changes no byte of it.

items.title: Parts
items.text: A part library is a Python data package: TOML files describing parts, and no code. Fransys never reads a spreadsheet or a manufacturer's own format directly; every part your design uses comes from an installed library written against the part-file contract. This page covers starting a design from a library, the typed parts module, class codes, linting and load failures. The contract itself is the "Part file contract" page of the site, at the version you installed. Read it before you write a library.

items.title: Starting a design
items.text:
fr.design takes the import names of one or more installed part-data packages and returns a design d with every part, function and port of those libraries loaded. A device names its part by manufacturer part number (MPN), as a string. This is the data-driven path: the part list can come from a table or a file.

# easy: start a design
import fransys as fr

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.device("H1", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
d.device("H2", "DEMO-LAMP-24")

A part is either a typed object from the generated parts module or an MPN string. That is one argument of d.device, not two spellings of one task. Use the typed object when you write the part by hand and want completion and checking, and the string when the MPN comes from data. Two parts with one MPN from two makers have no spelling in this release.

items.title: The typed parts module
items.text:
The generator writes one Python module for a library: a class per part, with its functions and pins as typed attributes. Your editor then completes H1.lamp[1] and flags a pin the part does not have. Regenerate the module whenever the library changes. Run this from a shell:

python -m fransys parts-module demo_parts demo_typed.py

fr.parts_module("demo_parts") returns the same module as text, when a script writes the file itself.

The part library generates this module and ships it, and the projects that use the library import it rather than generate their own. A pin whose marking is not a Python name gets an attribute by the one name rule (authoring.md): the pin 1/L1 is k.main.P_1_L1 and 24V1 is psu.P_24V1, each checked by ty. The pin is also k.main["1/L1"]. Pass interface= a tuple of the part's function names and a misspelt name is a ty error.

The part argument of d.device is a string or a generated class. A string is checked when you build. Two part names that map to one attribute fail generation, and so do two pins of one function.

A function stands in a d.series when its line side is known: a coil's A1 and a contact's odd pin give it, else state side.

A pin that sources a wiring row, such as a drive's U, V and W outputs, states it with source_row = "AC_L1" (any WiringRow name). A d.series wire from that pin then takes the row's colour without wire=.

The module records the library's digest. fr.design(P, ...) compares that digest with the library it loads and raises an error naming the command above when the module is stale. A whitespace edit in a part file is not stale; any changed fact is. The efficient level of the task builds the same model with the typed module and a loop:

# efficient: start a design
import subprocess
import sys

import fransys as fr

subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, "-m", "fransys", "parts-module", "demo_parts", "demo_typed.py"], check=True
)
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
import demo_typed as P

d = fr.design(P)
for tag in ("H1", "H2"):
    d.device(tag, P.DEMO_LAMP_24)

items.title: Class codes
items.text:
A part's class_code seeds its printed designation (-Q1, -Q2). Recommended codes, IEC 81346-2:2019:

Object Code Contactor, main switch, switch-disconnector Q Fuse, MCB (protection) F Relay, PLC coupler and modules, network switch K Overload relay, sensor, current transformer B Signal lamp, meter, display P Terminal, terminal strip X Plug, socket, board header (connector) J Power supply, transformer T Motor, solenoid actuator M Suppressor diode, resistor R Board (PCB), rack U Cable, harness W Heater E Push button, selector, emergency stop S

items.title: Loading a library without a design
items.text:
fr.parts takes the same import names and returns a single Draft holding every part, function, port and facet record, each carrying the file and line it came from. Use it to lint a library or build without a design:

import fransys as fr

parts = fr.parts("demo_parts")

Loading several libraries together, as in fr.design("a", "b") or fr.parts("a", "b"), merges them into one library.

items.title: Linting a library
items.text:
fr.lint(*libraries) checks one or more libraries against the part-file contract without building a model: every part file's fields, enum values, port and link shapes, and the cross-file rules (duplicate parts, duplicate connector labels, and so on), collected as Findings.

findings = fr.lint("demo_parts")
assert not [f for f in findings if f.severity is fr.Severity.ERROR]

The argument is the library's import name, resolved exactly as fr.parts resolves it: an installed package's own root, the directory that directly holds library.toml. For the demo library that is demo_parts, the inner package, never examples/demo-parts, the outer project folder that merely contains it (and holds the package's own pyproject.toml, not a part file). Passing the project folder's name is the mistake to watch for. fr.lint and fr.parts both want the package's own name, the same one you would give uv add or an import statement.

items.title: When a library fails to load
items.text:
fr.parts runs the same checks fr.lint does before it builds anything, and refuses to load a library that fails them: it raises fr.PartLibraryError, whose findings attribute holds every finding lint collected, warnings included, not only the errors that caused the raise. So does fr.design. A library with a genuine problem (a part file missing its required [part] table, in this made-up example) never reaches your model:

import sys
from pathlib import Path

Path("bad_parts/parts").mkdir(parents=True)
Path("bad_parts/__init__.py").write_text('"""A broken library, for this example only."""\n')
Path("bad_parts/library.toml").write_text(
    'schema = 1\nname = "bad-parts"\nversion = "0.0.1"\ndescription = "missing its [part] table"\n'
)
Path("bad_parts/parts/broken.toml").write_text("schema = 1\n")
sys.path.insert(0, ".")

try:
    fr.parts("bad_parts")
except fr.PartLibraryError as e:
    assert e.findings[0].code == "FIELD_MISSING"
else:
    raise AssertionError("expected PartLibraryError")

Catch fr.PartLibraryError around a load whose library you do not control yourself: one built by a separate team or vendor. An uncaught PartLibraryError already stops your script right there, with Python's own one-line traceback. Catching it instead gets you e.findings: every finding the failed load collected, not only the one that raised, so you can report the library's whole set of problems at once instead of fixing them one exception at a time.

items.title: A contact a person or a machine operates
items.text:
A push button, an emergency stop, a selector or a limit switch states what operates its contacts in [part]: operated_by = "push", "mushroom", "turn" or "position". Its contacts are switch functions, and the drawing picks the symbol from the operator and the rest state: a push button closed at rest draws push-button-break. A part that wants one actuator over several contacts states one switch function per contact.

A complete device, such as a limit switch, states it on itself. A head sold apart from its contact blocks states it and has no function. Each block holds one switch and joins the head with parent=:

s1 = d.device("S1", "DEMO-HEAD-ESTOP")
first = d.device(None, "DEMO-BLOCK-1NC", name="nc-1", parent=s1)
second = d.device(None, "DEMO-BLOCK-1NC-21", name="nc-2", parent=s1)

Both blocks print -S1, and each draws the emergency-stop symbol. d.layout.profile(actuator_each_contact=False) draws one actuator per device: the first block, 11-12, draws the symbol and the list of both contacts; the second draws its break contact with a reference to the first.

items.title: Ratings from a datasheet
items.text:
A part's rating fields are read straight off its datasheet, but a battery or cell datasheet often states its rating as a C-rate against the part's capacity rather than as a current: 1C on 310 Ah is 310 A. Do that multiplication yourself before writing the part file. A [function.operating] table's max_current_dc_a is a current, in amps, never a C-rate. Fransys stores whatever number you give it and does not compute this conversion.

A protective device's datasheet gives its breaking capacity as points: the voltage, the current it breaks there and, for DC, the circuit's time constant. A part states them in [rating] or [function.rating] as breaking_ac and breaking_dc. A source's datasheet gives its fault current and time constant in [function.operating].

# a DC fuse function
[function.rating]
voltage_dc_v = "1000"
current_dc_a = "125"
breaking_dc = [{ voltage_v = "1000", current_a = "15000", time_constant_ms = "15" }]

# a battery function
[function.operating]
nominal_voltage_v = "51.2"
fault_current_dc_a = "6000"
fault_time_constant_ms = "2"

A replaceable part, such as a fuse link in its holder, is its own part file. It states a top-level [rating] and has no [[function]]. The holder keeps the pads and the footprint.

[part]
mpn = "DEMO-FUSE-LINK-4A-T"
manufacturer = "Demo"
description = "Replaceable fuse link for a PCB holder, 4 A time-lag, 1000 V DC"
category = "protection"
class_code = "F"

[rating]
voltage_dc_v = "1000"
current_dc_a = "4"

d.rating("DEMO-FUSE-LINK-4A-T") reads that rating. Put the link in its holder with parent=, as authoring.md shows. A link with min_breaking_current_a is partial-range and bounds no current.

import fransys as fr

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
rating = d.rating("DEMO-FUSE-LINK-4A-T")
assert rating is not None and rating.current_dc_a == 4

items.title: Reading a part's rating while authoring
items.text:
d.rating(part, function) and d.operating(part, function) read a rating or operating envelope from the catalogue. It is a lookup, not a build step. Either gives None where the part states nothing.

import fransys as fr

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
part_rating = d.rating("DEMO-TBLK-2P-DUAL")
terminal_rating = d.rating("DEMO-TBLK-2P-DUAL", "terminal")
lamp_operating = d.operating("DEMO-LAMP-24", "lamp")

items.title: An accessory in its holder
items.text:
A part with no function, put in another device with parent=, is an accessory. A fuse link in its PCB holder is one: the link prints F1 and has no number or row. An authored tag makes it an ordinary item. parent= also takes a terminal strip, for a jumper bar on a bridged run.

import fransys as fr

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
f1 = d.device("F1", "DEMO-FUSE-HOLDER-PCB")
link = d.device(None, "DEMO-FUSE-LINK-4A-T", name="link", parent=f1)
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
x1.run("L", 3, bridged=True)
bar = d.device(None, "DEMO-JUMPER-BAR-3P", name="bar", parent=x1)
model = fr.build(d).model
assert fr.derive.item_designation(model, link.id) == "F1"
assert fr.derive.item_designation(model, bar.id) == "X1"

items.title: Reading the pages as numbers
items.text:
fr.readability(result) returns a ReadabilityReport with the numbers behind the findings: one ReadabilityPage row for each schematic page in .pages and one ReadabilityUnit row for each unit in .units. The three types are also in fr.derive. The same model gives equal rows, so compare a unit between revisions by its rows. It writes no file and fr.write does not emit it. It lays the schematic out again. Only a drawing set that some document prints gets rows. The look findings (PAGE_UNDERFILLED, WIRE_OVER_LABEL, TEXT_OVERLAP, LONE_CELL) skip the other sets too.

The findings these numbers back are in drawing.md.

  • drawing_set, number and unit. The page as printed in the corner, and the unit it belongs to (None for the design's own pages).
  • text_height_mm and min_text_height_mm. The smallest printed capital height in mm and its floor. Change nothing when text_height_mm is at or over the floor. When under, raise text_height_mm on the profile.
  • fill_percent. The share of the page's content box the drawing covers, in whole percent. A low number is a mostly empty page with small text. Merge its group into the page before it, or drop a break_before.
  • wire_crossings. How often a wire or a fan-out leg runs across a wire of another net or another cable's core line or leg. A cable's own legs and line meet by design. A high number means a tangled page. Order the groups with order, or put the crossing nets on separate pages.
  • wire_bends, wire_length_mm. The direction changes and the total length in mm of every conductor line drawn on the page: routed wires, straight power leads and fan-out legs. A harness or cable line is not counted. Many bends or a long total mean a winding page: a shorter run or a nearer neighbour reads better. They are numbers to compare between revisions, not a target the layout optimises.
  • struck_labels. Texts a wire runs through (WIRE_OVER_LABEL). It is INFO: report it with the smallest model.
  • text_overlaps. Texts that overlap each other or a symbol they do not belong to (TEXT_OVERLAP).
  • lone_cells. Symbols standing alone on a page (LONE_CELL). Keep the circuit in one block, or wire the symbol.
  • contact_images, contact_image_targets and single_contact_images. The coil images on the page, the contacts they list and the images that list one. Many single images mean a relay used for one contact: a plain wire may read better.
  • single_contact_images_other_page. The single images whose one contact is on another page, a part of single_contact_images. Such an image points off the page, so it reads less well than one beside its contact.
  • stars, star_branches and single_branch_stars. The net references on the page, the branches they name on other pages and the references that name one. Many on several pages mean the net is cut across pages. Declare the supply so it is drawn once, or keep the net's ends together. A star can also stand on one page, and then it is no cut. A pin with two or more wires takes a reference for each end. One breaker pin feeding two coils gives each of the three ports a marker naming the other two. A wire that would turn back round its own device is a marker pair too. A contact above a box, with both pins wired to the box's top pins, is one. For the first, distribute through a terminal strip with a named, bridged run (checklist item 4). A bridged three-terminal run took one page from 2 stars to 1.
  • contacts_not_drawn. The contact-image entries that print N/A: a contact no conductor reaches. Information only, with no finding, since N/A is how a contact with nothing drawn prints. Many on one coil mean a relay bought for contacts the circuit does not use.
  • references_off_document. References on the page to a page of another document that print no location. A reader cannot tell which document to open. REFERENCE_OFF_DOCUMENT is a warning that names the reference and its page. The bar is 0. Print both drawing sets in one document. Or give the target's drawing set a location, so the reference names it. A reference that prints its location, such as +FLDp1:2A, is correct.
  • page_cuts. The wires of two ports cut at a page break, each naming one other page. Keep the two ends in one block, or add a terminal where the circuit changes page.

A reference text reads p<n>:<cell> for sheet n of the reference's own drawing set. It reads p<set>.<page>:<cell> for a sheet of another set. A net reference adds the net's number, #<n>, then its first target. That target is a terminal of the net when it has one, else the first other end in reading order. A marker with more than two other ends prints that target and +k for the k others. A contact no conductor reaches prints N/A in place of a position. Pole-linked contacts of one item in one row print one back reference to the coil. The coil's table lists every contact.

report.loose_symbols counts the symbols of the whole build that no page draws, those with nothing connected. No page row carries it. A unit row counts its own loose symbols, adds up the counts of its pages and their wire length, and takes the smallest text_height_mm and fill_percent and the highest min_text_height_mm. Its pages is the page count.

from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU


class Cabinet(NamedTuple):
    pass


Path("cover.md").write_text("# Cabinet\n", encoding="utf-8")


@fr.unit(
    "cab", revision=1, interface_version=1, date="2026-01-01", text="First", by="XX",
    title="Cabinet", number="C-1",
)
def measured(c):
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    for i in range(1, 6):
        k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
        h = c.device(f"H{i}", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
        c.series(dc.plus, k.co_1.no, h.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    return Cabinet()


d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.add(measured, "U1")
doc = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "cab", cover=Path("cover.md"))
report = fr.readability(fr.build(d, doc))
assert report.pages
assert all(page.text_height_mm >= page.min_text_height_mm for page in report.pages)
assert sum(unit.pages for unit in report.units) == len(report.pages)

items.title: Reading: records, lookups and ratings
items.text: This page covers the records that describe a model's structure, the lookups that find them, and the ratings and currents that say what a circuit may carry. Each record type has a table function that returns every record of that type, keyed by id. Every name here is reached as fr.derive.NAME.

items.title: Records
items.text:
• Aspect is one of the three IEC 81346 views of the same objects: FUNCTION, PRODUCT and LOCATION.
  • AspectNode is a node in one aspect tree. Its fields are id, key, aspect, parent (an AspectNode id, or None at the root), label, description and ext. A LOCATION node with label C1 is the place +C1. The table is aspect_nodes.
  • Placement puts one item at one aspect node. Its fields are id, key, item, node and ext. An item has at most one placement per aspect, so one item can have a product placement and a location placement. The table is placements.
  • Boundary marks a function as part of a unit's interface. Its fields are id, key, unit, function, name and ext. name is the field name the unit gave the function, or None. One function can be the boundary of several units. The table is boundaries.
  • Port is a connection point on a function. Its fields are id, key, function, template, name, role, marking and ext. template is None for a port without a part template. The marking field is the pin text printed on the drawing: None prints the port's name, an empty string prints nothing, and any other string prints as given.
  • PortRole says what a port is for. Its members are GENERIC, INTERNAL, EXTERNAL, PE, COMMON, BREAK and MAKE. A terminal's two ports are INTERNAL (panel side) and EXTERNAL (field cable side). A contact's ports are COMMON, BREAK (closed at rest) or MAKE (closed when operated).
  • Conductor is a physical connection with exactly two ends. Its fields are id, key, a, b, kind, carrier (the item that carries it, or None) and ext. a and b are stored in id order, so they do not say a direction. The table is conductors.
  • ConductorKind says what realises a conductor. Its members are WIRE, CORE, JUMPER, BUSBAR, MOUNT, RAIL and LEAD. MOUNT, BUSBAR, RAIL and LEAD are links: they close a net and are never wires.
  • PhysicalNet is one net found from real connectivity: a maximal set of ports joined by conductors. Its only field is ports, sorted by id. It differs from a declared net, which is the intent the author wrote. Two closures over the same wiring compare equal.
  • NetClass says what kind of potential or signal a Net carries. Its members are POWER, CONTROL, SIGNAL, PE and GENERIC. A 24 V supply rail is POWER; a 4-20 mA transmitter loop is SIGNAL. Read it as net.net_class on a row of fr.derive.nets.

items.title: Lookups
items.text:
• aspect_nodes(model) returns every AspectNode, keyed by id. It is the model's own table, not a copy, and it is empty when the model has none.
  • placements(model) returns every Placement, keyed by id, in the same way.
  • boundaries(model) returns every Boundary, keyed by id, in the same way.
  • conductors(model) returns every Conductor, keyed by id, in the same way.
  • item_location(model, item) returns the id of the LOCATION node the item is placed at. It uses the item's own placement, or the nearest placed ancestor's. It returns None when there is none. It raises SchemaError when item is not an item of the model.
  • items_at(model, node) returns the ids of every item at node or at any node below it, once each and sorted by id. An item counts by its own placement, or by its nearest placed ancestor's. It raises SchemaError when node is not an aspect node of the model.
  • effective_placement(model, item, aspect) returns the id of the AspectNode where item sits in aspect: its own placement, else its nearest placed ancestor's, else None. It walks Item.parent and stops on a cycle. A tie in one aspect resolves to the smallest placement id. It raises SchemaError when item is not an item of the model. Use it when you need one aspect's node; item_location is its LOCATION case.
  • subtree takes a model and a node. It returns the ids of every descendant of node, following parent, with node itself left out. The result is sorted by id. It follows parent in any aspect and stops on a cycle. It raises SchemaError when node is not an aspect node.
  • net_of takes a model and a port. It returns the PhysicalNet that contains the port. It returns None when the port is not a port of the model.
  • revision_history takes a model and an optional release. It returns the Revision records of a release, in date order, then by version and revision as numbers, so revision 2 comes before revision 10. With release=None it returns the project's own history. It raises SchemaError when release is not None and is not a release of the model.

Use item_location when a list needs an item's place and the place may be inherited. Use items_at when you need everything in a cabinet or on a board, including the items under it.

items.title: Id aliases
items.text: fransys_model.derive exports UnitId, ItemId, FunctionId, PortId, DocumentId, NetId, ConductorId, AspectNodeId and UnitReleaseId. Each is Id[...] of its record class. Annotate a value with the alias, so a module that only reads ids imports no record class. An output package reads sheets, documents and connector items through DocumentRow, SheetRow, document_row, document_sheet, kind_sheet, schematic_page_ids and connector_item of the same module, never through a record. fr.derive does not re-export them.

items.title: Ratings and currents
items.text:
• Rating says what a function or a part is rated for. Its fields are voltage_ac_v, voltage_dc_v, current_ac_a, current_dc_a, min_breaking_current_a, power_loss_w, breaking_ac and breaking_dc. A field is None when the datasheet gives no value. AC voltages are RMS, and DC voltages are the highest permissible potential. Currents are continuous ratings, except min_breaking_current_a, which is the lowest current a partial-range fuse breaks. The model checks the types only; comparing a rating with the plant is a check's job.
  • CurrentPosition is one rated current path. Its fields are functions (sorted), bounds and ports. bounds holds at most one CurrentBound per current kind, AC before DC. ports are the two end ports of the path, and they tell apart paths that pass through the same functions, one per pole.
  • CurrentChain is a block of the current graph. Its only field is positions, in the order that the chain lists them. The graph treats every switched link as closed. A position that exists only in some switch state is a chain on its own.
  • LimitRole says what set a bound. Its members are SOURCE, a source's continuous limit, and PROTECTION, a full-range protective device.
  • port_potential_current takes a model and a port. It returns the current kind, AC or DC, of the supply behind the port's potential. It returns None when the port has no potential rank, and it always returns None for protective earth, which belongs to no supply.

items.title: Reading: rows, columns and printed texts
items.text: This page covers fr.derive, the facade's read-only layer. It holds the column orders and labels of the list outputs and the row types they are built from. It also holds the row functions, and the texts and order keys every list shares. Use these to read a model yourself and get the same numbers, text and order the outputs print.
path: Reading: rows, columns and printed texts

items.title: Column and label constants
items.text:
Each constant is a tuple or a dict of field names. The list outputs read them in order, so a column appears where its name appears here.

  • BOM_COLUMNS is ('mpn', 'revision', 'manufacturer', 'description', 'count', 'designations'). It orders the columns of the bill of materials list.
  • CABLE_LIST_COLUMNS is ('designation', 'mpn', 'description', 'core_count', 'gauge_mm2', 'length_mm', 'from_label', 'to_label', 'pairs'). It orders the columns of the cable list. The two *_label columns are the far-end texts of the cable.
  • CORE_LIST_COLUMNS is ('cable', 'core', 'colour', 'pair', 'end_a', 'end_b', 'note'). It orders the columns of the core list. pair is the core's pair word, note is spare for a spare core.
  • DESIGNATION_COLUMNS is ('designation', 'reference', 'description'). It orders the columns of the designation list: the printed designation, the full reference and the description.
  • CONNECTOR_COLUMNS is ('designation', 'style', 'pincount', 'gender', 'mate_designation'). It orders the connector part of the connector list. Each pin line repeats these fields.
  • PIN_COLUMNS is ('marking', 'net', 'mate_port_designation', 'ends'). It orders the pin part of the connector list, after CONNECTOR_COLUMNS. One line per pin.
  • CONNECTOR_LABELS is {'marking': 'Pin', 'mate_port_designation': 'Mate'}. It gives the headings of those two columns in the connector table of a PDF.
  • PLC_COLUMNS is ('pin', 'channel_name', 'signal', 'signal_name', 'wired_to'). It orders the PLC list, which has one row per pin. The field device is not printed in this list, although the row carries it.
  • TERMINAL_COLUMNS is ('designation', 'group', 'index', 'internal_ends', 'external_ends', 'jumper_group'). It orders the terminal list of a strip.
  • TERMINAL_LABELS is {'internal_ends': 'Side A', 'external_ends': 'Side B'}. It gives the headings of the two far-end columns of a terminal list. The CSV file writes them in snake case, as side_a and side_b.
  • WIRE_COLUMNS is ('from_', 'to', 'colour', 'cross_section_mm2', 'label'). It orders the wire list.
  • WIRE_LABELS is {'from_': 'from'}. It changes only the heading of the from_ column, which the field name cannot hold, so the wire list prints from.
  • CELL_SEPARATOR is '; '. It joins the parts of one list cell that holds more than one value, such as several far ends of a terminal. Empty parts are left out.
path: Reading: rows, columns and printed texts

items.title: Row types
items.text:
Every row is a frozen record. A row is the one shape an output reads, so the layout and the renderers never look up the model for these facts.

  • CableRow is one core of one cable, both ends. Fields: cable, cable_designation, index, colour, conductor, end_a, end_a_designation, end_b, end_b_designation. The ends are ports; the designations are their printed text.
  • ChannelScaling is the scaling of a field device, projected so a formatter never looks it up. Fields: unit, raw_min, raw_max (integers), and eng_min, eng_max (decimals).
  • ConnectorPin is one pin of a board connector. Fields: port, marking, net, mate_port, mate_port_designation, ends. The marking is the port's name. The net is the declared net that lists the port, or None when none does. The mate's pin is the port of the same name on the mated function. The ends are the far ends of every conductor on the pin or on its mate, as a terminal row prints them; empty when there is none.
  • ConnectorRow is one connector of a board, as connector_rows lists it. Fields: connector, designation, style, pincount, gender, mate, mate_designation, pins. The gender is None when the part file states none. The mate is None when the connector is unmated. The pins is a tuple of ConnectorPin.
  • DesignationRow is one line of the designation list. Fields: item, designation, reference, description. The designation is the printed designation, and reference is the reference designation.
  • HarnessCore is one core of a harness cable, with the label its wire carries. Fields: conductor, index, colour, label, end_a, end_a_designation, end_b, end_b_designation. The label is None when the wire has none. Every core of one cable runs from the same physical end to the same other end.
  • HarnessEnd is one item that a core lands on: a connector housing, a plain device, or a strip of terminals. Fields: item, designation, connector, style, pincount, gender, mpn, pins. The designation is the item's product designation for every end. The connector fields are None for a plain device or a strip. When a core lands on a terminal with a parent, item is the strip, and pins holds one HarnessPin per landed terminal.
  • HarnessPin is one port of a harness end that a core lands on. Fields: port, marking. The marking is the port's own name. For a terminal in a strip it is the bare group:index text, such as L1:1, without the strip's designation, because the end already prints the strip.
  • PlcChannelRow is one pin of a PLC channel. Fields: channel, port, pin, channel_name, signal, wired_to, field_device, field_device_designation, signal_name. The pin is the pin's printed designation (-A2:5) and channel_name the channel's own number. The wired_to joins the far ends of that pin's conductors with CELL_SEPARATOR, or is None when nothing is printed. The three field fields are None for a channel with no bound device.
  • PlcRackChannel is one channel of a rack module, bound or spare. Fields: channel, number, signal, field_device, field_device_designation, signal_name, scaling, name_stem. The field fields are None for a spare channel. The scaling is None when the bound device has no scaling facet. The name_stem is the text an output names the channel after: the field device and its signal name, else the module's designation and the channel's index in the module.
  • PlcRackModule is one PLC module of a rack, with its channels in order. Modules go by position, else by their own tag. Channels with one number go by the function names in the part file, in natural order. A block tag never changes the order of racks, modules or channels (model-0259). Fields: module, designation, mpn, description, position, channels. The mpn and description come from the part. The position is None when the author never gave one.
  • PlcTable is one table of the PLC list: the channels of one controller or module. Fields: item, designation and rows. item carries the channels, designation is its printed designation and the table's heading, and rows are its PlcChannelRows in list order, never empty.
  • BoardNetlist is a board's parts, footprints and nets. Fields: board, board_designation, parts, nets and without_footprint. without_footprint lists the board's parts whose part carries no footprint; a netlist cannot place them, so parts omits them. An accessory prints its holder's designation, so it is never listed.
  • NetlistPart is one placed part of a BoardNetlist. Fields: item, designation (relative to the board), mpn, footprint_library, footprint_name and installed. installed is the item's own flag: a part not installed stays listed, and the output decides what to do with it.
  • NetlistNet is one net of a BoardNetlist. Fields: name and pins, the ports it joins.
  • TerminalRow is one terminal of a strip's connection list. Fields: terminal, designation, group, index, internal, external, internal_ends, external_ends, jumper_group. An unused terminal has empty internal and external tuples. Bridged terminals share one jumper_group number. The internal_ends[i] is the far end of internal[i], and the same for external.

items.title: Row functions
items.text:
Each function takes a frozen model and returns rows. None of them writes a file or reads a clock. Most raise a schema error when a named item, function or unit is not in the model, or when an item has no designation. boards takes no such check.

  • boards returns the ids of every item whose part carries a board facet. It sorts them by natural designation, then by id. The export enumeration and the PDF document contents use this same function, so they agree on what a board is.
  • cable_rows returns one CableRow per core of a cable. Cores sort by their index, then by conductor id. Its unit keyword keeps the cores drawn by one unit's document.
  • designation_list returns one DesignationRow per item, terminals included, sorted by designation, then id. An accessory that takes its parent's designation has no row. Its unit keyword keeps the rows of one unit only; the unit's sole root has no row.
  • board_netlist takes a model and a board item. It returns the BoardNetlist of that board. Its parts are the footprinted descendants of the board. Its nets join the board's internal conductors and its declared nets, never Mates. It raises a schema error when the board is not an item of the model, or when it or a listed item has no designation. Use it to check a board's connectivity yourself; the KiCad export builds the same netlist.
  • plc_channel_rows returns one PlcChannelRow per pin of each PLC channel function, in list order: channels as the PLC list orders them, the pins of a channel by name. Its unit keyword keeps one unit's channels. Its context keyword sets the location the list prints for, and it has no effect once unit is given.
  • plc_tables returns the rows of plc_channel_rows, grouped into one PlcTable per carrying item, in the same order. A controller's own channels form its table, the modules' tables follow in rack order, and items in no rack come last, one table each. An item with no channel has no table. Its unit and context keywords are those of plc_channel_rows. Use it when you print one table per controller or module, as the PLC list does.
  • signal_word returns the word a printed list uses for a SignalType: DI, DO, AI (V), AI (mA), AO (V), AO (mA), RTD or DO (relay). The CSV keeps the enum value.
  • plc_list_rows takes PlcChannelRows and returns one PLC_COLUMNS tuple per row for a printed list. The signal is its signal_word. A channel with no device and no wire prints spare as its signal name.

  • terminal_rows returns one TerminalRow per terminal of a strip. Terminals sort by the natural key of their group, then by index, then by id. A far end outside the given context prints with its location path in front, such as +EXT-M1:U1. A far end inside it prints short, such as -B12:2/T1.

  • open_core_rows(model, cable, *, unit=None) returns one OpenCoreRow per open core of cable, by core number. An open core is a spare or a screen earthed at one end. A row holds the core's index, colour, the port it lands on (at, at_designation; None and "" for none) and spare, false for an SH screen. HarnessCable.open_cores holds the same rows.

  • core_list_rows(model, *, unit=None) returns one CoreListRow per core of every cable cable_list_rows lists. The order is the cable list's, then core number. The wired cores and the open ones are in it, and the ends print as the cable drawing prints them. A spare parked on a pin has it as end_a. pair is P1 or screen P1, "" outside a pair, and note is spare for a spare core. CORE_LIST_COLUMNS names the fields, in print order. cores.csv is this list.
  • contents_rows(cables) reshapes a tuple of HarnessCables into one ContentsRow per cable. The tuple comes from harness_cables, top_level_cables or unit_cables. The row keeps the cable's product facts and adds ends. That is every end's designation, in the cable's own order, joined by an en dash, and a blank end drops its dash. CONTENTS_COLUMNS names its columns, in print order.

items.title: Printed texts and order keys
items.text:
These functions give the one text and the one order that each list uses. A list that prints a label or sorts a column calls them rather than building its own.

  • cable_title returns the cable's printed title. It is its designation, then a space and its MPN when the cable has one. Without an MPN it is the designation alone.
  • function_designation renders a function as its item's designation, a colon and the function's name, such as JB1:J1. Its unit keyword sets whether the text is written for one unit's document or for the whole model.
  • item_description returns the text a list shows for an item. It is the item's own description, else its part's description, else an empty string. The part's text is never copied onto the item.
  • release_order returns the order key of a unit release or a history entry, from a version and a revision as two integers. The key is a pair of integers, so revision 10 sorts after revision 9. Compare releases with this key, never with printed text, because the text "1.10" sorts before "1.9".
  • sideless_pins gives the pins of two series ends that have no line side, each in pin order, as SidelessPins(first, second, problem). It takes a label and a tuple of port templates for each end. The order is the marking by value, and the pin's name when it prints none. problem is the message that says why the ends cannot pair, or None. They cannot pair with a different number of pins, or the same names in another order. A series between two connectors pairs their pins with it.
